features.title: Step 4 — Actual vs Predicted as every candidate's base chart, with its own diagnostic beside it
features.description: Give every candidate in Model Selection the same base chart — actual against predicted over the test split — so candidates are compared on the one view every algorithm can produce. The per-algorithm diagnostic (a loss curve where the estimator iterates, paired train-vs-test marks where it does not) becomes a SECOND chart beside it rather than the only one, so a closed-form algorithm is no longer represented by a chart shape that exists to say it has nothing to show.
userDecisions: ACTUAL VS PREDICTED IS THE BASE, NOT THE ALTERNATIVE (resolved). MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 built loss visualisation as the primary per-candidate view, with mode B (paired marks) as the honest fallback for the seven algorithms that cannot produce a curve. That was correct for what it set out to do and leaves ols/ridge/pls/grp/svm/random_forest — the majority of the catalogue — represented by two dots. Actual-vs-predicted is producible by every algorithm from the artifact each run already writes, so it becomes the common ground and the diagnostic becomes supplementary.

TWO CHARTS PER CANDIDATE, NOT ONE MERGED (resolved). The base answers 'does this model track reality'; the diagnostic answers 'did it converge, and how'. Overlaying a loss trajectory on a value series would put two incompatible y-axes in one frame and imply a relationship between them that does not exist.
findings: STEP 4's CHARTS TODAY ARE MOSTLY A STATEMENT THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO PLOT. MODEL-FLOW-013-T05's own live verification, run against the pinned library versions rather than fakes, established which algorithms actually yield a loss history: ols/ridge/pls/grp/svm/random_forest return None; mlp returns train-only; lightgbm/xgboost return train+validation; and hist_gradient_boosting returns EMPTY ARRAYS for any dataset at or under 10,000 rows — the common case in this trainer's domain — so it too falls to mode B. That is seven of ten algorithms whose entire visual representation in the comparison step is two paired marks. The marks are honest and were the right call; they are not a basis for comparing models.

EVERY CANDIDATE ALREADY HAS THE DATA FOR THE BASE CHART. A SUCCEEDED run writes predictions.parquet under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ with schema timestamp/y_true/y_pred — confirmed against a real file (run 61f9aa28: 1,341 rows, three columns, no nulls). Every algorithm writes it, closed-form included, because it is the output of predict() and not a property of the fitting procedure. MODEL-FLOW-004 already built the read path (run_predictions in Python, getDraftRunPredictionsService in NestJS) and both chart components (ActualVsPredictedChart, ResidualChart). This feature is composition of proven parts — which is why its risk sits in payload volume (T02) and not in its panels.

THE READ ROUTE IS DRAFT-RUN-SCOPED AND ITS REACH OVER A CANDIDATE RUN IS UNVERIFIED. GET .../model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId/predictions resolves keys off the run row, and a candidate run IS a ModelTrainingRun with the same columns — so it most likely already works. But 'most likely' is what MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found wrong five times out of seven, and MODEL-FLOW-013-T09's whole reason for existing was to stop a later feature being built on the assumption of one run per draft. T01 confirms by calling it against a real candidate run, not by reading the resolver.

FIVE CANDIDATES x A FULL TEST SPLIT IS A PAYLOAD PROBLEM MODEL-FLOW-004 DELIBERATELY DID NOT SOLVE. That feature set MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS=20000 and built NO decimation branch, recording in the schema's own comment that a run over the cap is refused by name rather than silently sampled, and that the design for whoever hits the cap first was deferred. It was sized for ONE chart on ONE run: 1,341 points observed against a 20,000 cap is comfortable. Step 4 renders every candidate at once — five runs of that size is 6,705 points fetched over five requests, and a larger dataset multiplies both. This feature is the caller that hits the deferred design.

DS-LAKE ALREADY SOLVED THE SHAPE OF THIS AND ITS ANSWER DOES NOT TRANSFER UNCHANGED. scatter_service decimates by 2D grid binning explicitly NOT via the LTTB path /preview uses, because a scatter's axes are tag values rather than time. An actual-vs-predicted chart IS time-ordered, so LTTB is the right family here — but the series must be decimated as a PAIR (y_true and y_pred at the same kept timestamps) or the two lines would be sampled at different points and the visible gap between them, which is the entire thing a reader looks at, would become an artefact of sampling.

MODE SELECTION MUST STAY A PROPERTY OF THE RUN. MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a established renderModeFor(candidate) as the single branch site, keyed on whether the run has a lossHistory and never on the algorithm name, precisely so the client holds no membership list to drift when lstm/gru unblock or the catalogue grows. Adding a second chart must not reintroduce a name-keyed branch anywhere — the base chart is unconditional, and only the diagnostic consults that one existing predicate.

T01 AUDIT, 2026-09-04 — READ FROM SOURCE AND LIVE DB/MINIO, NOT FROM THIS ENTRY'S OWN FINDINGS ABOVE. Five of the eight findings above turned out wrong or stale on inspection: (1) the predictions route ALREADY serves a candidate run with no code change — getDraftRunPredictionsService (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:695) filters `where: { id: runId, modelDraftId: draftId }` only; candidateJobId is never selected or tested, and launchDraftRun (:474-484) sets BOTH modelDraftId and candidateJobId on a candidate run — so finding 3's 'unverified reach' is resolved, not merely likely. (2) The measured ceiling is 4,633 rows, not the 1,341 this entry's own finding 2 and T01(b) both name — 131 predictions.parquet objects enumerated in MinIO, largest is 4,633 rows / 318,244 B as JSON (68.7 B/point); 20 candidates undecimated is 6.07 MB, at 1,000 points/candidate it is 1.31 MB. (3) Step 4 already fetches once per job, not per candidate — useCandidateJob (use-candidate-job.ts:23) is a single GET of the whole job — but CandidateResult (services/model-draft.ts:424-449) carries no predictionsKey, so the client cannot tell which candidates have a series without a further fetch; finding 4's 'five sequential requests' framing was about a fetch pattern that was never built. (4) ActualVsPredictedChart hardcodes height={320} and ResidualChart height={280} (T01(d) confirmed neither renders at small-multiple size unchanged), and worse, EVAL_SYNC_ID='evaluation' (actual-vs-predicted-chart.tsx:17) is a module constant wired into syncId on both — N mounted instances would share one Recharts sync group and crosshair across every card, not just an axis-collision problem. (5) A scored CV run DOES write predictions.parquet — contradicting MODEL-FLOW-016 AC5 read literally: 2 of 4 CV runs in the live DB carry predictionsKey AND holdoutMetrics at the same key path, because images/trainer/app/pipelines/score.py:56-66 writes it in score mode; the same key means two different populations (test-split vs holdout) depending on scoring phase. The discriminator already exists (cvScoringPhaseOf, hooks/use-draft-run-evaluation.ts:58-63, plus Step 5's own 'Holdout residual diagnostics' vs 'Test-split residual diagnostics' vocabulary) and a CV run can never be a candidate today (ModelCandidateJob has no nSplits column, runDtoFor never sets one), so this only bites the standalone Step-4 path, not T02-T06's candidate-set work. New finding not in the original eight: the per-job candidate ceiling is 24, not 20 — CreateCandidateJobSchema caps candidates at 20 (dto/model-candidate-job.authorized.dto.ts:50) but SWEEP_THEN_TUNE appends a phase-2 group to the same array, bounded by TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB=4 (lib/tuning-grid.ts:21). Confirmed correct from the entry above: findings 1 (mostly mode B today) and 6 (renderModeFor stays the single branch site) needed no correction. LTTB-on-y_true (T02's chosen decimation basis) was measured against residual-driven bucketing on the two largest real runs: y_true-driven keeps 99.1% and 98.2% of the full-frame max|residual| — within the tolerance needed for a shared grid across candidates sharing a splitSpec, confirmed identical (7 candidates, job 1088da7e, byte-identical 1,703-row timestamp grid).
openDecisions: SMALL MULTIPLES OR ONE OVERLAID CHART FOR THE BASE VIEW? Per-candidate charts scale to any number and read one at a time; a single chart with actual once and each candidate's prediction as its own series makes divergence directly comparable but becomes unreadable past three or four candidates and needs a colour key that survives a FAILED candidate leaving a gap. MODEL-FLOW-013-T07's existing layout is one row per candidate, so small multiples is the smaller change — recorded rather than assumed, because the overlaid version is the one an engineer comparing two close candidates would actually want. RESOLVED 2026-09-04, USER DECISION: both — one full-width overlaid chart per phase group (Sweep / Tuning <winner>) above the small-multiple grid, since candidates sharing a splitSpec share an identical decimated timestamp grid (T01 finding above), so the overlay costs no extra machinery beyond T02's paired decimation.

tasks.title: Audit: can the predictions route serve a candidate run, and what does the payload actually weigh
tasks.detail:
READ AND CALL, DO NOT INFER — MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code, and -004/-005/-006/-012 each opened with an audit that changed their own scope.

Confirm: (a) GET .../model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId/predictions returns a real series for a run whose candidateJobId is set, called against a real candidate run rather than reasoned about from the resolver (finding 3); (b) the observed point count per candidate on the largest real dataset available, against MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS=20000 — the 1,341 measured on run 61f9aa28 is one run on one dataset and is not the ceiling; (c) whether Step 4's existing fetch is per-candidate or one call, since five sequential requests on step entry is a different problem from one large one; (d) whether ActualVsPredictedChart and ResidualChart can render at small-multiple size without their axis labels and legends colliding — they were built for one full-width chart.

If (a) comes back refusing a candidate run, T03 gains a route change and this stops being composition.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04. All four sub-items read from source and confirmed against live DB/MinIO, in parallel across three focused audits (backend resolver/schema/candidate-job service, client Step 4 UI/chart components, python artifact/object-store/trainer). Findings recorded as a dated append to this entry's own findings list above, per the -018-T01 precedent of not silently correcting a claim already recorded. (a) resolves clean — no route change needed, T03 is pure composition as hoped. (b)/(c)/(d) all needed correction: real ceiling 4,633 rows not 1,341; Step 4 already fetches the job in one call but per-candidate series still need a batch fetch of their own; both existing pipeline charts need optional height/syncId props before they can mount N-up. New finding: a scored CV run's predictionsKey means holdout, not test-split — scoped out of T02-T06 (no CV candidate exists today) but recorded for whoever adds one.

tasks.title: Decimate paired series for comparison, and say when it happened
tasks.detail:
The deferred design MODEL-FLOW-004 recorded, now that this feature is its first caller (finding 4). LTTB over the time axis, not scatter_service's 2D grid binning — that method exists because a scatter's axes are tag values; this series is time-ordered (finding 5).

DECIMATE THE PAIR AT THE SAME TIMESTAMPS. Sampling y_true and y_pred independently would make the visible gap between the lines an artefact of which points each series happened to keep — and that gap is the only thing a reader is looking at. This is the load-bearing constraint of the whole task.

STATE IT WHERE IT HAPPENED, following the precedent DraftScatterResult already sets: it carries both `points` (decimated) and `n` (the true count) plus a `downsampled` flag, and TagScatterChart renders 'N of M shown; fit uses all M'. Do the same rather than showing a quietly thinned series — a chart that hides its own sampling is one a reader cannot calibrate.

RESIDUAL FIGURES ARE NOT RECOMPUTED FROM THE DECIMATED SERIES. run_predictions computes residual_sd and its residual_rmse_check over the FULL frame; those stay full-frame, exactly as scatter's regression coefficients are fit over the full Good-filtered frame while its plotted cloud is decimated.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04. `run_predictions_batch` added to artifact_service.py, decimating with `lttb_indices` keyed on (timestamp, y_true) and slicing y_pred by the SAME index set — measured (not assumed) against the two largest real predictions.parquet objects: y_true-driven bucketing keeps 99.1%/98.2% of the full-frame max|residual| versus a residual-driven basis, the tradeoff recorded in the function's own docstring since it decides whether the client's overlay chart can share one grid across candidates. New schema constants MAX_PREDICTION_BATCH_RUNS=24 (not 20 — see T01 finding on SWEEP_THEN_TUNE's phase-2 append) and MAX_PREDICTION_BATCH_POINTS=2000, enforced by Pydantic on the request, not re-checked in the handler. Soft-fails per run (mirrors the loss-history hydration precedent in reconcileAndShape) rather than 422ing the whole batch. New route POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/predictions/batch, registered and confirmed live. 8 new pytest cases in test_artifact_service_run_predictions_batch.py, including the paired-decimation proof (V02 shape) and the full-frame-scalar proof (V03 shape); all 13 pre-existing run_predictions tests still pass unchanged.

tasks.title: One fetch for a candidate set's series, not one per candidate
tasks.detail:
Step 4 needs every terminal candidate's series at once. Five sequential per-run requests on step entry is five artifact reads for one screen — the same argument MODEL-FLOW-014's userDecisions used to reject two /boxplot calls in favour of one /split-stats.

Resolve every key off the job and run rows, never from the request — the discipline getDraftRunPredictionsService established and mintUploadUrls applies on the write side. A PENDING or QUEUED candidate contributes no series and is not an error.

BOUNDED BY CANDIDATE COUNT TOO, not only by points per candidate: CreateCandidateJobSchema caps a set at 20, so twenty decimated series is the real worst case and the per-candidate budget must be set against that, not against a set of five. Refuse an oversized response by name rather than truncating silently, and record the reasoning in the schema's own comment for whoever raises the cap.

CHECK BEFORE BUILDING whether T01(c) found the existing shape already sufficient — if Step 4 already fetches once, this task is smaller than it reads.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04. New GET /:draftId/runs/predictions/batch on ModelDraftRunAuthorizedController, query-string runIds (comma-separated, matching ListRowsSchema.tags' existing precedent), bounded at MAX_PREDICTION_BATCH_RUN_IDS=24 by RunPredictionsBatchQuerySchema/the global ZodValidationPipe — refused there, not re-checked in the service. Keyed on a run-id SET, not a job id (AC10): a MODEL-FLOW-018 selectedRunId run has candidateJobId=null, so a job-keyed batch would silently drop the standalone selection path's runs. getDraftRunPredictionsBatchService resolves predictionsKey off the run rows (findMany, scoped to modelDraftId), drops any run that is not SUCCEEDED or has no predictionsKey WITHOUT erroring (a stale/foreign run id is silently absent, not 404'd — a batch view of many candidates must not fail the whole screen over one bad id), then makes exactly one runPredictionsBatch python call and maps each result item back to its runId via the resolved key. Verified live: the route registers correctly (POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/predictions/batch confirmed via FastAPI route introspection) and does not collide with the existing GET /:draftId/runs/:runId (Fastify's find-my-way router prioritises the literal three-segment path). 5 new jest cases in model-run-launch.authorized.service.spec.ts (404 on missing draft, modelDraftId scoping, silent-drop of unreadable runs, empty-result short-circuit with no python call, runId back-mapping) — all pass, 22/22 in the suite. check-types and eslint clean on every touched file (pre-existing unrelated errors in other WIP files on this branch confirmed via git stash, not introduced here).

tasks.title: Actual vs Predicted as the unconditional base chart per candidate
tasks.detail:
Every terminal candidate gets one, regardless of algorithm — that is the whole point (finding 1). Reuse ActualVsPredictedChart rather than writing a second implementation of the same view; MODEL-FLOW-004 already carries its ±1 SD band and its own doc comment on what the band means.

NO NAME-KEYED BRANCH ANYWHERE (finding 6). The base chart is unconditional; renderModeFor stays the single branch site and is consulted only by T05's diagonstic. A `switch (algorithm)` added here would be the second source of truth MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a exists to prevent, and it would drift toward showing an empty chart rather than an honest one.

A FAILED candidate keeps its row and its reason and shows no chart — it produced no predictions, and an empty chart frame reads as a model that predicted nothing rather than one that never ran. MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 already established that a failed candidate stays listed rather than disappearing; this extends that rule to the chart area.

HONEST STATES, reusing MODEL-FLOW-004's own vocabulary rather than a second set of words for the same conditions: candidate still running, candidate terminal but its predictions unreadable, and — once MODEL-FLOW-016 lands — a CV candidate that has no predictions.parquef at all by design and points at its scoring phase instead.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04. New CandidateBaseChart component (pipeline/model-selection/candidate-base-chart.tsx) reuses ActualVsPredictedChart unchanged (only two new optional props added to that component: height, syncId, both defaulted so Step 5 renders byte-identically). Rendered above CandidateChart (the existing diagnostic) inside CandidateRow's existing `status === 'SUCCEEDED'` gate — a FAILED candidate's chart-frame suppression required no new code, since that gate already excludes it. Honest states: null runId renders nothing, loading shows a spinner, no predictionsKey/predictions unreadable/soft-failed each get their own one-line message, never a blank frame. No branch on algorithm anywhere — confirmed both by the new candidate() render test (V01) and the new static-source guard (V05, model-selection-contract.test.ts).

tasks.title: The per-algorithm diagnostic moves beside the base, unchanged in substance
tasks.detail:
MODEL-FLOW-013-T07's two modes stay exactly as built and verified — mode A's train series with its second series labelled 'Test split' (never 'Validation'), its Y axis labelled from the run's own metric name via modeAMetricLabel rather than assumed RMSE; mode B's paired marks rendered as plain divs with no Line, no path element and no .recharts-wrapper, so a two-point line cannot be faked into a curve. That component and its tests are not rewritten; only its position and its billing change.

WHAT CHANGES IS ITS STATUS. It was the primary view and is now supplementary, which is what makes mode B acceptable rather than thin: two paired marks beside a real actual-vs-predicted series is a supporting detail; two paired marks alone was a candidate's entire representation.

LABEL WHAT EACH CHART ANSWERS, in the UI and not only here. 'Does it track reality' and 'did it converge' are different questions, and a reader given two charts with no framing will assume the second is a refinement of the first.

EPOCH COUNT AND ITERATION COUNT ARE NOT UNIVERSAL AND MUST NOT BE PRINTED AS IF THEY WERE: mlp reports its own loss_curve_ length, lightgbm/xgboost report n_estimators-many rounds, and the seven mode-B algorithms have no iteration concept at all. Read the length from the run's own artifact; never derive it from a hyperparameter the estimator may have stopped short of.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04. `CandidateChart` (both branches) and `run-selection.ts` were NOT rewritten — verified byte-for-byte except for one added line per branch: a 'Did it converge?' label above mode A's chart and above mode B's paired-mark caption respectively. The base chart's own 'Does it track reality?' label sits above it in CandidateRow. Existing mode A/B tests (recharts-wrapper DOM-count assertions) pass unchanged, confirming the label addition altered no rendering logic. Iteration counts were already sourced from `lossHistory.series` length via `modeARows` (MODEL-FLOW-013-T05), not touched by this task.

tasks.title: Layout that survives twenty candidates and a mixed set
tasks.detail:
Two charts per candidate against a 20-candidate cap is forty charts. Whatever T01(d) found about small-multiple rendering decides whether both charts sit side by side per row, or the diagnostic is revealed per candidate on demand.

A MIXED SET IS THE NORMAL CASE, not an edge one: an algorithm sweep across ols/ridge/lightgbm/mlp/svm yields two mode-A diagnostics and three mode-B in one screen. The layout must not make a mode-B row look broken next to a mode-A row — they are different answers to the same question, not a complete and an incomplete rendering of one.

MODEL-FLOW-013-T11's phase grouping ('Sweep' / 'Tuning <winner>') already exists and renders only once a phase-2 group is present. This layout sits inside those groups and must not flatten them — a tuning phase's candidates all share one algorithm, so their diagnostics are directly comparable in a way the sweep phase's are not, which is worth preserving visually.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04, per user decision (2026-09-04): stacked, not side-by-side — base chart above the diagnostic in each card (T01(d) confirmed neither existing chart renders legibly at half-width), user chose 'below base, always visible' over a reveal-on-demand toggle. CandidateGroups' phase1/phase2 grouping is UNCHANGED in structure — only its inner `grid()` helper (renamed `section()`) gained a `CandidateOverlayChart` above the existing candidate grid; `CandidateGroups`' own phase-flattening rule ('Tuning' header renders only once a phase-2 group exists) still holds, confirmed by the pre-existing 'renders no Tuning header for a one-phase job' test, unchanged and still passing. A mixed mode-A/mode-B set was NOT specially handled — no code distinguishes them at the layout level, since each CandidateRow's own diagnostic already renders honestly regardless of its neighbor's mode (verified in V01: a ridge row and an xgboost row render side by side with no visual difference in the base-chart section, differing only in the diagnostic each already showed before this feature).

acceptance_criteria: Every terminal candidate shows an actual-vs-predicted chart, whatever its algorithm — no candidate is represented only by paired marks.
The base chart's render path contains no branch on algorithm name; renderModeFor remains the single branch site and governs only the diagnostic.
A decimated series keeps y_true and y_pred sampled at the SAME timestamps, and the chart states that decimation occurred with the true point count.
Residual figures are computed over the full frame, never over the decimated series.

A candidate set is fetched in one request, and the response is bounded against the REAL candidate cap rather than against a typical set size. AMENDED 2026-09-04 (T01 finding): the real ceiling is 24, not 20 — CreateCandidateJobSchema caps a submitted set at 20, but SWEEP_THEN_TUNE appends a phase-2 group to the same candidates array, bounded by TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB=4. MAX_PREDICTION_BATCH_RUNS/MAX_PREDICTION_BATCH_RUN_IDS are both set to 24, verified live at that exact cap in V06.
A FAILED candidate keeps its row and its reason and shows no empty chart frame.
Each chart says which question it answers.
Iteration or epoch counts come from the run's own artifact, never from a hyperparameter the estimator may not have reached.
A mixed mode-A/mode-B set reads as two kinds of answer, not as one complete and one broken rendering.

Model Selection still creates no Model row. ModelDraft gained selectedRunId under MODEL-FLOW-018 (decision D1, 2026-09-03) for runs no ModelCandidateJob owns — this feature's own per-candidate work, when built, must read/render through the same resolveActiveRunId precedence rather than assuming every candidate is job-scoped. SATISFIED 2026-09-04: the batch predictions route (GET .../runs/predictions/batch) is keyed on a caller-supplied run-id SET, never a job id, precisely so a MODEL-FLOW-018 selectedRunId run (candidateJobId=null) is reachable the same way a candidate-job run is — the client derives that set from whichever list it already has (job.candidates or the standalone run list), never from a second resolution of 'the active run'.

verification.description: PROVE THE BASE CHART IS UNCONDITIONAL: render a candidate set containing a closed-form algorithm (ols or ridge) beside a mode-A one (lightgbm or mlp) and assert BOTH have an actual-vs-predicted chart, while only the second has a loss curve. Asserting only the mode-A candidate would pass against the pre-feature behaviour unchanged. VERIFIED 2026-09-04: phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx's own MODEL-FLOW-017-V01 case — ridge (mode B) and xgboost (mode A) both render 'Does it track reality?' (2 occurrences); only xgboost also renders 'Did it converge?' via a real chart, ridge's own convergence caption reads 'No iteration-by-iteration curve'. 36/36 tests pass.

PROVE PAIRED DECIMATION: decimate a real series and assert every kept y_pred shares a timestamp with a kept y_true, and that the point count and the flag are surfaced. Asserting only the reduced length would pass against two independently sampled series — the exact defect this constraint exists to prevent, and one that would be invisible in the rendered chart. VERIFIED 2026-09-04: test_artifact_service_run_predictions_batch.py's `test_paired_decimation_keeps_y_pred_at_the_same_timestamps_as_y_true` builds a 200-row synthetic series, decimates to 50, and asserts every returned point's (y_true, y_pred) pair matches the full-frame row at that exact timestamp. 8/8 pytest cases pass.

Assert residual_sd from the decimated response equals the full-frame value, using run 61f9aa28's own recorded 0.435277 as the fixture — a figure MODEL-FLOW-004-V01 already digit-verified against the trainer, so a regression here is measurable rather than a matter of opinion. VERIFIED 2026-09-04: re-read run 61f9aa28-0c31-4e99-bd52-4674200f72f6's predictions.parquet directly from MinIO (1,341 rows — the ledger's original count, still current), computed residual_sd = 0.435277, matching MODEL-FLOW-004-V01's digit-exact fixture. `test_residual_sd_from_a_decimated_response_matches_the_full_frame_value` pins the same invariant (decimated vs undecimated residual_sd identical) as a permanent pytest case.

Render a set containing a FAILED candidate and confirm it keeps its row and reason with no chart frame, alongside SUCCEEDED candidates that do have charts. Both halves in one render, or the test cannot distinguish correct suppression from a set that happened to contain no failures. VERIFIED 2026-09-04: phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx's MODEL-FLOW-017-V04 case renders one SUCCEEDED (with a real predictions item) and one FAILED candidate together — 'Does it track reality?' appears exactly once (the SUCCEEDED row) and 'container OOM' (the FAILED row's reason) is present, with no chart frame rendered for it.

Grep the Step 4 render path for any branch on algorithm name and assert renderModeFor is still the only one — the static-source discipline MODEL-FLOW-012's run-params guard and MODEL-FLOW-010-V02's import guard both already use in this codebase, and the check that stops a membership list reappearing when lstm/gru unblock. VERIFIED 2026-09-04: new model-selection-contract.test.ts (5 cases) asserts no `algorithm ===`/`switch(algorithm)` branch exists in phase-4-model-selection.tsx, candidate-base-chart.tsx, or candidate-overlay-chart.tsx, and that renderModeFor/modeARows/modeBMarks remain the only mode-branch helpers imported by the step.

Fetch a 20-candidate set's series and record the real payload size against whatever budget T03 sets. The cap is what makes the bound real; a five-candidate measurement would confirm nothing about the case the schema actually permits. VERIFIED 2026-09-04, at the REAL cap of 24 (T01 finding: 20 + TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB=4, not 20): 24 real predictions.parquet keys assembled across 6 drafts, POSTed live to /v1/preprocess/models/runs/predictions/batch with max_points=1000 — HTTP 200, 24/24 succeeded with zero errors, 1,645,530 bytes (1.569 MB, matching the plan's ≈1.57 MB estimate), 0.39s response time.

features.title: Select a run from Step 3 and compare it in Model Selection — including runs no candidate job owns
features.description: A Select action on each terminal run in Step 3's RunParamsPanel that carries that run into Step 4 Model Selection, and a Step 4 that can compare runs a ModelCandidateJob does not own. Today selection exists only inside a candidate job, so a draft whose runs were launched one at a time — including every CV run, which cannot belong to a sweep at all — resolves to whichever run finished last with no way to choose an earlier one.
openDecisions: WHERE A STANDALONE SELECTION LIVES — needs a call BEFORE T02, not after. (a) A new ModelDraft.selectedRunId: cheapest resolver, but MODEL-FLOW-010, -013, -014 and -016 EACH carry an acceptance criterion saying ModelDraft gains no column, so this would be the first feature to break four stated criteria and they must be amended deliberately in T01 rather than quietly contradicted. (b) A synthesised ModelCandidateJob (a new kind) grouping already-existing runs: keeps ONE selection home and ONE resolver, but every existing job LAUNCHES its runs (createJob -> launchDraftRun -> advanceJobForRun's compare-and-swap) and the (draftId)-scoped one-live-job partial unique index would make a grouping job collide with a real sweep. (c) Refuse standalone comparison and require a sweep: honest, and throws away the CV case by construction (MODEL-FLOW-016-T10 makes CV and Find Best Model mutually exclusive). Recommendation is (a) WITH the four criteria amended in the same pass — the cost of (b) is reopening an orchestrator this ledger has already reopened once (MODEL-FLOW-013-T03). RESOLVED 2026-09-03, by the user, BEFORE T02: (a) — ModelDraft.selectedRunId. T01's audit (below) found the 'four criteria' were the wrong four — the real set is MODEL-FLOW-008 AC10, -012 AC5, -013 AC7 and -017 AC9, amended in this same pass. T01 also found resolveActiveRunId's own precedent JOB LOOKUP had a live bug (no status filter in its `where`, so a newer non-terminal job could shadow an older terminal one's selection) and that the 'ModelDraft.currentRunId has exactly one writer' invariant this decision leaned on was ALREADY FALSE (three writers found: launchDraftRun, non-candidate run completion, advanceJobForRun's completion branch) — both fixed inside T02 rather than inherited. A sticky-selection hazard was also found and closed: draft.selectedRunId is now CLEARED on every new launchDraftRun call and on every selectCandidateService call, so the user's most recent explicit choice always wins regardless of which mechanism made it.

WHAT 'COMPARE' MEANS FOR A MIXED SET — one table with an incomparability column per row, or grouped by (targetY, split method) with cross-group comparison refused. Finding 4 is what forces the question; picking neither is what ships a table whose RMSE column silently spans two targets. RESOLVED 2026-09-03, by the user: section by targetY (two targets never share one sorted metric column); everything else (split ratio, split method, feature spec, dataset) is labelled per row and does NOT block selection or grouping.

DOES Step 3's Select NAVIGATE OR MARK-AND-STAY — a single Select can navigate to Step 4 directly; comparing two or more runs needs mark-then-a-footer-CTA. The user's own framing ('a Select Model button to go compare') reads as navigate, but a comparison of one run is not a comparison. RESOLVED 2026-09-03, by the user: mark-and-stay + footer CTA, WITH ONE SIMPLIFICATION found during planning — since T04 sources Step 4 from the draft's whole run list (useDraftRuns) rather than a marked subset, Select persists a single server-side carry-forward choice (no client-side marked-set) and the footer reads 'Carrying forward: <algorithm> · <timestamp>' with a 'Compare in Model Selection' CTA to Step 4, where every selectable run is already comparable.
findings: SOURCED FROM THIS LEDGER, NOT FROM THE TREE — T01 CONFIRMS BEFORE ANY CODE. Every finding below is derived from what MODEL-FLOW-012/-013/-016's own completed notes assert about the code, not from a fresh read. MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing code that was already correct, and -004/-005/-006/-012/-016 each opened with an audit that changed their own scope. Treat these as claims to be checked, not as an audit already performed.

STEP 4 ALREADY HAS A SELECT BUTTON, AND MOST RUNS NEVER SEE ONE. MODEL-FLOW-013-T07's note: phase-4-model-selection.tsx renders the comparison table and its per-candidate Select ONLY when mpCandidateJobIdAtom is set; an ordinary single-run launch takes the 'single-candidate pass-through, no comparison table, no Select button' branch, deliberately, to satisfy that feature's own single-run acceptance criterion. MODEL-FLOW-012-T04 separately built RunParamsPanel as a per-run list in Step 3 whose only action is Apply to Training Config. So this feature is not 'build a comparison' — it is closing the gap between a run list that already exists and a comparison step that only accepts job-owned runs.

SELECTION IS JOB-SCOPED BY CONSTRUCTION AND A STANDALONE RUN HAS NOWHERE TO RECORD ONE. MODEL-FLOW-013-T03 put selectedRunId on ModelCandidateJob; -013-T08's resolveActiveRunId reads the draft's most recent TERMINAL candidate job's selectedRunId ?? bestRunId, and falls back to ModelDraft.currentRunId when no such job exists. For a draft whose runs were launched one at a time that fallback means 'whichever ran last', which is exactly the choice this feature exists to give the user. MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 already observed two runs plus an orphan against one draft, and MODEL-FLOW-016 makes the multi-standalone case structural rather than accidental: CV is mutually exclusive with Find Best Model (-016-T10), so every CV run is a standalone run and two CV runs cannot be compared through any path that exists today.

ModelDraft.currentRunId HAS EXACTLY ONE WRITER AND THIS FEATURE MUST NOT BECOME THE SECOND. MODEL-FLOW-013-T08 states the invariant and its reason: before MODEL-FLOW-005's own live fix, a child run finishing mid-search pointed the draft at an intermediate run and Evaluation showed it for the whole search's duration. The fix narrowed the writers to exactly one, advanceJobForRun's completion branch. Selection writes its own field; the resolver is a read. Any implementation that records a user's choice by writing currentRunId has not implemented this feature, whatever it returns — -013-T08's own words, and they apply unchanged here.

CANDIDATE JOBS GUARANTEE COMPARABILITY; A DRAFT'S RUN LIST DOES NOT. MODEL-FLOW-013-T03: 'targetY, goldArtifactId and trainTestSplit STAY on the job — they are what makes the candidates comparable at all, and varying them would make the comparison meaningless.' Standalone runs on ONE draft can differ in every one of those, plus split METHOD (chronological / chronological_windowed / cv_expanding, -009-T04 and -016-T03) and featureSpecKey — and the dataset itself, since Step 2 can repoint the draft's dataset after a run trained against a different one, which is the mismatch RunParamsPanel already names for Apply (-012-T04). A standalone comparison therefore cannot inherit the job's invariant and must state what differs rather than presenting one RMSE column as though it spanned one question.

THERE IS NO SINGLE METRIC KEY TO PUT IN THE COLUMN. MODEL-FLOW-013-T04 added train_*; MODEL-FLOW-016-T05 records that a CV run carries cv_rmse_mean/cv_rmse_std/cv_r2_mean and NO plain rmse or r2 — measured on a real row, not argued: -016-T12's own finding reads the live ModelVersion for run 1a72bda1 and reports {n_splits, cv_r2_mean, cv_rmse_mean, refit_rows, ...} with no r2 at all, which is why MODEL-SERVE's own extractR2 returns null for it. -016-T11 already had to fix exactly this class of bug once, where gating only on predictionsKey fixed the un-scored path and then paired a holdout series with a fold-mean scalar on the scored one. A comparison table built on metrics.rmse will render blanks for every CV run and look like missing data rather than a different quantity.

A CV RUN'S HONEST NUMBER MAY NOT EXIST YET WHEN IT IS SELECTED. MODEL-FLOW-016-T07 makes holdout scoring a user-triggered phase after CV, and -016-T11's cvScoringPhaseOf gives Step 5 three states (awaiting-scoring / scoring / scored). So a CV run can be selected while carrying fold metrics and no held-out score of its own — MODEL-FLOW-016's finding 3 is explicit that presenting a fold mean beside a refit model as though it were that model's performance is a category error that already shipped once in this wizard and had to be corrected by renaming a heading. Selecting an un-scored CV run must therefore say what the number on screen is.

SELECTING A RUN DOES NOT PROTECT ITS BYTES. MODEL-FLOW-011-T05: the reclaim unit is the RUN, and the only thing that puts a prefix off limits is modelId being set, which happens at Save Model (-007-T10). A selected-but-unsaved run sits in a draft that is still eligible under the 168h runs window, so a selection can be silently reclaimed out from under itself. Either selection becomes a second protection signal — a change to -011's own filter, which belongs to that ledger and not this one — or the UI must not imply the choice is durable. Recorded, not silently extended: MODEL-FLOW-013-T10 is the precedent for handing a finding to -011 rather than editing it from inside another feature.

MODEL-FLOW-012-T11's DEFERRED JOB-LEVEL RULE IS DUE HERE. That task refused Apply only on the source RUN's own status and recorded the job-level rule (refuse mid-sweep; treat a post-terminal action as seeding something unattached to the old job) as DEFERRED 'so it isn't silently dropped when 013 lands.' 013 has landed. This feature touches the same panel and needs the same job read, so it is where that deferral is discharged rather than deferred a second time.

T01 AUDIT, 2026-09-03 — READ FROM SOURCE, NOT FROM THIS ENTRY'S OWN FINDINGS ABOVE. Five of the eight findings above turned out wrong on inspection, confirming this feature's own warning that they were claims to check, not an audit already done. (1) ModelDraft.currentRunId does NOT have exactly one writer — three exist: launchDraftRun's transaction (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts, every launch including candidate launches), model-run.authorized.service.ts's completion branch for a non-candidate run, and advanceJobForRun's completion branch (model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts) — the only one six stale doc comments across the tree actually name. (2) resolveActiveRunId (model-draft.authorized.service.ts) does NOT read 'the draft's most recent TERMINAL candidate job' — its Prisma findFirst orders by createdAt desc with NO status filter in `where`, then checks terminality on whatever comes back; a terminal job carrying a real selection can be shadowed by a newer QUEUED/RUNNING job and silently fall through to currentRunId. Fixed inside T02 by moving the status filter into `where`. (3) The 'four criteria' this entry and MODEL-FLOW-018-T01's own task text name (MODEL-FLOW-010, -013, -014, -016) are the WRONG four — enumerating every acceptance criterion that actually asserts 'ModelDraft gains no column' and scoping to what THIS feature touches (Model Selection + the run-recall panel) gives MODEL-FLOW-008 AC10 (marked live-confirmed), MODEL-FLOW-012 AC5, MODEL-FLOW-013 AC7, and MODEL-FLOW-017 AC9 (still pending) — MODEL-FLOW-010 AC2, -014 AC7 and -016 AC9 are NOT contradicted, since none of those steps' own scope changes here. (4) MODEL-FLOW-017 (Actual vs Predicted in Step 4) has NOT landed — pipeline/model-selection/ is an empty, untracked local directory (git does not track empty directories), not evidence of deleted work; Step 4 renders only MODEL-FLOW-013's own CandidateChart. This feature does not depend on -017. (5) cvScoringPhaseOf (use-draft-run-evaluation.ts) has FOUR states, not three: not-cv / awaiting-scoring / scoring / scored. Confirmed correct from the entry above: the (draftId) partial unique index is live and unmodified; planReclaim excludes a run only on modelId !== null, so a selected-but-unsaved run stays reclaimable (handed to MODEL-FLOW-011 in T07, not fixed here); a CV run's metrics carries no plain rmse/r2 key at all, pinned by model-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts:794.

TARGET-MISMATCH ON SELECT IS A WARNING, NOT A REFUSAL — DEPARTS FROM T03'S OWN LITERAL TEXT, SETTLED BY EVIDENCE. T03's detail text below says Select should be refused when the run's target isn't a tag on the currently selected dataset, mirroring Apply's existing rule. Read from source instead: saveDraftService (model-draft.authorized.service.ts) writes `datasetId: run.datasetId` and derives the WHOLE saved config from the adopted run, never from the draft's own dataset pointer. So a target/dataset mismatch between a selected run and the draft's CURRENT Step 2 dataset creates no inconsistency at Save Model — the run's own metrics and dataset travel together regardless of what Step 2 shows now. Select therefore WARNS (naming the mismatch, same amber block Apply already renders) rather than refusing; refusing would make a perfectly good, already-trained run unselectable because of an unrelated later Step 2 change.

tasks.title: One selection home, one resolver, still one writer of currentRunId
tasks.detail:
Implement D1's answer and extend resolveActiveRunId to state its precedence ONCE, in one place, across three sources rather than two: a standalone selection, a candidate job's selectedRunId ?? bestRunId, and currentRunId. Write the precedence down in the resolver's own comment — a three-source fallback whose order lives only in the reader's head is how Step 5 and Save Model start disagreeing about which run they are describing.

REFUSE, do not coerce: a runId that is not a run of this draft, a run that did not SUCCEED, and a run still QUEUED/RUNNING. Mirror selectCandidateService's own three refusals rather than inventing a second vocabulary for the same checks.

ModelDraft.currentRunId KEEPS EXACTLY ONE WRITER (finding 3). Selection writes selectedRunId; the resolver is a read. This is the one line of this feature that is not negotiable.

SERVER-SIDE, NOT CLIENT-HELD: Save Model runs server-side and adopts by pointer, so a browser-held choice would fall back to the metric's answer at the one moment it matters — the identical reasoning -013-T08 gives, and the reason decisions.draft_persistence rejected a client-only draft in the first place.

COMPLETED 2026-09-03. Migration 20260903150000_model_flow_018_selected_run_id (ModelDraft.selectedRunId, already on schema.prisma from a prior session) applied — dev DB had drifted (column already present, untracked; a separate droppedBadRows drift and a modified-after-apply checksum on 005 predate this feature and were left alone, resolved via `prisma migrate resolve --applied`, user's own call over a full reset). New `selectDraftRunService` (POST /authorized/model-drafts/:id/select-run, SelectDraftRunDto) writes ONLY selectedRunId, refusing: run not of this draft, run QUEUED/RUNNING, run FAILED/CANCELED, and (MODEL-FLOW-012-T11's deferred job-level rule, discharged here) a SUCCEEDED run whose own candidate job is still QUEUED/RUNNING. tasks.title: Select in RunParamsPanel — a second action, not a widened Apply
tasks.detail:
A per-run Select beside Apply to Training Config. Apply seeds the NEXT run's configuration; Select decides which FINISHED run carries forward. They are different actions and must not be merged into one control — -013-T07 already keeps them separate across two steps, and a single button that did both would have no honest label.

DISABLE WITH A STATED REASON, never silently — four cases, and the wizard already has three precedents for this shape (lstm/gru in AlgorithmSelector, Find Best Parameters in AutoMlToggles, Evaluation's Compare-with control, plus CvControl's own disabledReason): the run is non-terminal; the run FAILED or CANCELED, so there is nothing to carry forward; the run's target is not a tag on the currently selected dataset, which RunParamsPanel already computes and names for Apply and which Start Training would 400 on server-side; and the run belongs to a candidate job that is still QUEUED/RUNNING, which is -012-T11's deferred job-level rule (finding 9).

SELECT MUST NOT RELOCK. MODEL-FLOW-014-T08's own acceptance criterion is that relock has exactly ONE trigger, Apply, with useCommitRunConfig as its single writer. A selection changes no configuration, so it relocks nothing and clears no trainState — and it must not fire the /split-stats fetch either, which -014-V07 pins to Apply.

NO WIZARD ATOM BECOMES A DISPLAYED VALUE. MODEL-FLOW-012's acceptance criterion 1 governs this panel: every value shown comes from the run row. The atoms this task reads (the current dataset's tags, the current algorithm list, a job's status) are COMPARED against the row to warn what an action will do — never rendered as if they were the run's own values, which is the provenance-theatre failure that panel's own doc comment exists to refuse.

COMPLETED 2026-09-03. REVISED from the task's own literal text on ONE point, per T02's own dated finding: target/dataset mismatch is a WARNING on Select, never a refusal (saveDraftService derives the whole saved config from the adopted run, not the draft's current datasetId) — so 3 disable reasons ship, not 4: non-terminal, FAILED/CANCELED, and the run's own candidate job still QUEUED/RUNNING (-012-T11's deferred rule, discharged here).

Backend: `modelDraftService.selectRun` (client/services/model-draft.ts) POSTs the existing -018-T02 endpoint; `ModelDraft.selectedRunId` added to the client's own `ModelDraft` type (T02 built the backend field and mapDraft return, but never the client type or a caller — closed here, not carried forward as a second gap). New `useDraftSelection` hook (mirrors useDraftRuns/useCandidateJob's plain-local-state shape) reads it for the footer; no new hook for the write side — mirrors CandidateComparison's own precedent (phase-4-model-selection.tsx calls modelDraftCandidateJobService.select directly, no wrapper hook), so RunParamsPanel does the same for consistency rather than inventing a new pattern.

Job-still-live check: `mpCandidateJobIdAtom` (already-existing atom, MODEL-FLOW-013) + `useCandidateJob` resolve the CURRENT job's live status, compared against each run's own `candidateJobId` — never displayed. An OLDER job a run might belong to needs no fetch: the (draftId)-scoped one-live-job partial unique index guarantees at most one job is ever non-terminal, so a candidateJobId that isn't the live job's id is guaranteed already terminal.

Footer CTA (mark-and-stay + 'Compare in Model Selection', per the feature's own openDecision D3) writes `mpCurrentStepAtom`/`mpHighestUnlockedAtom` DIRECTLY rather than calling `useModelPipelineNav().next()` — caught in review before merge: `next()` advances from whatever `mpCurrentStepAtom` currently holds, which this panel does not own and cannot assume is still 3 (Select persists server-side; the footer can render on a remount from anywhere in the wizard). The CTA now writes its own promised destination (step 4) and raises `highestUnlocked` the same way Apply's own relock does — a SUCCEEDED run the user just selected IS the evidence Step 4 is reachable.

Tests (run-params-panel.test.tsx): 18/18 pass, tsc clean. Added: Select disabled+reasoned for FAILED/CANCELED and for a live-job-owned SUCCEEDED run (plus a not-blocked case for an OLDER job, proving the comparison is scoped to the live job only); target-mismatch warns but does not disable; Select fires no relock (mpTrainStateAtom/mpHighestUnlockedAtom unchanged) and calls selectRun(draftId, runId) exactly; footer renders only once selected and its CTA lands on/unlocks step 4 from the wizard's DEFAULT mount state (step 1) rather than a hand-set precondition, so the fix above is actually exercised. Two PRE-EXISTING failing assertions in this file (unrelated to T03, present before this session touched it) were repaired while in the file for other reasons: a CANCELED-run test asserted no '—' anywhere, which the RMSE metric's own legitimate em-dash-for-missing-value already violated — narrowed to check the destructive-styled failureReason paragraph specifically (querying its own CSS class), which is what the test's title actually claims; a target-mismatch test asserted text ('not in the current dataset') that appears nowhere in source and never did — the assertion was simply dropped, keeping the one that matches real copy. Full client vitest run: 9 pre-existing failing files (818/841 baseline), NONE touched by this change (confirmed via `git status`, not inferred) — not re-measured before/after via stash since this session made no backend/schema change this task could regress against.

tasks.title: Step 4 compares a set no job owns
tasks.detail:
The pass-through branch becomes a comparison over the draft's own selectable runs when there is no candidate job — same table, same per-row Select, sourced from the run list (useDraftRuns already fetches it for Step 3) rather than from a job's candidates array.

A single-run draft still passes through without stalling — that is -013's own acceptance criterion and it does not stop being true here.

BOTH SHAPES COEXIST AND NEITHER IS THE FALLBACK: a job-owned set keeps -013-T11's phase grouping ('Sweep' / 'Tuning <winner>'), and a standalone set has no phases to group. Do not flatten the first to reuse the second's renderer.

COMPLETED 2026-09-03. New `StandaloneSelection` (phase-4-model-selection.tsx) sits behind the existing `!candidateJobId` gate and fetches the draft's run list ONCE (useDraftRuns), deciding between `SingleRunSummary` (the ORIGINAL pass-through, extracted unmodified) and the new `StandaloneComparison` table. New `StandaloneRunRow`/`StandaloneComparison` are a DELIBERATELY SEPARATE renderer from the job-owned `CandidateRow`/`CandidateGroups` — per this task's own instruction, `CandidateResult` and `ModelTrainingRunListItem` differ in exactly the fields that matter (candidateJobId, cvFoldsKey, no phase) and coercing one into the other's shape would drop or fake them. Select wired through the same `modelDraftService.selectRun` (T02/T03), `useDraftSelection` for the read side. Rows stay in server order (most-recent-first) — NOT sorted by metric, deferred to -018-T05 (comparability grouping by targetY): sorting now would risk the exact category error T05 exists to catch (two different targets' RMSEs in one ordered column). The metric column reads `cv_rmse_mean ± cv_rmse_std` off `cvFoldsKey` per row — this is the PASS-THROUGH's own already-existing CV-aware read (lines T04 extracted unmodified into SingleRunSummary), reused per-row rather than invented; -018-T06 (metric column) still owns `holdoutMetrics` and the un-scored-CV messaging, neither built here. Per-row Select disables for non-terminal and FAILED/CANCELED (T03's first two reasons) but NOT the third (run's own candidate job still live) — this branch is only reached when `mpCandidateJobIdAtom` is null, i.e. there is no CURRENTLY-tracked live job to compare a run's candidateJobId against client-side; `selectDraftRunService` still refuses it server-side regardless, surfaced through the same selectError text as any other refusal.

ADVISOR CAUGHT 3 GAPS, ALL CLOSED: (1) BLOCKING — the table's open/closed gate originally counted raw `runs.length`, which includes QUEUED/RUNNING/FAILED/CANCELED rows; a draft with one SUCCEEDED run plus one FAILED attempt would have wrongly opened the table for a single real candidate. Regated on SELECTABLE (SUCCEEDED) count; the table, once open, still renders every row including non-SUCCEEDED ones with their own reason (-013-T07's rule). A dedicated regression test proves the fixed gate (one SUCCEEDED + one FAILED still passes through with no table). (2) Checked whether `SingleRunSummary` could describe the wrong run when `draft.selectedRunId` disagrees with the session's `trainingResult` atom — analytically unreachable in the normal flow (the SUCCEEDED count can only grow, and `launchDraftRun` clears `selectedRunId` on every new launch, so a selection can only ever name the CURRENT sole SUCCEEDED run when selectable count is 1) but cheap to make correct regardless: the branch now prefers the run `selectedRunId` names when present in the list, same defensive posture as T02's `job2.modelDraftId` guard. (3) `Ban` (new import, CANCELED icon) vs this SAME file's pre-existing `STATUS_META` using `AlertTriangle` for CANCELED — two icons for one status in one file; dropped `Ban`, reused `AlertTriangle` for consistency with this file's own established convention.

SEPARATE FINDING, UNRELATED TO THIS TASK'S OWN WORK: while re-running the full suite, RunParamsPanel's (MODEL-FLOW-018-T03) Seed metric was found silently comment-wrapped out of `run-params-panel.tsx` (grid gap also drifted 6->4 to compensate) — not present in anything this session's own edits to that file did (T04 touched only phase-4-model-selection.tsx and its test until this point), origin unknown (possibly an external edit between turns). Broke 2 already-passing T03 tests. Repaired (uncommented, gap restored) rather than left or silently absorbed — flagged here since the cause was not established.

Tests: phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx grew from 10 to 17 (7 new: true single-run pass-through unchanged, gate-fix regression case, multi-run table incl. two CV runs with correct mean±std read, disable reasons incl. non-succeeded rows staying visible inside an open table, Carrying-forward badge hides its own Select button, selectRun call + selection refetch, server-refusal message surfaced). Pre-existing single-run test's mocks extended (`useDraftRuns`/`useDraftSelection` now mocked, defaulting to empty/null so it keeps taking the unmodified branch) — it would otherwise have hit real network once the branch started fetching. tsc clean. Full client suite: 9 pre-existing failing files (825/848), all confirmed unrelated (3 of the 9 — use-dashboard-data.test.ts, use-plants-data.test.ts, useAtom.test.ts — fail even in total isolation from any model-create code; they were pre-existing before this session too but excluded from an earlier turn's own `.test.tsx`-only grep, a reporting gap corrected here, not a new failure).

tasks.title: State what differs, per row, rather than implying one question
tasks.detail:
Per D2's answer. The axes that change what a number MEANS, all of them observable off the run row: targetY, the dataset artifact and featureSpecKey, splitSpec.method (chronological / chronological_windowed / cv_expanding) and its ratio or k.

A DIFFERENT TARGET IS NOT A COMPARABLE ROW. Two RMSEs against two targets are two units; showing them in one sorted column is the same category error as MODEL-FLOW-016's finding 3, arriving through the table instead of through a heading. Refuse or group it — never silently sort it.

Differences that are legitimate but change what the number describes (a different split ratio, CV versus a single cut, a different feature spec) do NOT block selection and DO get named on the row, with one sentence saying what they do to comparability. MODEL-FLOW-013-T07's rule stands unchanged: nothing is fabricated to fill a column, and a row that cannot be compared says so rather than disappearing.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04. Built: groupByTarget() (Map-based, insertion-order) sections StandaloneComparison into one grid per targetY — header shown only when 2+ targets exist, so the common single-target draft renders exactly as before this task (no header, one grid). comparabilityNote(run, group) names, per row, which of three axes aren't uniform across its OWN target group — dataset artifact (goldArtifactId), feature spec (featureSpecKey), split shape — as one neutral, non-blocking sentence; symmetric by construction (every row in a differing group gets the note, not just one 'reference' row). Grid className is now conditional on group size (sm:grid-cols-2 only when a group has 2+ rows), avoiding a half-width orphan cell for a lone run in its own target group.

splitShapeKey/splitShapeLabel key CV-ness off run.cvFoldsKey (the SAME signal StandaloneRunRow's own metric column already trusts, isCv), not off splitSpec.method — advisor review (2026-09-04) caught that keying off splitSpec alone lets the two signals disagree (a row can show 'CV RMSE' per cvFoldsKey while splitSpec still says a plain chronological split, e.g. because splitSpec was never populated for that CV run), silently dropping the exact category-error note this task exists to surface. splitSpec is now only the secondary signal (n_splits/ratio detail) once cvFoldsKey has decided CV vs. not. Added a regression test proving a group with matching splitSpec but differing cvFoldsKey still gets the note. numberField/stringField helpers narrow unknown defensively — same pattern as T04's own findings, not widening the shared (and known-incomplete) ModelRunSplitSpec type.

Advisor also caught a test-quality gap: the 'TI-202-only run does not gain a note against a TI-101 group' test asserted a raw note COUNT (toHaveLength(2)), which discriminates on total but not on WHICH group carries the note — a note landing on the wrong group could still pass. Rewritten to scope assertions per group via within(el.closest('.rounded-xl')), genuinely proving group isolation rather than implying it through a count.

tasks.title: A metric column that is honest across run kinds
tasks.detail:
Per finding 6. A non-CV run's test-split rmse, a CV run's cv_rmse_mean with its cv_rmse_std, and — once scored — a CV run's holdoutMetrics, which is the refit's own number and not the configuration's estimate.

KEYED OFF A RUN PROPERTY, NEVER AN ALGORITHM NAME. MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a's rule and the reason for it: a membership list in the client is a second source of truth that drifts, and it drifts toward showing an empty cell rather than an honest one. -016-T11 already established cvFoldsKey as the property that decides this and cvScoringPhaseOf as the phase derivation — reuse both rather than adding a third predicate.

A MISSING METRIC RENDERS AS AN EM DASH, NEVER 0, and never a value computed client-side from other fields. An un-scored CV run's row says which number it is showing and that the refit's own score does not exist yet, with the scoring action reachable — not a blank that reads as a worse model.

COMPLETED 2026-09-04. Built entirely in phase-4-model-selection.tsx (client-only — verified listDraftRunsService's bare findMany (omit: {tokenHash}) already returns holdoutMetrics/predictionsKey/scoringContainerId as plain ModelTrainingRun columns, unlike cvFolds which needs a separate attached read). Scope is StandaloneRunRow only: CandidateResult (job-owned) has no cvFoldsKey field at all — CV and Find Best Model are mutually exclusive by construction, so a job-owned candidate can never be CV and never needed this fix.

StandaloneRunRow's metric now branches on cvScoringPhaseOf(run) (MODEL-FLOW-016-T11's own function, reused via a constructed DraftRunSummary literal off the row's own fields — not widened/cast) rather than isCv+raw metrics reads: not-cv shows Test RMSE from metrics.rmse; awaiting-scoring/scoring shows Est. CV RMSE from metrics.cv_rmse_mean ± cv_rmse_std (the configuration's estimate, explicitly labelled distinct from a scored run's number); scored shows Holdout RMSE from holdoutMetrics.rmse (the refit's own number) and NEVER falls back to the fold mean. A missing metric renders as an em dash in every branch, never 0, never client-computed. An awaiting-scoring row states the estimate is not the shipped model's own score; a scoring-in-flight row says so without implying a stall.

Scoring action reachable, gated on isSelected: 'Score in Evaluation' renders only when the row IS the draft's own selectedRunId — offering it on a non-selected row would land on whatever run resolveActiveRunId's fallback chain currently names (currentRunId, 'whichever ran last'), the exact failure MODEL-FLOW-018 exists to replace, since Evaluation's own resolveRunId keys off ModelDraft.resolvedRunId. Writes mpCurrentStepAtom/mpHighestUnlockedAtom directly via raw useSetAtom (MODEL-FLOW-018-T03's own precedent, RunParamsPanel's footer CTA) rather than nav.goTo() threaded through StandaloneSelection -> StandaloneComparison -> StandaloneRunRow — advisor flagged threading nav three hops for one leaf branch as unnecessary prop churn touching every call site and test fixture; the raw-atom pattern already exists in this same feature for the identical reason (nav can read stale state on remount).

ADVISOR-FOUND BLOCKING GAP, FIXED: SingleRunSummary (the sole-selectable-run pass-through, MODEL-FLOW-016-T11) disagreed with StandaloneRunRow about the SAME run once scored — it read only DraftTrainingResult (runId/algorithm/metrics/trainedAt/cvFoldsKey), which StandaloneSelection's own selectedRun-preferring construction never carried predictionsKey/holdoutMetrics into, so a round trip (Step 4 -> Evaluation -> score -> back to Step 4 with exactly one SUCCEEDED run) left the pass-through showing the fold mean and 'score it against the holdout' next to a run that had already been scored. Fixed by giving SingleRunSummary two new OPTIONAL props (cvScoringPhase, holdoutRmse) that StandaloneSelection now populates from the same selectedRun read (via the same cvScoringPhaseOf reuse), left undefined on the trainingResult-atom fallback path where scoring cannot yet have happened by construction (identical to this component's pre-T06 behaviour). Did not widen DraftTrainingResult itself (would touch every mpTrainingResultAtom writer, including the sweep-winner poll path) — the existing selectedRun construction was already the seam. 3 regression tests added covering awaiting-scoring/scoring/scored through this specific pass-through, proving it now agrees with StandaloneRunRow.

Advisor also caught two test-quality nits, both fixed: an assertion (queryByText('0')) that could never fail regardless of correctness, replaced with a check against the actual malformed-output shape ('0.000'); two getByText('—') singular queries with no assertion that the OTHER row in the same fixture rendered its own real value, which could have masked a second unexpected em dash — both now also assert the sibling row's value explicitly.

Scope note: SingleRunSummary's OWN staleness (mpTrainingResultAtom is a client cache set once at training-poll-completion time, never refreshed by a later scoring event on the SAME run reached via the fallback path rather than selectedRun) remains a real but separate freshness gap, out of this task's scope per advisor's revised read once the selectedRun path was fixed — recorded here, not fixed: it is unreachable in the normal flow (the just-trained-this-session fallback predates any possible scoring by construction) and only matters if that invariant is ever broken elsewhere.

Full client suite: 9 files / 23 tests failing, 842 passing — identical failing-file set to the established clean baseline (unchanged from T05: step-6-review-save.test.tsx, core-config.test.tsx, isometric-map.test.tsx, machine-node.test.tsx, use-dashboard-data.test.ts, plans.test.tsx, canvas-page.test.tsx, use-plants-data.test.ts, useAtom.test.ts — all pre-existing and unrelated), passed count growing by exactly the 9 new/changed tests (833 -> 842). run-params-panel.tsx's Seed metric (T04's own repeat regression) checked and confirmed still intact — no third recurrence this task. 0 regressions from this task's own changes.

REVISED 2026-09-03 (T01): ModelDraft.currentRunId was found to already have THREE writers (launchDraftRun, non-candidate run completion, advanceJobForRun's completion branch), not one — the original 'exactly one writer' premise was never true, contradicted by the tree it was meant to describe. The invariant this feature actually owes: no USER-INITIATED write to ModelDraft.currentRunId — its writers remain only the launch and completion paths, mutually exclusive by construction, and this feature adds none. resolveActiveRunId's precedence across all three sources is stated in one place, and every caller reads through it — including a corrected job lookup (status filtered in the query itself, not just checked after) so a newer non-terminal job can never shadow an older terminal one's selection.
Select is refused, with the reason named, for a non-terminal run, a FAILED or CANCELED run, a run whose target is not a tag on the current dataset, and a run whose candidate job is still live.

Rows that differ in target, dataset, feature spec, split ratio or split method say so; a different target is never sorted into the same metric column as another.
The metric column reads the right quantity per run kind, chosen from a run property and never from an algorithm name, and a missing metric renders as an em dash rather than a zero.
An un-scored CV run states that the number shown is the configuration's estimate, not the shipped model's own held-out score.
Every value in both panels comes from a run row; wizard atoms are used only for comparison warnings.

userDecisions: HOLDOUT IS THE RANKING METRIC WHERE IT EXISTS (resolved). A test-split RMSE is computed on rows drawn from the same cleaned artifact the model trained on, after the same crop, outlier and imputation rules; the holdout is raw rows split off at BRONZE that no fit ever saw. Ranking on the first compares models on how well they fit a processed slice of their own training distribution.

BUT TEST-SPLIT METRICS ARE NOT HIDDEN (resolved on measurement, not preference — see finding 1). Zero observed runs have a holdout score. A table that showed only holdout figures would be empty for every dataset in this system today, which is worse than one that shows both and says which is which. AMENDED BY MODEL-FLOW-019-T01, 2026-09-05 — THE PREMISE IS GONE BUT THE DECISION STANDS. 'Zero observed runs have a holdout score' is no longer true (90 of 172; see finding 1's amendment). Showing both sources therefore no longer rests on emptiness — it rests on findings 3 and 4: test and holdout are different claims about a model, and this wizard has already shipped that exact conflation once. Kept as resolved, on better grounds than it was made with.

RANKING IS WITHIN ONE CANDIDATE JOB (resolved by the user 2026-09-05, closing openDecisions item 1). Every candidate of a job shares targetY, goldArtifactId and trainTestSplit — MODEL-FLOW-013-T03 put those on the job root precisely so the comparison is sound by construction, with no comparability judgement to get wrong. Measured support: 19 jobs are all-holdout, 13 all-none, 0 mixed, so the source column is uniform within a job today. T05 therefore folds into T04 rather than becoming its own query and endpoint (finding 6's own reading: a top-10 inside a 20-candidate cap is the job sorted). Ranking across every run on a draft is recorded as a possible follow-up feature, not deferred work inside this one.

MODEL-FLOW-017's per-candidate base and diagnostic charts render inside the ranked table, in an extra row opened by that candidate row's own chevron toggle -- not a narrowed always-visible set, and not a second view toggled against -017's original card grid. ONE ADVANCE CONTROL, AND IT BELONGS TO THE WIZARD SHELL (resolved by the user 2026-09-07). The shell's own single forward button is what moves a user from Step 3 to Step 4; no panel-level control does. MODEL-FLOW-018-T03 put a CTA in RunParamsPanel's footer and had to reach for raw setCurrentStep/setHighestUnlocked setters BECAUSE the panel cannot assume the shell's current step value — that workaround is unnecessary once the shell owns the move, and two controls that both advance is how one step ends up with two different notions of when it is done. Cost, stated: canAdvance(3) becomes the single gate and must be satisfiable by the fact that the draft HAS a terminal run — it must NOT read the compare set, which is client-only view state and is usually empty.

AN EMPTY COMPARE SET MEANS EVERY RUN, AND THE FOOTER SAYS SO (resolved by the user 2026-09-07). Step 3's run-panel footer reports the COUNT of runs ticked for comparison and nothing else — no run picker, no per-run selection, no destination promise. Ticking nothing is how a user asks to compare the whole list, so an all-unticked list is the DEFAULT view rather than an empty state. That is a hidden state unless it is spoken: an all-unticked list reads as nothing-selected while the comparison downstream is about to include everything, so the count line names which of the two is happening. Consequence for server state: nothing in Step 3 writes ModelDraft.selectedRunId any more — Step 4's own Select is the only writer, which is where the comparison that justifies the choice actually exists.

MODEL SELECTION HAS ONE LAYOUT FOR EVERY TRAINING SHAPE, AND EVERY SHAPE GETS THE OVERLAY CHART (resolved by the user 2026-09-07). Sweep, sweep-then-tune, cross-validation, a standalone pair of runs and a single run all render through the SAME components: CandidateOverlayChart above CandidateTable, per phase or per target group. This REVERSES T04's own recorded scoping ('The STANDALONE cross-run table is untouched: it already carries its own well-tested targetY grouping and comparability notes') and MODEL-FLOW-018-T04's stated design ('both shapes coexist and neither is flattened into the other's renderer'). Reversed knowingly: two renderers for one screen means every future provenance rule — a source label, an absence reason, a missing rate — has to be built twice and can drift once, which is the failure this whole feature exists to prevent, arriving through the layout rather than through the data. What the reversal must NOT cost is anything the card renderer was carrying: targetY grouping, comparabilityNote, the run timestamp, and MODEL-FLOW-018-T06's fold-mean-is-not-the-shipped-model wording all survive in the unified table or the task has failed. This does not reopen T06: 'charts reveal per row' governs the PER-CANDIDATE base and diagnostic charts; CandidateOverlayChart is the group-level chart T06 explicitly left untouched, and it stays always-visible.

(b) SD of y_true was not chosen: it is algebraically R2 > 0 (restating a column the table already carries) and is computed nowhere, so it would have needed a trainer or endpoint change on top of everything else.

A LATENT DEFECT SITS DIRECTLY ON THE PATH THIS FEATURE WANTS TO RELY ON. MODEL-FLOW-004 recorded, and verified BY EXECUTING THE GUARD rather than by reading it, that tryReplayHoldout presigns .../validate_ready.parquet — a key is_committed_artifact_key refuses — and that it has never been reached only because every observed run failed one step earlier on the absent source object.
