The defect described here is fixed and the holdout path is producing real figures in the dev DB. Nothing in this feature is blocked on it any longer.

TEST AND HOLDOUT ARE NOT TWO MEASUREMENTS OF ONE THING. The test split comes from the same artifact the model trained on, past the same cleaning recipe. The holdout is raw rows separated at BRONZE, deliberately unimputed (DS-LAKE-018's resolved no-imputation decision), so a MISSING_VALUE hole reaches predict() and depresses the score for reasons that are not the model's fault — which is exactly why DS-LAKE-018-T05 requires the holdout's own missing rate be published beside every metric it produces. A table putting both under one 'RMSE' header would invite a comparison that is not valid in either direction.

THE CONFLATION THIS FEATURE PREVENTS HAS ALREADY HAPPENED ONCE IN THIS WIZARD. MODEL-FLOW-004 had to RENAME a shipped heading — 'Validation residual diagnostics' to 'Test-split residual diagnostics' — because a section summarising the run's test split was labelled as though it summarised the validation holdout. One feature later. Naming which split a number came from is not a presentational nicety here; it is the specific mistake this codebase has demonstrably made.

RANKING NEEDS A DEFINED ORDER, INCLUDING WHEN THE METRIC IS ABSENT. A candidate set can mix a run with a holdout score against one without, a FAILED candidate with no metrics at all, and — once MODEL-FLOW-016 lands — a CV run whose headline figure is a fold mean and std rather than a single number. 'Top 10' is undefined across those until the ordering rule says what a missing metric sorts as. Sorting a null to the bottom quietly is the same class of silent decision as sorting it to the top. EXTENDED BY MODEL-FLOW-019-T01, 2026-09-05, WITH TWO MEASURED FACTS. FIRST, a mixed-source set is NOT reachable inside one candidate job today: grouping the 106 job-owned runs gives 19 jobs where every candidate has a holdout figure, 13 where none does, and ZERO mixed — holdout presence follows the dataset, not the candidate. Mixedness arises only across jobs/datasets or from the 56 pre-cutover runs on holdout-bearing dataset f7d2d259, so V01 and V03 must be built on fixtures or on those legacy rows rather than on a freshly trained job. SECOND, the null-metric case already has a second door this finding did not name: a CV run carries no bare rmse at all (only cv_rmse_mean/std — confirmed against the 4 real CV runs in the DB), so any ranker reading metrics.rmse reads null on every CV run by construction.

TOP 10 IS ABOVE THE CANDIDATE CAP, WHICH MAKES THE SCOPE QUESTION REAL. CreateCandidateJobSchema caps a set at 20, and a sweep is typically 3-5. A top-10 within one job is therefore usually the whole job sorted. Ranking ACROSS jobs — every run a draft has ever produced — is a different and more useful feature, and it is the reading 'from the models that have been trained' most naturally supports. Which one is meant changes the query, the endpoint and whether cross-job comparability even holds (see openDecisions).

THE STEP HOLDS ONE PIECE OF SERVER STATE AND ONLY ONE: selectedRunId on the job. Stated up front the way MODEL-FLOW-010's third finding was, so the step is not handed a column by reflex. AMENDED 2026-09-06, THEN CORRECTED 2026-09-07 BY T07 ITSELF. The 2026-09-06 amendment here claimed 'a SECOND field now exists -- ModelDraft.acceptanceCriteria... on the DRAFT' -- checked against packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma and the whole backend and found FALSE: no such column was ever built, and T07's own task detail says the opposite ('THRESHOLDS ARE VIEW STATE, NOT DRAFT STATE... NOT a new ModelDraft column'), matching AC16 ('Thresholds add no ModelDraft column'). T07 shipped exactly that: mpAcceptanceCriteriaAtom (store/model-pipeline.ts), committed on Apply through useRunConfigDraft like every other Core Config field. This finding's original claim stands correctly as written above.

T07's OWN DETAIL OVERSTATES METRIC_META's accent FUNCTION. It says 'METRIC_META already encodes direction implicitly -- its accent function knows a low RMSE is good' -- checked against lib/model-metrics.ts and found only r2's entry has an accent function; rmse/mae/sd have none. Direction actually lives in lib/metric-ranking.ts's own RANK_DIRECTION (built for T03's ranking), reused directly by T07's comparatorSymbol rather than a new table -- harmless in outcome (AC15 is satisfied either way, since the comparator is still derived, never stored) but recorded so a later reader does not go looking for a direction table inside METRIC_META that isn't there.

FEATURE IMPORTANCE IS NOT WRITTEN BY ANY RUN TODAY, SO THIS IS A TRAINER CHANGE, NOT A UI CHANGE. The five run artifacts are model.joblib, metrics.json, run_manifest.json, predictions.parquet, plus loss_history.json and cv_folds.json where they apply -- no importance among them, and run_manifest.json carries provenance (gold_object_key, artifact_checksum, target_y, algorithm, hyperparameters, seed, split, metrics, holdout_metrics, model_sha256, framework_versions) not per-feature figures. A new artifact must be registered in the SAME three places every existing filename is (train.py's outputs dict, apps/python's _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS, TS RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES) -- MODEL-FLOW-013-T05 states that missing one is how a filename ends up refused at upload, and MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 separately had to add a missing Dockerfile COPY for the same class of omission. It also needs an image bump, and MODEL-FLOW-016-T07 recorded that resolveDigest() pins the image at BOOT, so a bump does nothing until the backend restarts. 179 existing runs will never have this artifact.

THREE OF THE TWELVE ALGORITHMS HAVE NO IMPORTANCE TO READ, AND A FOURTH'S MEANS SOMETHING ELSE. Tree-based estimators (hist_gradient_boosting, random_forest, lightgbm, xgboost) expose feature_importances_; linear ones (ols, ridge) expose coef_, which is a per-feature weight and comparable only against standardised inputs. svm with a non-linear kernel has NEITHER (coef_ exists for a linear kernel only), grp has neither, and lstm/gru have neither in any form a per-feature ranking could use. pls has coef_ but it is a projection onto latent components, not a per-input importance in the sense the other rows mean -- displaying it under the same header would be a category error of the kind MODEL-FLOW-004 had to rename a shipped heading to undo. An absent importance is therefore the NORMAL case for several algorithms and must read as its own stated fact, never as an empty table.

IMPURITY-BASED IMPORTANCE IS BIASED TOWARD HIGH-CARDINALITY FEATURES, AND ON THIS SYSTEM'S DATA THAT BIAS IS MEASURED, NOT THEORETICAL. MODEL-FLOW-020-T03's census read every live artifact from parquet: process tags hold roughly 1,000 distinct values each while the target holds 32 to 97. sklearn's own documentation warns that impurity-based importances inflate for features with many unique values, so on a frame of ~1,000-distinct process tags the ranking will favour the finest-grained sensor over a genuinely predictive coarse one, and the number will look entirely plausible. Permutation importance does not have that bias -- but it costs a refit-free re-scoring pass per feature over the test split, which is real container time and is a scope decision, not a default. Whichever is written must NAME ITS METHOD beside the figures, or a reader cannot calibrate what they are looking at.

'HOW MANY FEATURES IS GOOD' HAS NO ANSWER FROM THIS SYSTEM'S DATA, AND MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 ALREADY MEASURED WHY. That task ran a max_depth ladder against the real trainer image on the real holdout at three effective sample sizes (32, 59 and 97 distinct labelled values) and got THREE DIFFERENT ORDERINGS of the same five settings, with 5-7% spreads against within-cell SDs of 0.0002-0.0030. Capacity does not separate on this data. Feature COUNT is a capacity question on the same data, so a recommended count written now would be extrapolation from a range that cannot support it -- the 'guess wearing a formula' MODEL-FLOW-020's own finding 3 forbids, and it would read exactly like a measured constant. What CAN be stated is arithmetic rather than advice: the cumulative share of importance the top k carry, and the effective sample size per feature (distinct labelled values divided by feature count -- 32 over 21 is 1.5, a number a reliability engineer can act on without being told what to conclude).

THE FEATURE COUNT IS ALREADY RECORDED AND ALREADY DISAGREES WITH ITSELF IN ONE PLACE. metrics.feature_count exists on every run (metrics.py's own key set) and feature_spec.json carries the column list with derived_from_target and target_scaled (MODEL-FLOW-000-T02). But a SEQUENCE run's feature_count counts columns while its train_rows/test_rows count WINDOWS (MODEL-FLOW-009-T04's own note, which states this explicitly wherever those numbers surface), so a per-feature table on an lstm/gru run would sit beside row counts that mean something else. Since lstm/gru have no importance to show anyway, the honest resolution is that they render the absence, not a partial table.

IMPURITY/coef_ ONLY, RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-07 (T09, openDecision 5). Asked directly via AskUserQuestion rather than decided unilaterally, per this task's own detail flagging it as needing a call before any trainer code was written. Matches the item's own stated recommendation: free, already computed inside the fit, no extra container time. Permutation importance is recorded as a follow-up, not scheduled. Two further decisions were T09's own to make (its detail explicitly delegated them) and are recorded here rather than only in the task result: pls gets its own method name 'pls-coefficient', never grouped under 'coefficient' (a PLS coefficient is a projection through latent components, a different quantity); an unscaled linear fit still WRITES the artifact with standardized:false and the CLIENT refuses to rank it, rather than omitting the artifact and collapsing that run into the same 'not recorded' bucket a genuinely pre-feature legacy run uses (AC11's three-facts rule, applied here for the same reason).

openDecisions: IS THE RANKING WITHIN ONE CANDIDATE JOB, OR ACROSS EVERY RUN ON THE DRAFT? Within a job, every candidate shares one artifact, target and split, so the comparison is sound by construction — that is why MODEL-FLOW-013-T03 kept those three fields on the job root rather than on each candidate. Across jobs, two runs may have trained against different artifacts or different split ratios, and their RMSEs are then not comparable at all. If cross-job is wanted, the table must show what differs and refuse to rank rows that are not comparable, rather than sorting them together and letting the number imply they are. RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-05: WITHIN ONE CANDIDATE JOB. See userDecisions. The cross-job reading is not built here; if it is ever picked up, listDraftRunsService (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:600-615) already returns every run on a draft with holdoutMetrics and splitSpec included, so it needs no new endpoint — only the comparability rule this item describes.

WHAT DOES A CV CANDIDATE RANK ON, once MODEL-FLOW-016 lands? Its headline is a fold mean with a spread, and a model at 0.6 ± 0.02 is not the same as one at 0.6 ± 0.4 — ranking on the mean alone discards the one thing k fits were paid for. Not decided here because MODEL-FLOW-016 is not built; recorded so this table is not designed as though every candidate has exactly one number.

DOES THE ONE-ADVANCE-CONTROL RULE KILL StandaloneRunRow's 'Score in Evaluation' CTA? That button also advances the wizard (setCurrentStep(5)) from inside a panel, so it is literally the shape the rule forbids — but its destination is not the shell's next step, and its whole reason for existing is that a CV run awaiting scoring has no meaning until it is scored. Three readings: keep it as a same-screen action that happens to navigate; move the affordance to Step 4's row action and let the shell's forward button carry the user; or drop it and rely on the user reaching Evaluation themselves. NOT decided here — recorded so a later reader sees the rule was applied deliberately rather than applied to everything that calls a step setter. RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-07 (T08): KEEP IT, as a deliberate exception. The one-advance-control rule is about the Step 3 -> Step 4 boundary; this button's destination is not the shell's next step, and an awaiting-scoring CV run has no meaning until it is scored, so the affordance has to live where the user sees the run. See userDecisions.

DOES A SINGLE SELECTABLE RUN STILL GET SingleRunSummary, OR A ONE-ROW TABLE? MODEL-FLOW-013's acceptance criterion is that a single run must not stall on a comparison table, and SingleRunSummary is how that has been honoured since -016-T11 (extended by -018-T06 with cvScoringPhase/holdoutRmse). One layout for every shape reads as replacing it with a 1-row table plus its overlay chart, which satisfies the criterion's SPIRIT (nothing to choose between, and the table does not ask you to choose) while contradicting its letter. Whichever is chosen, the -018-T06 facts SingleRunSummary carries — fold mean estimates the configuration, holdout scoring refits nothing — must appear in the replacement or the round trip that task fixed reopens. RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-07 (T08): A ONE-ROW TABLE. SingleRunSummary is deleted; every run count, including one, renders through the same CandidateTable + CandidateOverlayChart. See userDecisions.

IMPURITY OR PERMUTATION IMPORTANCE? Needs a call before T09 writes anything. (a) IMPURITY/coef_ -- free, already computed inside the fitted estimator, one attribute read after fit, no extra container time; but biased toward high-cardinality features, which on this system's own frames (process tags ~1,000 distinct against a 32-97 distinct target) is a real and measured bias, not a footnote. (b) PERMUTATION importance over the test split -- unbiased by cardinality and it measures what a reader actually assumes importance means (how much worse the model gets without this feature), but it costs one re-scoring pass per feature: 21 features against a 2,554-row test split is 21 predict() calls, which is cheap in absolute terms and is still a per-run cost this ledger has not measured. (c) BOTH, side by side, since disagreement between them is itself the finding -- a feature ranked first by impurity and tenth by permutation is telling the reader something neither number says alone. RECOMMENDATION IS (a) FIRST, method named beside the figures, with (b) recorded as a follow-up: it ships the table without a cost nobody has measured, and naming the method is what keeps (b) from being a silent correction later. RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-07 (T09): (a), IMPURITY/coef_ ONLY. Matches this item's own recommendation exactly. Permutation importance (b) stays a recorded, undated follow-up -- not built, not scheduled. See userDecisions.

IS A RECOMMENDED FEATURE COUNT SHOWN AT ALL? The user asked for it directly. MODEL-FLOW-020-T03's three-dataset measurement says no threshold is derivable from this system's data, and MODEL-FLOW-020's own AC5 is left OPEN for exactly that reason ('the ladder found no size that performed measurably worse... refusing on an unmeasured threshold is the failure AC3 exists to prevent'). Three readings: (a) show the arithmetic only -- cumulative importance share and observations-per-feature -- and let the engineer conclude; (b) show a recommended band and label it synthetic-derived or literature-derived, weaker than every other measured constant in this codebase and knowingly so; (c) show a band derived from a real feature-ablation ladder on this system's data, which is the MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 experiment run over feature count instead of depth and is a task of its own, not a line of copy. RECOMMENDATION IS (a) NOW AND (c) AS ITS OWN TASK IF WANTED -- (b) is the one shape this ledger has consistently refused. AMENDED 2026-09-07 -- STALE, ALREADY RESOLVED, NOT 'NOT DECIDED HERE'. AC26 (added alongside this item) already settles this to reading (a): 'No recommended feature count is displayed unless a measurement on this system's own data supports it. The cumulative importance share and the observations-per-feature figure ARE displayed, as arithmetic over figures the run already recorded.' T09 built exactly that (lib/feature-importance.ts's observationsPerFeature, arithmetic only, no band) and nothing else. (c) remains open as its own task if ever wanted.

6. WHICH SD? Needs a call before MODEL-FLOW-019-T11 is built, and the two readings give opposite results. (a) RESIDUAL SD — what run_predictions already computes and what Step 5's +/-1 SD band shows; then RMSE/SD is a BIAS ratio, RMSE >= SD always, and 'RMSE < SD' is unsatisfiable. (b) SD OF y_true — 'my error is smaller than the natural variation in the data', which is satisfiable, is probably what a reader means by it, and is ALGEBRAICALLY EQUAL to R2 > 0 since R2 = 1 - MSE/Var(y), so it restates a metric the table already carries; it is also computed nowhere, because run_predictions returns y-RANGES and not the target's SD, so (b) is a trainer or endpoint change on top of everything else. RECOMMENDATION IS (a): it is free, bias is not visible anywhere else in this wizard, and (b) would add a second column meaning what R2 already means. RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-08: (a) RESIDUAL SD. Matches this item's own recommendation exactly -- free, already computed inside run_predictions, bias is not visible anywhere else in this wizard. See userDecisions.

8. WHERE DOES PERMUTATION IMPORTANCE GO? The request reads 'under the Actual vs Predicted chart', which attaches naturally to the SCATTER (a chart has a slot relative to another chart) and less so to an importance table. Three readings: (a) beside the impurity and coefficient figures in MODEL-FLOW-019-T09's existing bottom-section table, where the disagreement between the two methods — the whole reason to compute permutation at all, per openDecision 5's option (c) — is visible in one glance; (b) as its own horizontal bar chart under the parity scatter, which matches the request literally and separates the two methods by a screen; (c) both, the table for comparison and a chart for scanning. RECOMMENDATION IS (a): the value is the comparison, and MODEL-FLOW-019-T09 already placed importance beneath the residual diagnostics with the method named beside the figures, the cumulative share, and the observations-per-feature line — a second placement would split one subject across two sections of one step.

9. WHICH SEED DRIVES THE PERMUTATION, AND EITHER ANSWER CONTRADICTS SOMETHING ALREADY SHIPPED. permutation_importance takes a random_state. (a) THE RUN'S OWN SEED — reproducible from the run row, which is what every other recorded figure in this system is, but it makes the seed determine the permutation figures of ridge, ols, svm and pls, and MODEL-FLOW-012's RunParamsPanel currently labels the seed 'Ignored by' exactly those four (SEED_CONSUMING_ALGORITHMS, 8 of 12, pinned by the live source guard MODEL-FLOW-014-T07 rebuilt against build_model). That label becomes false the moment permutation lands, and MODEL-FLOW-012-T05's own finding is that a control whose stated effect does not match its real one is the defect it exists to annotate away. (b) A FIXED CONSTANT independent of the run — keeps the label true and the figures reproducible, but introduces a second notion of randomness in a system that records exactly one seed per run. RECOMMENDATION IS (a) WITH THE LABEL AMENDED to say the seed is ignored by the ESTIMATOR for those four and is still used by permutation importance — the honesty-by-annotation shape MODEL-FLOW-012-T05 chose for lossFunction, rather than either a silent contradiction or a second seed.

7. IS THE HOLDOUT-ONLY NARROWING REOPENED? The user resolved MODEL-FLOW-019-T07 to holdout-only on 2026-09-07 ('criteria apply in Validate metric only') and the test-split threshold column was removed. But holdout_RMSE / test_RMSE is the ratio with the most teeth — this feature's own T04 detail says so ('a candidate at test 0.42 and holdout 0.81 is telling you the cleaning recipe flattered it') — and it needs BOTH sources by definition. Three readings: keep holdout-only and drop that pair; allow a cross-source RATIO as the single exception, since a ratio is not a test-split THRESHOLD and the earlier objection was about thresholds; or reopen the narrowing entirely. NOT decided here — recorded so a later reader sees the constraint was respected rather than forgotten. RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-08: CROSS-SOURCE RATIO AS THE SINGLE EXCEPTION. Criteria stay holdout-only as THRESHOLDS -- the 2026-09-07 decision is not reopened -- but holdout_X / test_X is admitted as a RATIO, since a ratio is not a test-split threshold and the earlier objection was about thresholds specifically. See userDecisions.

10. DOES THE USER PICK BOTH OPERANDS FREELY, OR PICK A PRE-ORIENTED PAIR AND ONLY THE OPERATOR? T12 is written to the LITERAL ask ('เลือก Operation เอง กับทำ label ที่จะเทียบเองได้') — both operands free, filtered to admissible combinations, canonicalised on commit. The alternative is a pair dropdown (offerableRatioPairs' own existing shape, pre-oriented) plus an operator, which makes AC38's canonicalisation unnecessary by construction and AC29/AC30/AC36 unenforceable-by-the-user rather than refused-after-the-fact, at the cost of a less direct reading of the request. Recorded rather than decided silently: if the free-operand picker proves fiddly in use, this is the fallback and it is strictly smaller. RESOLVED BY THE USER 2026-09-08: PAIR LIST + OPERATOR TOGGLE (the fallback this item itself recorded as 'strictly smaller'). Only 4 pairs x 2 operators = 8 criteria are reachable at all, so a pre-oriented pair dropdown plus a per-row </> toggle covers the whole space with the smallest change to shipped code. Canonicalisation (AC31/AC38) is still implemented and proven in lib/, but the UI itself cannot construct a mirror through this picker shape. See userDecisions.

tasks.title: Audit: which metric each Step 4 figure is currently reading, and whether any of them is a holdout figure
tasks.detail:
READ, DO NOT INFER — this ledger's own precedent is MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit finding five of seven tasks already correct, and -004/-005/-006/-012 each opening with an audit that changed their own scope.

Establish: (a) what getJobService's shaped candidate actually returns today — MODEL-FLOW-013-T06's note says metrics (test split) and trainMetrics (from -013-T04's train_* keys), and whether holdoutMetrics is in that shape at all; (b) what bestRunId is computed FROM — MODEL-FLOW-005 chose RMSE and this feature must know whether that RMSE is the test-split one (almost certainly, given finding 1) before it changes what the table ranks on; (c) whether any Step 4 or Step 5 surface currently displays a holdout number, and if so whether it is labelled as one; (d) the current state of MODEL-FLOW-016-T08's fix, since finding 2 makes every holdout claim here contingent on it.

If (b) comes back showing bestRunId is already holdout-derived where available, this feature's ranking half shrinks considerably.
tasks.result:
COMPLETED 2026-09-05 — READ, NOT INFERRED. Backend and client read from source; the holdout question settled against the LIVE dev DB (postgres softsensorproject-db-1 / soft_sensor_db) rather than against this feature's own recorded findings, which is what caught findings 1 and 2 being stale. No product code touched, no run launched, no Model row created; every DB statement was a SELECT.

(a) THE SHAPED CANDIDATE DOES NOT CARRY A HOLDOUT FIGURE AT ALL. model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts:771-812 (reconcileAndShape, used by getJobService:681) returns runId, algorithm, hyperparameters, phase, status, failureReason, metrics {r2,rmse,mae} (test split), trainMetrics {r2,rmse,mae} (read off the same run.metrics object's train_* keys, MODEL-FLOW-013-T04), lossHistoryKey, lossHistory, predictionsKey, cvFoldsKey, scoringContainerId. run.holdoutMetrics is never read and never projected; neither is splitSpec. The job envelope (:669-688) spreads the raw ModelCandidateJob row, so bestRunId/bestRmse/selectedRunId do reach the client. So the answer to this feature's own framing is: the candidate-job path has NOTHING to conflate today, and gains a holdout figure only when this mapper projects one — which is T02's work, not a repair.

(b) bestRunId IS TEST-SPLIT RMSE, NOT HOLDOUT. advanceJobForRun (same file, :315-530) calls extractRmse(run.metrics) (:86-90, :353) and compares rmse < job.bestRmse (:361-362). run.holdoutMetrics is never consulted. FAILED/CANCELED candidates return earlier (:328-351) and never enter the comparison; a null/non-finite rmse makes isBetter false, so a SUCCEEDED run with no metrics can never win — silently skipped, not errored. schema.prisma:1482-1486 documents the choice as deliberate and not configurable in this pass. T01's own stated escape hatch ('if bestRunId is already holdout-derived, the ranking half shrinks') does NOT apply: T03 is real work.

(c) A HOLDOUT NUMBER IS ALREADY ON SCREEN — IN ONE OF STEP 4'S TWO PATHS, AND IT IS ALREADY LABELLED. phase-4-model-selection.tsx:1149-1183 branches on mpCandidateJobIdAtom. Candidate-job path (CandidateComparison): the only per-candidate figure is candidate.metrics?.rmse under the label 'Test RMSE' (:291-299); Mode-B bars read trainMetrics.rmse / metrics.rmse (lib/run-selection.ts:70-75); Mode-A's second loss series is labelled 'Test split' (:106-131). No holdout anywhere. Standalone path (MODEL-FLOW-018's, source type ModelTrainingRunListItem which DOES carry holdoutMetrics, services/model-draft.ts:250): StandaloneRunRow (:738-925) already renders three labelled cases — 'Holdout RMSE' from run.holdoutMetrics.rmse when cvPhase==='scored', 'Test RMSE' from run.metrics.rmse when not CV, and 'Est. CV RMSE' from cv_rmse_mean ± cv_rmse_std otherwise; SingleRunSummary (:514-577, :1111-1113) says the same in prose. Step 5 also speaks of the holdout throughout (phase-5-evaluation.tsx:292,300,312,358,364,530,535 — 'Score against holdout', 'Holdout residual diagnostics'). CONCLUSION: the conflation risk is ASYMMETRIC. Half of Step 4 already names its source correctly; the table this feature adds must not lose that, and the candidate-job half must be given the same discipline as it gains holdout data.

(d) MODEL-FLOW-016-T08 HAS LANDED — findings 1 and 2 of this feature are STALE. T08 reads completed/100 with a live verification note dated 2026-09-01 (presign_run_object against a real validate_ready.parquet, 200 + working URL + row_count 1153). Measured on the dev DB 2026-09-05, read-only:
  SELECT count(*) total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE "holdoutMetrics" IS NOT NULL) with_holdout FROM "ModelTrainingRun";  -> 172 total, 90 with holdout.
  Per-day on the main dataset f7d2d259: 2026-08-27/28/31 = 0 of 43 with holdout; 2026-09-01 = 6 of 15; 2026-09-02 onward = 10/10, 35/39, 26/26, and ZERO SUCCEEDED runs without a holdout figure. That is T08 landing, dated by the data itself.
  So finding 1 ('holdoutMetrics IS NULL ON EVERY RUN OBSERVED') and finding 2 ('every claim here is contingent on T08 landing') were true when this feature was written and are false now. userDecision 2's stated premise — that a holdout-only table would be empty for every dataset — no longer holds. Both amended in place rather than deleted.

(e) A MIXED SOURCE SET IS NOT REACHABLE INSIDE ONE CANDIDATE JOB TODAY. Grouping the 106 job-owned runs by job: 19 jobs where every candidate has a holdout figure, 13 where none does, ZERO mixed. Holdout presence is a property of the DATASET, not of the candidate — 2 of the 4 datasets that have runs have holdout-bearing runs (f7d2d259: 77 of 133; 8a101c61: 13 of 17), the other two have none at all. Mixedness therefore arises only (i) across jobs/datasets, or (ii) from pre-2026-09-02 runs on a holdout-bearing dataset (56 such runs on f7d2d259). V01 and V03 must be built on fixtures or on those legacy rows; a freshly trained job will not produce a mixed set.

(f) THE HOLDOUT'S 'MISSING RATE' EXISTS AS COUNTS, NOT AS A RATE. Real stored shape, sampled from the two most recent holdout-bearing runs: {"r2": -2.5595, "mae": 0.1432, "rmse": 0.1687, "row_count": 1153, "dropped_unlabelled": 0, "dropped_bad_features": 0}. Built once in images/trainer/app/holdout.py:120-137 (score_holdout), shared by both the inline training-time path (pipelines/__init__.py:165-199) and score mode (pipelines/score.py:56-63). So AC2's 'missing rate' is DERIVABLE (dropped_* over row_count + dropped_*) but is not stored as a rate, and a legacy row may lack the keys entirely — which is exactly the honest-legacy-null case V02 already asks for. T02 must decide whether the rate is computed client-side or carried; it must not be invented from nothing.

(g) METRIC KEY NAMES ACROSS THE THREE SOURCES. r2/mae/rmse are spelled identically everywhere because one helper produces them (images/trainer/app/metrics.py:35-47, used by test, train and holdout alike). The COUNT keys are not shared: holdout has row_count/dropped_unlabelled/dropped_bad_features; the test-split dict has train_rows/test_rows/feature_count and no dropped_* equivalent. CV runs carry no bare rmse at all — cv_{r2,mae,rmse}_{mean,std}, n_splits, refit_rows, feature_count (pipelines/cv_expanding.py:89-98), confirmed against the 4 real CV runs in the DB. A ranker reading 'metrics.rmse' therefore reads null on every CV run by construction, which is finding 5's null-ordering problem arriving through a second door.

(h) NO TYPE ANYWHERE CARRIES A METRIC'S SOURCE. dto/model-run.authorized.dto.ts:8 defines MetricsSchema = z.record(z.string(), JsonScalar) and RunCompleteSchema (:237) and ScoreCompleteSchema (:245,:277) reuse it verbatim for both metrics and holdoutMetrics. Prisma has two untyped Json? columns (schema.prisma:1117, 1127) whose own doc comment says they are the SAME shape, 'Deliberately a SEPARATE column, never merged'. Client-side CandidateResult (services/model-draft.ts:497-535) has no holdoutMetrics field at all. So source is encoded today ONLY by which column a value sits in — T02's 'tagged shape rather than two parallel fields' is genuinely absent, not merely unlabelled.

(i) TWO THINGS T04 ASSUMED THAT ARE NOT TRUE. FIRST, the shared metric vocabulary is not rmse/r2/mae: lib/model-metrics.ts:14-16 defines METRIC_KEYS = ['r2','rmse','sd'] with METRIC_META labels R²/RMSE/SD (:44-66), state in store/model-pipeline.ts:212, last-metric guard at phase-5-evaluation.tsx:430-432. Step 5 has sd and NO mae; the run metrics have mae and NO sd (sd is residual-derived). Resolved by the user 2026-09-05 — see userDecisions. SECOND, there is no sortable table in this codebase: components/ui/table.tsx is the plain shadcn primitive, no @tanstack/react-table dependency, and no sort state/handler anywhere in apps/client (~20 consumers, none sortable). T04's 'sortable' is net-new UI work, not a prop on something existing.

(j) T05'S READ PATH ALREADY EXISTS. GET /authorized/model-drafts/:draftId/runs -> listDraftRunsService (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:600-615) returns every ModelTrainingRun on a draft as the raw row minus tokenHash — richer than the candidate shape, holdoutMetrics and splitSpec included. So the cross-job reading needed no new endpoint. Moot for now: the user resolved openDecision 1 to within-one-job on 2026-09-05.

(k) LAYOUT T06 MUST FIT (recorded now so -017 is not re-read later). CandidateGroups (phase-4-model-selection.tsx:434-489) renders, per phase group, a full-width CandidateOverlayChart above a grid sm:grid-cols-2 of CandidateRow cards; each card is header (status, algorithm, hyperparameters, Test RMSE) + CandidateBaseChart ('Does it track reality?') + inline CandidateChart ('Did it converge?') + Select. Groups are labelled 'Sweep' and 'Tuning {algorithm}' (:481-485). Two charts per card against a 20-candidate cap is what T06 says is not a table.

LEDGER REPAIR DONE UNDER THIS TASK, stated rather than smuggled: docs/feature_list.json DID NOT PARSE when this task was picked up. The MODEL-FLOW-019 block (uncommitted; HEAD's copy parses) carried 16 unescaped double quotes inside T04's detail string — around Test RMSE, Holdout RMSE, Validate RMSE, Test split, Validation, Validation residual diagnostics, Test-split residual diagnostics and Holdout — plus a trailing comma after the last acceptance_criteria entry. Both fixed, plus one missing space ('test 0.42,and holdout'). Until that fix no session could set a status or write a result programmatically, and every tool reading this ledger failed.

tasks.title: Every metric carries its source, in the type and not only in a label
tasks.detail:
A number's provenance must be inseparable from the number. Carry the source on the value — a tagged shape rather than two parallel fields a renderer could pick the wrong one of — so a UI cannot display a figure without also having in hand what it is a figure OF.

WHY THE TYPE AND NOT A COLUMN HEADER: a header is a promise the renderer makes; a tagged value is a fact the renderer cannot drop. MODEL-FLOW-004's renamed heading (finding 4) was exactly a header that had drifted from the data beneath it, and a header can drift again the next time the table is reworked.

Three sources exist and must stay distinguishable: the run's own TEST SPLIT, the dataset's raw validation HOLDOUT, and — once MODEL-FLOW-016 lands — a CV FOLD ESTIMATE, which is a mean with a spread rather than a single measurement.

A holdout figure travels WITH ITS MISSING RATE, per DS-LAKE-018-T05's own requirement that the rate be published beside every metric it produces. Under that feature's resolved no-imputation decision the holdout stays raw, so a hole reaches predict() and depresses the score with no trace of why (finding 3) — a holdout RMSE shown without its rate reads as a verdict on the model when it may be a verdict on the data. T01 NOTE, 2026-09-05: the rate is DERIVABLE BUT NOT STORED AS A RATE. Real holdoutMetrics carry counts — {r2, mae, rmse, row_count, dropped_unlabelled, dropped_bad_features} (built once in images/trainer/app/holdout.py:120-137, shared by the inline and score-mode paths). A rate needs row_count as its denominator, and a legacy row may lack the keys entirely, which is precisely V02's honest-legacy-null case. Also for T02: source is encoded today ONLY by which column a value sits in — MetricsSchema (dto/model-run.authorized.dto.ts:8) is reused verbatim for metrics and holdoutMetrics, Prisma has two untyped Json? columns (schema.prisma:1117,1127), and CandidateResult (services/model-draft.ts:497-535) has no holdoutMetrics field at all. The tagged shape this task asks for is genuinely absent, and the candidate-job mapper (reconcileAndShape, model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts:771-812) is where it has to start.
tasks.result:
COMPLETED 2026-09-05. The tagged shape exists end to end — backend mapper, wire type, client derivation — and the one shipped surface that already made this distinction by hand now reads it from the type instead. No rendered string changed.

WHAT WAS BUILT.
1. BACKEND, model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts: reconcileAndShape now emits `sourcedMetrics` (a discriminated union, tagged on `source`) and `holdoutAbsence` per candidate. Three sources: 'test-split' {r2,rmse,mae}; 'holdout' {r2,rmse,mae,rowCount,droppedUnlabelled,droppedBadFeatures}; 'cv-fold-estimate' {nSplits,mean,std} — the CV entry deliberately has NO bare rmse/r2/mae field, because a real CV run's metrics have none either (T01 finding (g)) and a fold mean wearing a measurement's name is the exact conflation this feature exists to stop. Built by two new private helpers (sourcedMetricsFor / holdoutAbsenceFor) beside the existing extractRmse, not a new lib module — one caller, so the codebase's own 2-callers dedup threshold is not met.
2. WHY NOT JUST ADD `holdoutMetrics` BESIDE `metrics`/`trainMetrics` — the obvious smaller change, rejected on this task's own wording ('a tagged shape rather than two parallel fields a renderer could pick the wrong one of'). A third parallel field would have left the wire untagged and pushed provenance back into whatever the renderer chose to do, which is the failure mode MODEL-FLOW-004's renamed heading already demonstrated. `metrics`/`trainMetrics` are UNCHANGED and still feed -013-T07's charts and -017's cards; the tagged view is additive.
3. THE DATASET-LEVEL FACT, and its cost. holdoutAbsence distinguishes 'no-dataset-holdout' (this dataset never had one — the common case, not an error) from 'not-scored-yet' (a CV run awaiting its own scoring phase) from 'not-recorded' (the dataset HAS a holdout and this run still carries no figure: a pre-2026-09-01 run or a failed replay — the one that hides a real defect if it renders blank). The first is not answerable from a run row, so reconcileAndShape resolves it via the EXISTING findHoldoutArtifact (lib/holdout-artifact.ts, MODEL-FLOW-016-T08's own helper) — ONE lookup per job read, not per candidate (every candidate shares goldArtifactId by -013-T03's design), skipped entirely unless some SUCCEEDED candidate actually lacks a figure, and soft-failing to null (which reads as 'not-recorded', never as a guess) the same way the loss-history read already does. Pinned by its own test asserting the lookup is NOT made when every candidate already has a holdout figure.
4. CLIENT, new pure module lib/metric-source.ts (the lib/run-selection.ts pattern — no React, no IO, colocated .test.ts): the same union as a client type, plus sourcedMetricsOf(run) for RAW run rows (the standalone path reads ModelTrainingRunListItem, not CandidateResult, so the builder takes a structural shape both satisfy), holdoutAbsenceOf(run, datasetHasHoldout), headlineMetricOf, rmseOf, and METRIC_SOURCE_LABELS. CandidateResult (services/model-draft.ts) gained `sourcedMetrics` and `holdoutAbsence`, importing the types from that module — types flow lib -> services, never back, so no cycle.
5. cvScoringPhaseOf MOVED from hooks/model/use-draft-run-evaluation.ts into lib/metric-source.ts and re-exported from its old home. It decides which SOURCE a run's headline figure has, which is this module's whole subject, and a pure derivation belongs in lib/ per this codebase's own split. Every existing import path (phase-5-evaluation, phase-6-deploy, phase-4-model-selection, and the two suites that importOriginal it) is untouched. Its parameter narrowed from DraftRunSummary to the three signals it actually reads, which meant the two hand-built DraftRunSummary literals in phase-4 could be deleted and the run row passed whole.
6. StandaloneRunRow (phase-4-model-selection.tsx) refactored to derive its figure from the tagged entries rather than reaching into run.holdoutMetrics/run.metrics itself — the proof the type works, and now the number and the label beneath it cannot come from different places. BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BY CONSTRUCTION and checked as such: the phase still picks the source (scored -> holdout, not-cv -> test split, otherwise the fold estimate) and METRIC_SOURCE_LABELS reproduces the exact shipped strings 'Holdout RMSE' / 'Test RMSE' / 'Est. CV RMSE'. Deliberately NOT headlineMetricOf, which prefers a holdout wherever one exists — correct for a table cell that says what it is, wrong here, since an ordinary run now usually HAS a holdout figure (90 of 172 runs, T01) and this shipped column would have silently relabelled itself.

WHAT THIS TASK DID NOT DO, stated rather than implied: no missing RATE is computed anywhere. The counts travel with the value and the rate is a render-time division — a rate needs a denominator a legacy row may not have, and inventing 0% is exactly the fabrication V02 asks to be ruled out. Rendering the three absence reasons, the rate, and the second column is T04's; T02 only guarantees the data cannot arrive without them.

VERIFIED. Backend: pnpm --filter backend check-types -> the same 5 pre-existing unrelated errors (auth/dataset-draft specs), zero new; jest 546 tests, 537 passing, the 9 failures being the identical pre-existing suite baseline (auth/plan/nodes/workspace/model-run controllers), zero new; model-candidate-job's own suite 34 -> 38 tests, all green. Client: pnpm --filter client check-types -> 7 pre-existing unrelated errors (dataset-compare-modal, alerts/model-evaluation/overview-tree specs), zero new; new lib/metric-source.test.ts 17 tests green; all 8 pipeline suites green (89 tests) including evaluation-contract, phase-3-evaluation and phase-6-deploy, which is what proves the cvScoringPhaseOf move broke no caller. Full client vitest: 866 passing / 25 failing across 10 files — every failing file is unrelated to this work (plants, canvas, plans, data-studio step 6, and the two training-config seed suites, whose failures are all 'Unable to find a label with the text of: /seed/i' from other uncommitted work in this tree, not from anything this task touched). The 018-era baseline of 9 files / 23 tests is stale: this tree has gained the uncommitted monitoring work since it was written.

NEW TESTS (21). Backend, 4: a plain candidate and a scored CV candidate in ONE set carrying DIFFERENT sources (the case a uniformly-sourced set could never distinguish from a table that tags nothing); the holdout entry carrying its three counts; the CV entry asserted NOT to have an `rmse` property; all three absence reasons produced from real row shapes; a FAILED candidate claiming nothing at all; and the skipped-lookup case. Client, 17: the same source rules plus legacy-null counts (a holdout figure with no count keys reads null, never 0), non-finite/non-numeric values narrowing to null rather than passing through, the four cvScoringPhaseOf phases, and the label strings asserted to equal the shipped column's exact wording.

TWO CHECKS AN ADVISOR PASS ASKED FOR BEFORE CLOSING, both answered rather than assumed. (1) THE SECOND CALLER: reconcileAndShape is shared with ModelRetrainAuthorizedService.getRetrainJobService (model-retrain.authorized.service.ts:385), which passes a MODEL-owned job — the same shape that already shipped a real 'drafts/null/runs/...' bug for lossHistoryKey once. That bug class does not apply here: ModelCandidateJob.goldArtifactId is NON-NULLABLE (schema.prisma:1459) and a retrain job fills it from incumbent.goldArtifactId (ModelVersion, :1241, itself pinned off the source run row), so it is a real DatasetArtifact id resolved by findHoldoutArtifact exactly as on the draft path — never a key rebuilt from an owner id. There is also no model-retrain.authorized.service.spec.ts at all, which is why the unchanged jest baseline could not have told us anything about that path either way — stated so a future reader does not mistake the green run for coverage it is not. (2) THE VALUE, NOT ONLY THE LABEL, IS UNCHANGED IN StandaloneRunRow: reasoned through the null cases rather than inferred from the passing suites. Old code read run.holdoutMetrics.rmse / run.metrics.rmse / cv_rmse_mean directly and printed an em dash when the number was not a finite number; new code prints an em dash when the tagged entry is absent OR its rmse is null, and sourcedMetricsOf emits the holdout entry exactly when run.holdoutMetrics is truthy and narrows every field with the same typeof/isFinite test. holdoutMetrics === {} yields an entry with rmse null -> em dash, as before; a 'scored' CV run with null holdoutMetrics (cvScoringPhaseOf keys 'scored' off predictionsKey, not the figure) yields no holdout entry -> em dash, as before. The two paths agree on every input, including the ones no test constructs.

tasks.title: Rank on the holdout where it exists, and say plainly when it does not
tasks.detail:
Per userDecisions, and constrained by finding 1: prefer the holdout figure for ordering; fall back to the test split; state which was used FOR THE ORDERING ITSELF, not only per cell. A user reading a ranked list is reading a claim about ordering, and that claim changes meaning entirely depending on which metric produced it.

DEFINE WHERE A MISSING METRIC SORTS, explicitly (finding 5). A FAILED candidate has no metrics; a candidate still running has none yet; a run whose holdout replay was skipped has no holdout figure. Sorting nulls quietly to the bottom is a decision, not a default — make it a stated one, and keep those rows visible with their reason rather than filtering them out, the rule MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 already established for FAILED candidates.

DO NOT MIX SOURCES WITHIN ONE ORDERING. Ranking a holdout-scored candidate against a test-scored one puts two incomparable numbers in one column and the ordering means nothing. Either rank within a source and group, or rank on the source every row shares — never sort a mixed column and present the result as a ranking.

RMSE STAYS THE DEFAULT, minimised. MODEL-FLOW-005 chose it over R² after a real observed run scored r2 = -1,110,858 while its rmse stayed a readable, comparable number; that reasoning is unchanged and this task does not reopen it.
tasks.result:
COMPLETED 2026-09-05. The ordering RULE, as a pure module with no consumer yet — T04's table is what renders it, and this ledger keeps the two separate. New file apps/client/lib/metric-ranking.ts (the lib/run-selection.ts pattern: no React, no IO, colocated .test.ts), generic over the row type so a caller ranks ONE phase group at a time without this module ever learning what a phase is (MODEL-FLOW-013-T11's grouping survives by construction, not by a special case).

THE ORDERING'S OWN SOURCE IS RETURNED, NOT ONLY THE CELLS'. rankCandidates() returns `orderingSource` ('holdout' | 'test-split' | 'cv-fold-estimate' | null) plus `fallbackReason`, because a ranked list is a claim about ordering and that claim changes meaning entirely with the metric behind it. Preference order: holdout (the only figure no fit ever saw), then the run's own test split, then a fold ESTIMATE last — an estimate of a configuration is the weakest of the three claims and is used only when it is all a set has.

THE FALLBACK NAMES WHETHER IT IS HONEST OR COVERING FOR A DEFECT — an addition beyond AC3's wording, made because T02's holdoutAbsence now makes it knowable. 'no-dataset-holdout' is an honest fallback: those datasets never had a holdout and never will produce one. 'holdout-not-recorded' is NOT: the dataset HAS one and some row still lacks its figure (a run older than the 2026-09-01 replay fix, or a failed replay), so ranking quietly on the test split would hide exactly what this feature's finding 2 was written about. 'holdout-not-scored-yet' sits between them (a CV run awaiting its scoring phase — a pending action, not a defect). Loudest wins where a set mixes them.

NEVER SORTS A MIXED COLUMN, enforced rather than documented. The ordering runs on the source EVERY eligible row shares or it does not run at all: a set with no such source comes back with orderingSource null and every row marked 'no-shared-source', in INPUT order, ranked by nothing. The case that makes this real is not hypothetical — one CV run awaiting scoring (fold estimate only) beside one plain run (test split only) is a set whose numbers cannot be ordered against each other at all, and sorting 0.22 against 0.40 there would present an estimate of a configuration and a measurement of a model as if one beat the other. A single holdout-scored row likewise cannot drag the whole set onto the holdout — pinned by its own test.

WHERE A MISSING METRIC SORTS IS STATED, NOT DEFAULTED. Five distinct reasons, each a different thing to tell the reader: 'no-run' (PENDING, never launched), 'not-finished' (QUEUED/RUNNING — it will have a figure later), 'failed' (FAILED/CANCELED — it never will), 'missing-metric' (terminal and successful, but no value in the ordering's source), 'no-shared-source' (nothing could be ordered at all). Unranked rows are KEPT, placed after the ranked ones in input order, each carrying its reason — never filtered out, the rule MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 already established for FAILED candidates. A non-terminal or failed row also cannot change WHICH source the set is ranked on: eligibility is decided by status first, so one FAILED candidate with no metrics does not collapse a holdout-ranked set onto the test split.

RMSE STAYS THE DEFAULT, MINIMISED, and this task did not reopen MODEL-FLOW-005's rmse-over-r2 choice. RANK_DIRECTION is {rmse:'min', mae:'min', r2:'max'} — r2 stays rankable rather than being refused, and the pathological real value that feature recorded (r2 = -1,110,858) is used as a fixture proving such a row sorts LAST under a max ordering rather than crashing or being dropped. A row with no value for the CHOSEN metric never orders as 0: it makes its source ineligible for the whole set, which is the refusal rather than a silent zero.

TIES SHARE A RANK (1, 1, 3 — competition style), input order preserved among them. Two models that scored the same did not place differently, and numbering them 1 and 2 would assert a winner the metric never chose. Pinned by a test with two identical rmse values, since a tie rule asserted only by the implementation is not a rule.

bestRunId IS UNTOUCHED, stated because a reader seeing 'rank on the holdout' will reasonably ask whether the winner changed. It did not: bestRunId is still computed server-side off the test-split rmse in advanceJobForRun (model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts:86-90, :353-362), and nothing in this task writes to it or reads it. This module orders a DISPLAY. The metric's own answer and the table's order are now two different things, which is precisely why T04's detail keeps the user's override visible.

ONE SMALL CHANGE IN metric-source.ts: rmseOf now delegates to a new metricValueOf(metric, key) so ranking can read r2/mae/rmse out of any source through one narrowing (a CV estimate answers from its own `mean`, the only number of that shape it has). rmseOf's behaviour is unchanged; its callers are untouched.

VERIFIED. New lib/metric-ranking.test.ts: 17 tests green (counted, not inferred), covering each rule above by the case that distinguishes it from a weaker implementation (holdout ordering that reverses the test-split order; both fallback reasons; the mixed-source refusal; all five unranked reasons with their placement; the tie; r2's direction). Full lib pair (ranking + source) 34 tests green.

ONE BUG OF MY OWN, FOUND BY AN ADVISOR PASS AFTER THE FIRST GREEN RUN AND FIXED WITH ITS OWN REGRESSION TEST: fallbackReason was computed over ALL rows when nothing ranked, so a refused (no-shared-source) set could come back with orderingSource null AND fallbackReason 'holdout-not-recorded' — reading as 'ranked on the test split because of a defect' about a set that was not ranked at all. There is no fallback without an ordering to fall back from. Now null whenever orderingSource is null, and the mixed-source fixture that would have caught it (both rows carrying holdoutAbsence) is a test rather than a note — the original mixed-source case set no absence at all, which is exactly why it passed over the bug. All 8 pipeline suites plus run-selection re-run after the metric-source edit: 9 files, 99 tests, green. pnpm --filter client check-types: 7 pre-existing unrelated errors, zero new, none in any file this task touched. Backend untouched by T03 — no endpoint, no DTO, no schema change; the ranking is a client-side derivation over data T02 already ships.

tasks.title: The table: sortable, with user-chosen columns
tasks.detail:
SD IS NOT A TABLE COLUMN. Residual standard deviation is a spread, not an error figure — it answers "how scattered are the residuals" rather than "how wrong is this model", so it does not rank and a threshold on it does not read as an acceptance criterion. It stays where it belongs: as the ±1 SD band on Evaluation's own charts (MODEL-FLOW-004's ActualVsPredictedChart and ResidualChart both take it and both document what the band means), and in MODEL-FLOW-017's per-candidate base chart. Removed from the ranked table's column set, and from METRIC_KEYS as far as this table's picker is concerned — which is why T07's threshold picker binds to rmse/r2/mae and not to whatever METRIC_KEYS happens to hold. BOTH SOURCES SHOW BY DEFAULT, not behind the picker. The DIFFERENCE between them is the most informative thing on this screen — a candidate at test 0.42 and holdout 0.81 is telling you the cleaning recipe flattered it — and hiding either half behind a toggle means a reader has to already suspect that in order to go looking for it. The picker governs WHICH METRICS (rmse, r2, mae) are shown, not which SOURCE. COLUMN NAMES ARE "Test RMSE" AND "Holdout RMSE", NOT "Validate RMSE". This codebase already uses `validate` for the dataset QUALITY GATE — /validate validation_report.json, DS-LAKE-019's blocking-vs-advisory checks — which has nothing to do with a model's score, and MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 separately requires a loss chart's second series be labelled "Test split" and never "Validation" for the same reason. MODEL-FLOW-004 already paid for this exact collision, renaming a shipped heading from "Validation residual diagnostics" to "Test-split residual diagnostics" one feature after it shipped. "Holdout" has one meaning in this system — the rows DS-LAKE-018 splits off at BRONZE — and is the word every schema field, column and comment already uses for them. AN ABSENT HOLDOUT FIGURE IS THREE DIFFERENT FACTS AND MUST READ AS THREE. The dataset has no holdout at all (the common case per finding 1, and not an error); the holdout exists but its replay failed (which hides a real defect if it renders as a blank); or the run has not been scored yet (MODEL-FLOW-016's own flow, where the next action is to trigger scoring). Collapsing all three to an em-dash tells a reader nothing about which situation they are in or what to do next.One row per candidate: algorithm, hyperparameters, status, and the metric columns the user selected. Sortable by any metric column.

REUSE THE COLUMN-PICKER VOCABULARY THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Step 5 has a Metrics dropdown driven by METRIC_KEYS/METRIC_META and mpSelectedMetricsAtom, including the guard that the last remaining metric cannot be deselected. A second picker with its own state and its own wording, one step away from the first, is how two surfaces start disagreeing about what a metric is called.

A HOLDOUT AND A TEST FIGURE FOR THE SAME METRIC ARE SEPARATE COLUMNS, never one column with a footnote. They are different claims (finding 3) and putting them in one cell would make the sort ambiguous the moment a set mixes both.

Keep MODEL-FLOW-013-T11's phase grouping ('Sweep' / 'Tuning <winner>') intact — a tuning phase's candidates share one algorithm and are directly comparable in a way the sweep phase's are not, and flattening that into one sorted list would lose it. Sorting within a group is the safe default; sorting across groups needs the comparability judgement openDecisions defers.

Selection stays where MODEL-FLOW-013-T08 put it: the user picks a row, selectedRunId records it, bestRunId still records what the metric chose. A ranked table makes the metric's answer more prominent, which is a reason to keep the override visible, not less. T01 NOTE, 2026-09-05 — TWO ASSUMPTIONS IN THIS TASK ARE WRONG, BOTH NOW RESOLVED OR PRICED. (1) The shared picker vocabulary is r2/rmse/sd, not rmse/r2/mae: Step 5 has sd and no mae, the run metrics have mae and no sd. User resolved 2026-09-05 to widen METRIC_KEYS/METRIC_META to r2/rmse/mae/sd and have Step 4 read that same list — see userDecisions. (2) There is no sortable table in this codebase: components/ui/table.tsx is the plain shadcn primitive, there is no @tanstack/react-table dependency, and no sort state or handler exists anywhere in apps/client (~20 consumers of the primitive, none sortable). 'Sortable' here is net-new UI. Also: half of Step 4 already does this task's job correctly — StandaloneRunRow (phase-4-model-selection.tsx:738-925) already labels 'Holdout RMSE' / 'Test RMSE' / 'Est. CV RMSE' per run, while the candidate-job path shows only 'Test RMSE' (:291-299) and has no holdout data to show until T02 projects it. The table must inherit the standalone path's labelling rather than replace it.
tasks.result:
COMPLETED 2026-09-05. Scoped to the CANDIDATE-JOB comparison (CandidateComparison/CandidateGroups in phase-4-model-selection.tsx) — the sweep/tune surface T01's audit and T03's ranking work are grounded on, where every row shares one artifact/target/split by construction (MODEL-FLOW-013-T03). The STANDALONE cross-run table (StandaloneComparison/StandaloneRunRow, MODEL-FLOW-018) is untouched: it already carries its own well-tested targetY grouping and comparability notes, is a materially different feature, and none of this task's findings were about it — confirmed by the full 43-test suite for this file passing with only ONE pre-existing assertion needing re-expression (see below), not a rewrite.

THE TABLE. A genuine sortable <table> (components/ui/table.tsx primitive, previously unused for sorting anywhere in this codebase — T01 confirmed this) replaces the per-candidate card grid. Two-row header: a metric group cell (colSpan 2, click-to-sort) over Test/Holdout sub-columns — never one column with a footnote (finding 3). One row per candidate: rank, algorithm + hyperparameters, status + failure reason, then Test/Holdout cells for every metric the picker has selected. Both source columns render BY DEFAULT, never behind a toggle (AC10) — the picker governs which METRICS show (rmse/r2/mae/sd), never which source.

RANKING IS WIRED IN, NOT REBUILT. rankCandidates (T03) runs PER PHASE GROUP (openDecisions item 1's resolution: within one job; MODEL-FLOW-013-T11's Sweep/Tuning split survives because each group gets its own table and its own ranking call — confirmed by the pre-existing 'renders both groups' test passing unchanged). rankingSummaryText (new, T03's own module) renders as one sentence above each table — e.g. 'Ranked by Holdout RMSE.' or 'Ranked by Test RMSE — this dataset has no validation holdout.' — satisfying AC3's 'states which was used for the ordering' literally, not per-cell. Clicking a metric's group header changes sortMetric; sd renders as a plain non-clickable label (RankMetricKey excludes it — there is nothing to sort BY, T02's own finding that sd is never in metrics/holdoutMetrics/a CV aggregate), with a title explaining why, never a dead click.

EVERY FIGURE CARRIES ITS SOURCE, LITERALLY THROUGH THE TYPE (AC1). MetricSourceCell takes a SourcedMetrics | null and reads it via T02's own metricValueOf — a cell cannot render a number without the tagged value it came from being what produced it. A HOLDOUT FIGURE NEVER APPEARS WITHOUT ITS MISSING RATE (AC2): computed from droppedUnlabelled + droppedBadFeatures over rowCount, rendered as a second line under the value; a legacy holdout missing the counts reads 'missing rate not recorded', never a fabricated 0% (MODEL-FLOW-010-T06's honest-legacy-null pattern, same discipline T02 already built into the type). AN ABSENT HOLDOUT FIGURE READS AS ONE OF THREE STATED FACTS (AC11) via T02's own holdoutAbsence: 'No holdout' / 'Awaiting scoring' / 'Not recorded' — never a blank em dash.

NEVER MIXES SOURCES UNDER ONE HEADER (finding 3, AC4). A candidate whose only non-holdout source is a CV fold estimate (structurally possible per the type, UNREACHABLE with real data today — CreateCandidateJobSchema has no nSplits field, confirmed zero job-owned CV runs in the dev DB) reads 'N/A — cross-validation' under the Test header rather than silently showing the fold mean there — the exact merge this feature exists to prevent, kept honest for a case that cannot happen today rather than assumed impossible forever.

A CANDIDATE WITH NO METRIC KEEPS ITS ROW (AC5), via T03's ranking module unchanged: FAILED/PENDING/RUNNING candidates sort to the bottom with a stated reason in the rank cell's title ('Did not finish' / 'Not launched yet' / 'Still running'), never dropped, never a fabricated number — proven by the pre-existing 'a FAILED one stays listed' test passing.

THE PICKER SHARES STEP 5's VOCABULARY AND ITS OWN STATE (AC6), not a lookalike. METRIC_KEYS/METRIC_META widened this task (r2/rmse/sd -> r2/rmse/mae/sd, the user's own resolved decision from T03) and mpSelectedMetricsAtom — the SAME jotai atom Step 5 reads and writes — is reused directly, so selecting metrics on one step affects the other; that is the literal reading of 'shares its vocabulary... rather than declaring a second one.' The cannot-deselect-the-last-metric guard is the identical component logic (toggleMetricSelection, extracted to lib/model-metrics.ts and now used by BOTH Step 4 and Step 5, replacing Step 5's own inline copy — one rule, not two that could drift).

SELECTION IS UNCHANGED (AC8). handleSelect still calls the same modelDraftCandidateJobService.select(draftId, jobId, runId); bestRunId is never read or written by anything in this task — it stays exactly what advanceJobForRun computed from the test-split rmse (T01's audit). The Select button and Selected badge are in the table now, not a card, but the same pre-existing tests for both ('marks the resolved winner...', 'calls select and refetches...') pass unchanged.

CHARTS ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT UNRECONCILED WITH T06, stated rather than smuggled. MODEL-FLOW-017's per-candidate base + diagnostic charts move OUT of the table row into a new CandidateChartList below it, one card per SUCCEEDED candidate, same order the table currently ranks them — so nothing regresses (the pre-existing MODEL-FLOW-017-V01/V04 chart tests pass unchanged) without this task picking one of T06's three listed layouts for it. T06's own detail names that as its job precisely because -017 had already shipped when this feature was picked up; building the reconciliation here would have made T06 a rubber stamp.

WIDENING METRIC_KEYS TOUCHED STEP 5, MEASURED SAFE FIRST. Added mae to ModelMetrics/fitFromRun/requireMetric's key union (hooks/model/use-draft-run-evaluation.ts) — verified against the live dev DB before making it a REQUIRED field: SELECT count(*) FROM "ModelTrainingRun" WHERE metrics ? 'rmse' AND NOT (metrics ? 'mae') and the same for holdoutMetrics both return 0. Five fixtures in phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx needed mae added (a runtime failure, not a type error — the test's own fit is typed unknown) or METRIC_META['mae'].format(undefined) would have thrown; fixed via one shared METRICS.mae constant rather than five separate literals.

ONE PRE-EXISTING ASSERTION RE-EXPRESSED, not deleted: 'Ridge Regression' now renders twice for a SUCCEEDED candidate (once in the table row, once as its chart card's own header) where it previously rendered once — getByText became getAllByText(...).length > 0, and the FAILED candidate's own single-occurrence assertion ('Support Vector Machine') was left as getByText, which is itself the proof its chart card is correctly absent.

tasks.title: Top-10 ranking — decide the scope before building the query
tasks.detail:
BLOCKED ON openDecisions ITEM 1, and stated as blocked rather than built to the narrower reading: within one job, 'top 10' is usually the whole job sorted (finding 6), which is T04 and needs nothing further. Across every run on the draft, it is a different query, a different endpoint and a real comparability problem.

IF CROSS-JOB IS CHOSEN: two runs may have trained against different artifacts, targets or split ratios, and their RMSEs are then not comparable at all. The table must surface what differs and refuse to rank rows that are not comparable, rather than sorting them together and letting adjacency imply they can be compared. MODEL-FLOW-013-T03 kept targetY, goldArtifactId and trainTestSplit on the JOB root precisely because varying them makes a comparison meaningless — that reasoning does not stop applying when the comparison spans jobs, it just stops being enforced by the schema.

The read path may already exist: modelDraftRunService.list(draftId) was added by MODEL-FLOW-012-T03 and returns every run on a draft. Check before building an endpoint (T01). T01 ANSWER + RESOLUTION, 2026-09-05: the read path DOES already exist — GET /authorized/model-drafts/:draftId/runs -> listDraftRunsService (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:600-615) returns every run on a draft as the raw row minus tokenHash, holdoutMetrics and splitSpec included. It is moot for now: the user resolved openDecisions item 1 to WITHIN ONE CANDIDATE JOB on 2026-09-05, so this task's work folds into T04 (a top-10 inside a 20-candidate cap is the job sorted) and no second query or endpoint is built. Left pending rather than completed because T04 is what discharges it; the cross-job reading survives as a possible follow-up feature with the comparability rule stated above. PROGRESS ARITHMETIC, STATED SO THE NEXT READER IS NOT LEFT GUESSING: this task still COUNTS toward the feature's six-task denominator and stays pending, but it will be discharged BY T04 rather than by work of its own — so the feature reaches 100 with five tasks implemented and this one closed as folded in, not with a sixth build.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-05 — DISCHARGED BY T04, NOT BUILT SEPARATELY. openDecisions item 1 was resolved by the user 2026-09-05 to WITHIN ONE CANDIDATE JOB (see userDecisions), which is exactly the scope T04 built: rankCandidates runs per phase group of one job, never across jobs. A top-10 within a 20-candidate cap (CreateCandidateJobSchema's own bound) is, per finding 6, the whole job sorted — which is what the table now shows, with a visible rank number on every row. The cross-job reading this task's own detail describes (a different query, a different endpoint, real comparability judgement) was NOT built — it is recorded as a possible follow-up feature, not deferred work silently left inside this one. If it is ever picked up, listDraftRunsService (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:600-615, confirmed in T01's audit) already returns every run on a draft with holdoutMetrics and splitSpec included, so it needs no new endpoint, only the comparability rule this task's own detail already states.

tasks.title: Acceptance criteria as advisory Core Config input, annotating the table
tasks.detail:
COMPARATOR IS DERIVED FROM THE METRIC, NOT CHOSEN. METRIC_META already encodes direction implicitly — its `accent` function knows a low RMSE is good and a high R² is — so the form shows "RMSE ≤ [ ]" and "R² ≥ [ ]" and offers no direction picker. Free choice would let a user set `rmse > 0.12`, which passes every model worse than the threshold: a criterion that reads as strict and admits everything, which is the failure shape with no symptom this ledger keeps naming.  THRESHOLDS ARE VIEW STATE, NOT DRAFT STATE. Held in a jotai atom beside mpSelectedMetricsAtom, which is what Step 5's own metric picker already uses — NOT a new ModelDraft column. This keeps finding 6 true as written ("the step holds one piece of server state and only one: selectedRunId") rather than requiring it be amended, and it is the honest classification: a threshold is how a user chooses to read a set, not a fact about what produced it. Cost,stated: thresholds do not survive a page reload. If they should, that is apersistence decision with a place to record it, not a field to add by reflex. ONLY DISPLAYED METRICS TAKE A THRESHOLD. mae rides in the served payloadundisplayed (T03's own note) and sd is a residual spread rather than an errorfigure — offering a threshold on a number the table does not show, or on onewhose direction is not obvious, invites a criterion the user cannot then seebeing evaluated. Bound the picker to the same METRIC_KEYS the columns comefrom. A user sets thresholds per metric before training — RMSE below some value, R² above another — and every candidate in the table is marked against them. FOUR readings of 'criteria' were possible and this is the one that ships; the other three are recorded here so a later reader can see they were considered rather than missed.

ADVISORY, NEVER BLOCKING. DS-LAKE-019 moved this codebase's statistical checks from blocking to advisory as an entire feature, on reasoning that transfers unchanged: a chronological split on plant data SHOULD shift, and a threshold right for one tag is wrong for the next. An RMSE ceiling is a judgement about whether a fit is fit for purpose, which is the engineer's to make against their own process knowledge — not a constant's. So a failing candidate is MARKED, never hidden, never barred from selection, and never blocks Save Model.

NOT A FILTER, for the reason MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 already established: a FAILED candidate keeps its row and its reason rather than disappearing, because a set that silently shrinks tells the user nothing about what was tried. A candidate that missed a threshold is the same case — the miss is the information.

NOT AN EARLY STOP either. Stopping a sweep once something passes leaves the remaining candidates unrun, and MODEL-FLOW-013-T03 kept targetY, goldArtifactId and trainTestSplit on the job root specifically so every candidate in a set is comparable. A partially-run set is not a comparison, and the ranking T03 builds would then order an arbitrary subset.

EVERY THRESHOLD NAMES ITS SOURCE, and this is the part a bare number gets wrong. 'RMSE < 0.12' is ambiguous: test-split and holdout figures for one model routinely differ by a factor (a candidate at test 0.42 and holdout 0.81 is the shape T03's own finding describes), so a threshold not bound to a source is compared against whichever number happened to be at hand. Reuse T02's tagged-value shape rather than declaring a second convention — a threshold carries {metric, comparator, value, source} and is evaluated only against a figure of that source.

A THRESHOLD WHOSE SOURCE IS ABSENT IS 'not evaluated', NOT 'failed'. holdoutMetrics is null on every run this system has produced (T03's own finding 1), so a holdout-sourced threshold has nothing to test against today. Marking those candidates as failing would report a missing measurement as a bad model — the inverse of the error, and equally wrong. This is the fourth absent-holdout state and joins the three T04 already distinguishes.

INSIDE APPLY, not on change: MODEL-FLOW-014-T08 makes Core Config commit on Apply, and a threshold re-evaluating per keystroke would repaint the table while the user is still typing the number.

tasks.title: One advance control, a count-only run footer, and one Model Selection layout for every training shape
tasks.detail:
Three changes the user resolved 2026-09-07, recorded as one task because they are one screen's worth of consequence and splitting them would let each half assume the other did the work.

(1) THE WIZARD SHELL OWNS THE MOVE. Remove RunParamsPanel's footer CTA and, with it, its raw setCurrentStep/setHighestUnlocked setters. The shell's own forward button becomes the single control. Then canAdvance(3) is the only gate and it must be satisfiable by the draft HAVING a terminal run — never by the compare set, which is client-only, usually empty, and would make the button unreachable in the default view. Audit every remaining setCurrentStep call inside a Step 3 or Step 4 panel before deleting any of them; openDecisions names the one (Score in Evaluation) that is not obviously in scope.

(2) THE FOOTER REPORTS A COUNT. No picker, no Select, no destination promise — the number of runs ticked, and the empty-set-means-all rule stated in words rather than left to be inferred from an unticked list. Nothing in Step 3 writes ModelDraft.selectedRunId after this; finding 6 stays true as written for a different reason than before (Step 3 now holds NO server state, and Step 4's Select is the single writer).

(3) THE COMPARE SET MUST SURVIVE THE STEP BOUNDARY, which is the part that silently does not work if it is missed. The set is local useState in RunParamsPanel today; Step 4 cannot see it. Lift it to a jotai atom beside mpSelectedMetricsAtom — the same view-state-not-draft-state classification T07's thresholds already use, for the same reason: it is how a user chooses to read a set, not a fact about what produced it. Step 4 must implement empty-means-all ITSELF; a Step 4 that resolves only from selectedRunId renders an empty screen the moment the footer says it is comparing all seven.

(4) ONE LAYOUT, AND THE OVERLAY CHART EVERYWHERE. Delete StandaloneRunRow and RUN_STATUS_META; map a run row to the candidate shape and render every path through CandidateOverlayChart + CandidateTable, one pair per phase group (candidate-job path) or per targetY group (standalone path). groupByTarget is NOT optional here and matters more after the change than before: CandidateTable RANKS its rows, and one table spanning two targets would order two different targets' RMSEs in a single column — the exact category error grouping-by-target exists to catch, now reachable by layout rather than by query. rankCandidates already refuses to rank across mixed metric sources on its own ('no-shared-source'), so a test-split figure is never ordered against a fold-mean estimate inside a group.

NEVER FAKE A FIELD THE RUN ROW CANNOT ANSWER. The mapper's holdoutAbsence must never report 'no-dataset-holdout' — that is a DATASET property, resolved server-side by reconcileAndShape via findHoldoutArtifact (T02), and a run row has no access to it. 'not-recorded' is the honest fallback, and it is also the one absence reason that hides a real defect, so it must not be reached by a guess. If the CandidateResult type demands a field the run row has no source for, widen the type to optional rather than passing a zero or an empty array.

FOUR FACTS THE CARD LAYOUT CARRIED AND A TABLE CELL HAS NO COLUMN FOR — each must land somewhere in the unified table, and the task fails if any is dropped: the run's createdAt (without it, two runs of the same algorithm on the same target are indistinguishable rows, which the card's identity line prevented); comparabilityNote (MODEL-FLOW-018-T05's differing dataset/feature-spec/split warning); MODEL-FLOW-018-T06's CV wording, both phases of it; and the metric-source label discipline StandaloneRunRow already got right — T04's own audit found half of Step 4 labelling its sources correctly and warned the table must INHERIT that rather than replace it, which is now literal.

JSON HYGIENE, since this task edits the ledger's own block: T01 recorded that this feature's block once failed to parse on 16 unescaped double quotes inside T04's detail, and that until it was fixed no session could set a status programmatically and every tool reading the ledger failed. Use single quotes inside these strings.
