tasks.title: Write feature importance as its own artifact, and rank it in Evaluation
tasks.detail:
FOUR LAYERS, AND THE FIRST THREE ARE WHY THIS IS NOT A UI TASK.

(1) THE TRAINER. After fit, read the fitted estimator's own importance and write feature_importance.json under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/, shaped like its siblings: {algorithm, method, features: [{name, importance}]} -- `method` is REQUIRED and names what was measured ('impurity', 'coefficient', 'permutation'), because the three are different quantities and a reader cannot calibrate an unlabelled one (see the openDecision). Registered in ALL THREE places: outputs dict, _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS, RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES -- plus the Dockerfile COPY if a new module is added, the omission MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 caught by source review before any container ran.

WRITE NOTHING RATHER THAN SOMETHING WRONG. svm on a non-linear kernel, grp, and lstm/gru have no importance to read: no artifact, no placeholder, no empty features array. pls has coef_ but on latent components -- decide explicitly whether it is written under a DISTINCT method name or omitted, and record which; what it must not do is appear under the same header as a tree's per-feature figure. hist_gradient_boosting is the trap MODEL-FLOW-013-T05 already hit once in this exact class of read: check the attribute's LENGTH, not merely its presence, since an empty array present as an attribute reads as a real (empty) result rather than an honest absence.

STANDARDISATION MATTERS FOR THE LINEAR CASE. ols/ridge coef_ are only comparable across features if the inputs were scaled, and feature_spec.json records the scalers actually applied. Either state the scaling in the artifact or refuse to rank an unscaled linear fit -- a coefficient table over unscaled inputs ranks by unit, not by influence.

(2) SCHEMA AND READ PATH. ModelTrainingRun.featureImportanceKey String?, nullable, and a run predating this feature reads as 'not recorded for this run' -- the honest-legacy-null pattern MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 established for validationMissingPct and MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 reused for frameworkVersions. NO compute-on-read reconstruction: it would mean loading model.joblib outside the trainer image, which is where the estimator's own libraries live (MODEL-FLOW-016-T07 established that apps/python has no sklearn/joblib at all).

Read path mirrors the cv_folds precedent EXACTLY (MODEL-FLOW-016-T11): a python route with the same guard-then-read-and-shape-check shape as get_run_cv_folds, a backend wrapper, and the parsed result attached by getDraftRunService -- the SAME endpoint the client already polls, soft-failing to null and logging, so a storage hiccup never fails the run fetch.

(3) THE TABLE, in Step 5 Evaluation, in the bottom section beneath the residual diagnostics. Top 10 by importance, descending, with the rank, the feature name, its importance and its share of the total. Every feature the run used is counted in the denominator even when only ten are listed, and the count is stated -- 'top 10 of 21' -- so a reader cannot mistake the list for the whole feature set.

BEYOND THE TOP 10, STATE THE TAIL RATHER THAN HIDING IT: one line giving what the remaining features carry in aggregate. A ranking whose top 10 hold 87% and one whose top 10 hold 41% are different findings about the same model, and only the second is visible if the tail is silent.

A TARGET-DERIVED FEATURE IS FLAGGED WHERE IT RANKS. feature_spec.json's derived_from_target is a transitive closure (MODEL-FLOW-000-T02) and a target-derived feature ranking first is the leakage shape that whole task exists to catch -- assert_no_target_leakage already refuses the unservable case at fit time, but a legitimately-derived feature dominating the ranking is a finding a reader must see, not an error. Read the flag off the run's own manifest, never re-derived client-side.

(4) THE COUNT, AS ARITHMETIC AND NOT ADVICE -- pending the openDecision. What is computable and honest: the cumulative importance share at k, and the effective sample size per feature (distinct labelled values from the run's own frozen splitStats sidecar, MODEL-FLOW-014-T06, divided by feature_count from metrics). On the real 8,350-row artifact that reads 32 distinct labelled values across 21 features -- 1.5 observations per feature, a number that speaks for itself. What must NOT be written is a recommended band: MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 measured three orderings across three effective sample sizes and closed as a no-op, so no threshold is derivable from this system's data, and MODEL-FLOW-020's own AC5 is left open for that reason.

STEP 4 IS NOT IN SCOPE. The user asked for Evaluation, and Step 4's own table is already two source columns per metric across up to 24 candidates -- adding a per-feature ranking per row is the '20 charts under one sortable header' problem T06 exists to prevent, arriving through a different column. If it is wanted there, it is a separate task and it belongs in the reveal-on-demand row T06 already built.
tasks.result:
COMPLETED 2026-09-07. METHOD DECISION RESOLVED BY THE USER (openDecision 5, this task): impurity/coef_ ONLY -- the free, already-computed-inside-the-fit attribute, never a permutation re-scoring pass. Recorded because the ledger's own text flagged this as 'needs a call before T09 writes anything' rather than something this task could decide alone. Permutation stays a recorded follow-up.

THREE DECISIONS T09's own detail explicitly delegated, made and recorded here: (a) pls gets its OWN method name, 'pls-coefficient', never 'coefficient' -- a PLS coefficient is a projection through latent components, a different quantity than an OLS coefficient, and putting both under one label is exactly the conflation this task exists to refuse. (b) importance is ALWAYS NON-NEGATIVE -- feature_importances_ already is; coef_ is SIGNED, so summing a signed vector for 'share of total' is meaningless (shares could exceed 100% or go negative) and descending sort would rank the most negative coefficient last. For a coefficient method, importance holds abs(coefficient) and the signed value rides beside it as coefficient. (c) an UNSCALED linear fit still WRITES the artifact, carrying standardized:false -- the CLIENT refuses to rank it (AC27), rather than omitting the artifact. Omitting it would make that run indistinguishable from a pre-feature legacy run, the exact collapse AC11's three-facts rule and V06 exist to prevent, arriving through a new door.

LAYER 1, TRAINER. New images/trainer/app/importance.py, mirroring metrics.extract_loss_history's shape exactly: one try/except that never fails the run, per-algorithm dispatch, None means no artifact and no placeholder. impurity for random_forest/lightgbm/xgboost (feature_importances_); coefficient for ols/ridge and svm ONLY when model.kernel == 'linear' (checked explicitly, not relied on as an AttributeError) (coef_); pls-coefficient for pls (coef_, 2-D shape flattened). hgb/hist_gradient_boosting, mlp, grp, non-linear svm, lstm, gru return None -- no quantity to read. LENGTH guard (not presence) refuses an empty-but-present array, the exact MODEL-FLOW-013-T05 trap this task's own detail names; every value also checked finite. standardized/scaling_methods read off feature_spec['scaling'] (feature_spec_service.py's own {tag,method} list) for the three coefficient methods, null for impurity. FEATURE_IMPORTANCE_FILENAME='feature_importance.json' added to artifacts.py beside CV_FOLDS_FILENAME. Wired into pipelines/__init__.py's _publish -- computed CENTRALLY (not via TrainingResult.extra_json), since result.model/prepared.feature_cols/prepared.feature_spec are already in scope there and it covers CV's own refit (fit k+1) uniformly, adding no new TrainingResult field -- which matters because context.py's own docstring exists so a fourth strategy cannot forget one of these. No Dockerfile change: the Dockerfile already COPYs the whole app/ package for exactly this reason (its own comment says so), so a new module needs no COPY line -- the MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 omission this task's detail warned about does not apply to this Dockerfile shape. New MIRRORS.md entry 7 for the three-copy filename constant. New test/test_importance.py (12 cases): real fitted RandomForestRegressor/Ridge, length-mismatch and empty-array refusal, non-finite refusal, every no-quantity algorithm, svm linear-vs-non-linear kernel, pls's distinct method name, an estimator that raises on attribute access. NOT executable against this repo's own local environment as-is -- no sklearn install anywhere in it (apps/python/.venv and apps/serving/.venv both lack it), and nothing in CI builds images/trainer's Dockerfile (confirmed by grep, same finding this ledger already recorded once). EXECUTED ANYWAY, in a throwaway venv built for this one check (scikit-learn==1.5.2 + pytest, outside this repo's own environments, discarded after): 12/12 PASS. Two of those cases use hand-written stubs for PLSRegression/linear-SVR's coef_ shape rather than a real fit -- separately verified those exact assumptions against a REAL fitted PLSRegression(n_components=2) and a REAL SVR(kernel='linear') on synthetic (50,3) data in the same venv: both report coef_.shape == (1, 3), exactly what the stubs assumed; SVR(kernel='rbf') confirmed to have NO coef_ attribute at all, confirming the explicit kernel=='linear' check in importance.py is load-bearing, not decorative. The trainer layer is now execution-verified against the real sklearn 1.5.2 API, not merely written correctly from documentation.

LAYER 2, SCHEMA/READ PATH -- mirrors the cv_folds precedent (MODEL-FLOW-016-T04/T11) exactly, file for file: object_store.py gains FEATURE_IMPORTANCE_FILENAME; artifact_service.py's _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS gains it; new get_run_feature_importance(store, body) copies get_run_cv_folds's guard-then-read-and-shape-check verbatim (filename check, is_draft_run_key OR is_model_run_key, shape validation). New schemas.preprocess.RunFeatureImportanceRequest/FeatureImportanceEntry/RunFeatureImportanceResponse. New router POST /models/runs/feature-importance. artifact-keys.ts gains 'feature_importance.json' in RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES. New python-preprocess-client.ts RunFeatureImportanceSchema + getRunFeatureImportance(sourceKey), mirroring getRunCvFolds. tasks.title: SD returns to Step 4, from the predictions batch it already fetches, with its own source
tasks.detail:
AMENDS THIS FEATURE'S OWN userDecision, dated rather than rewritten. That decision reads 'sd is residual-derived and absent from both metrics and holdoutMetrics, so Step 4 must render it as unavailable-for-this-source', and T04's detail says 'SD IS NOT A TABLE COLUMN'. Both were true of the SOURCE they described — the run row. They are not true of the source Step 4 now has.

THE DATA ALREADY ARRIVES IN STEP 4, VERIFY THIS BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING. MODEL-FLOW-004 built run_predictions computing residual_sd over the FULL frame (live-verified digit-exact at 0.435277 for run 61f9aa28, the fixture MODEL-FLOW-004-V01 pinned). MODEL-FLOW-017-T02 carried that scalar through run_predictions_batch unchanged and MODEL-FLOW-017-V03 proved it: residual_sd from a DECIMATED response equals the full-frame value. MODEL-FLOW-019-T06 then wired useCandidatePredictions into Step 4 for the reveal-on-demand charts, and MODEL-FLOW-021-T03 calls it again for its own table. So this is a cell reading a field of a response the step already has — no new endpoint, no new Prisma column, no second read of an artifact.

CONFIRM FROM SOURCE, DO NOT INFER (the discipline every audit task in this ledger opens with): that run_predictions_batch's per-run item actually carries residual_sd and not only the decimated points array; and whether useCandidatePredictions's own client type projects it or drops it, the same too-narrow-interface gap MODEL-FLOW-012-T01/T03 and MODEL-FLOW-020-T04 each found for a different column.

SD CARRIES A SOURCE LIKE EVERY OTHER FIGURE — AC1, and the reason this task is not a one-line cell. MODEL-FLOW-017-T01 finding 5 established that predictions.parquet holds a DIFFERENT POPULATION depending on scoring phase: for a non-CV run it is the test split; for a SCORED CV run score.py wrote the HOLDOUT there under the same predictionsKey. So residual_sd is a test-split figure or a holdout figure and the two are not interchangeable. Read the phase from cvScoringPhaseOf (lib/metric-source.ts) and tag the value through T02's own SourcedMetrics union rather than declaring a fourth convention — a bare 'SD' column spanning both populations is precisely the conflation MODEL-FLOW-004 had to rename a shipped heading to undo.

'MUST NOT BE NULL' IS SATISFIABLE ONLY IN THE FORM STATED HERE, and the difference matters: SD must be non-null for every run that HAS a prediction series, and where there is none the reason is named. Three honest causes, and AC11's own three-facts rule applies unchanged: an UNSCORED CV run has no predictions.parquet at all by design (MODEL-FLOW-016-T06, 'a CV run writes no predictions AT TRAIN TIME') and its next action is to score; a run predating MODEL-FLOW-004's endpoint has no readable series; and a run whose object prefix was reclaimed by MODEL-FLOW-011's sweeper has lost it — that third one hides a real defect and is the one that must never render as a blank. MODEL-FLOW-018-T07's open cross-ledger finding is exactly this: planReclaim excludes a run only on modelId, so a selected-but-unsaved run's bytes are still reclaimable, which means a null SD on a selected run is a live possibility rather than a theoretical one.

SD STAYS NON-RANKABLE, AND SAY WHY WHERE THE HEADER IS. T04 made its header non-sortable because RankMetricKey excludes it and there was nothing to sort by; the reason changes but the outcome does not. Ranking by residual SD ranks by SCATTER, and a biased model with tight scatter would sort above an unbiased one with wider scatter — an ordering that reads as 'better model' while measuring something else. RANK_DIRECTION gains no sd entry.

SHOW IT BESIDE RMSE, NOT IN A DISTANT COLUMN. Since residual_SD <= RMSE always and the gap is exactly the bias, the two adjacent are readable as a single fact about the model; separated by three metric columns they are two numbers a reader has to remember to compare. This is also what makes T11's RMSE/SD criterion checkable by eye rather than only by the criterion engine.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08. residual_sd confirmed present at every hop before writing anything (artifact_service.py:1661, full-frame, pre-decimation) through the zod schema (python-preprocess-client.ts) and the ...item spread to the client's residualSd -- no new endpoint, no new column. New pure module lib/residual-sd.ts (residualSdOf) tags the figure with cvScoringPhaseOf-derived population (holdout for a scored CV run, test-split otherwise) and names one of five states (a value; awaiting-scoring; scoring; no-series; unreadable, carrying the batch item's own error; not-recorded) -- never a bare blank. Step 4's five sd exclusion points (UNTRACKED_METRIC_KEYS, STEP4_METRIC_KEYS and its two picker uses, the belt-and-braces visibleMetrics filter) are removed; isRankMetricKey now reads RANK_DIRECTION directly rather than a second list, so sd stays structurally unrankable (AC33) without a maintained exclusion set. tasks.title: Acceptance criteria compare two figures instead of a typed threshold
tasks.detail:
REPLACES T07's TYPED THRESHOLD WITH A COMPARISON, AND THE MOTIVATION IS SOUND: an absolute threshold requires the reader to know the target's units and scale before the number means anything, so it does not transfer between targets and cannot be reviewed by anyone who has not seen that tag's range. A comparison between two figures of the same run is scale-free.

BUT THE TWO EXAMPLES AS WRITTEN CANNOT PASS, AND THIS IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN OPINION. For any residual vector, MAE <= RMSE (power-mean inequality, equality iff every |residual| is equal) and residual_SD <= RMSE (since RMSE^2 = SD^2 + mean(residual)^2, equality iff the residual mean is zero). So 'RMSE < MAE' and 'RMSE < SD' are UNSATISFIABLE and their reverses hold unconditionally. A criterion that can only ever read fail, or can only ever read pass, is the failure AC15 already forbids for the comparator — arriving instead through the operand pair. Refuse to express it, by construction, in the same way AC15 refuses a direction picker: an unsatisfiable pair must not be selectable.

WHAT SHIPS IS A RATIO WITH A DERIVED DIRECTION. {left, right, ratio} where left and right are (metric, source) pairs and the comparator is fixed by the pair's own known inequality, never chosen. Three pairs are worth having and each answers a different question:
  RMSE / MAE — outlier concentration. Range [1, sqrt(n)]. Near 1 means errors are uniform; large means a handful of misses dominate.
  RMSE / residual_SD — BIAS, and the gap is mean(residual) exactly. Depends on T10 landing and on openDecision 6 resolving to residual SD.
  holdout_RMSE / test_RMSE — the overfit gap, and the most informative figure on this screen by this feature's own T04 detail ('a candidate at test 0.42 and holdout 0.81 is telling you the cleaning recipe flattered it'). Depends on openDecision 7, since T07 was narrowed to holdout-only.

REFUSE A DIMENSIONALLY INVALID PAIR BY CONSTRUCTION, a refusal class that does not exist today. RMSE, MAE and SD are all in the target's own units; R2 is dimensionless. 'RMSE / R2' is not a scale-free ratio, it is a category error — the same class as the heading MODEL-FLOW-004 renamed, and as putting a PLS latent-component coefficient under a tree's importance header (MODEL-FLOW-019-T09's own pls-coefficient decision). Declare the unit class per metric and let the picker offer only same-class pairs. Do not enforce this with a hand-written list of allowed pairs: derive it, or it becomes a second source of truth about which metrics are which, the drift finding 5 of MODEL-FLOW-020 names.

NO RECOMMENDED RATIO IS SHIPPED — this is not conservatism, it is what MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 measured. That task ran a real capacity ladder on three effective sample sizes (32 / 59 / 97 distinct labelled values) against the real trainer image on the real holdout and got THREE DIFFERENT ORDERINGS of the same five settings, and closed as a measured no-op. AC5 of that feature is left open for exactly this reason. A default ratio written now would be extrapolation from a range that cannot support it, and it would read on screen exactly like a measured constant. Instead SHOW THE RUN'S OWN CURRENT RATIO beside the input, so the reader calibrates from a figure in front of them rather than from folklore — and carry the block-level caveat MODEL-FLOW-020-T05 already ships for suggested ranges, stated once rather than per field.

EVERY OTHER T07 RULE SURVIVES UNCHANGED AND MUST BE RE-PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED TO HAVE COME ALONG: advisory and never blocking, so a failing candidate is marked and still selectable and still saveable (AC13, and DS-LAKE-019's own reasoning for moving this codebase's statistical checks from blocking to advisory transfers verbatim); a ratio whose EITHER side is absent reads 'not evaluated', never 'fail' (AC14, and with two operands there are now two ways to be absent rather than one); view state in mpAcceptanceCriteriaAtom committed on Apply through useRunConfigDraft, no ModelDraft column (AC16, keeping finding 6 true as written); icon shape and never colour, since red and amber are reserved for workspace and plant status here.

MIGRATE THE EXISTING SHAPE, DO NOT SILENTLY DROP IT. Any AcceptanceCriterion already in mpAcceptanceCriteriaAtom is {metric, source, value}. T07 already faced this once when the concurrent holdout-only narrowing landed, and its answer was a stated migration notice with a Clear action rather than a silent discard. Do the same, or a user's existing criteria stop being applied with nothing on screen saying so.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08, both blocking decisions resolved by the user the same day (openDecisions 6 and 7, see userDecisions). AcceptanceCriterion widened from T07's {metric, source, value} to {left, right, ratio}. Offerable pairs are DERIVED (offerableRatioPairs(), lib/acceptance-criteria.ts) from two small tables -- METRIC_RATIO_META (unit class, non-negativity) and KNOWN_INEQUALITIES ([rmse,mae], [rmse,sd]) -- never hand-listed: RMSE/MAE and RMSE/SD offered only larger-over-smaller (floor 1, AC29); r2 offered no pair at all, sharing no unit class with anything else (AC30); holdout_X/test_X offered only for rmse/mae, the openDecision-7 exception. An SD-bearing pair is run-resolved on BOTH sides (neither operand names a source) since T10 established SD's population varies by run shape -- pinning it to one source would read not-evaluated on every run of the other shape. ratioValueOf is the single derivation both the table's verdict (evaluateRatioCriterion) and core-config.tsx's own 'current ratio' preview call (V14). Legacy {metric,source,value} criteria are detected by shape (isLegacyCriterion) and offered a Clear action, never silently dropped. ThresholdMark moved from a per-cell mark to a per-row Criteria column (RowCriteriaMarks) since a ratio belongs to the run, not to one figure. V10 (unreachable-pair proof), V13 (both absence directions), V14 (single derivation) proven in the rewritten lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts; V13's row-level rendering also proven end to end.

tasks.title: Criteria become a bare comparison — free operator, chosen labels, no typed value
tasks.detail:
REVERSES T11's SHIPPED RATIO FORM, ON THE USER'S OWN GROUND (2026-09-08): the right number is unknowable, so no number should be typed. That is not a preference — it is the same ground MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 closed on, having run a real capacity ladder at three effective sample sizes against the real trainer image on the real holdout and got THREE DIFFERENT ORDERINGS of the same five settings, leaving that feature's AC5 open because no threshold is derivable from this system's data. AC31 (no recommended ratio, show the run's own instead) was that problem worked around; removing the number removes it at the root. The criterion stays exactly what the user asks it to stay: ADVISORY, a warning and nothing more.

THE SHAPE. AcceptanceCriterion becomes {left, operator, right}, where an operand is {metric, source?} — the same optional-source convention T11 already shipped for SD, now generalised: a present source PINS the population, an absent one is RUN-RESOLVED. The `ratio` field is gone. Two operators only, and this is deliberate: strict and non-strict cannot be distinguished on two floating-point figures that are never exactly equal, and offering four would invite a reader to believe the choice carries meaning it does not.

WHAT MUST NOT BE FREE IS THE PAIR, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE SAFETY ARGUMENT. Some pairs have an order fixed by algebra rather than by the model: MAE <= RMSE always (power-mean inequality, equality iff every absolute residual is equal) and residual_SD <= RMSE always (RMSE^2 = SD^2 + mean(residual)^2, equality iff the residual mean is zero). A bare comparison on either fires on EVERY run that will ever exist in one direction and on NONE in the other — a warning with no information, which is AC15's own failure arriving through the operand pair instead of the comparator. So KNOWN_INEQUALITIES INVERTS ITS ROLE: T11 used it to ORIENT a ratio (larger over smaller, floor 1); T12 uses it to REFUSE the pair outright, in both directions. rmse-vs-mae and rmse-vs-sd stop being offerable at all.

WHAT IS OFFERABLE, each genuinely undetermined rather than merely permitted. (1) CROSS-SOURCE, SAME METRIC: holdout_X against test_X — the overfit gap this feature's own T04 detail calls the most informative figure on the screen, and whose order is only an EXPECTATION rather than a theorem, since a holdout window falling in a stable process period can genuinely score better than the test split. (2) MAE AGAINST RESIDUAL SD within one population, which has no fixed order at all: a zero-mean near-normal residual gives MAE around 0.8 times SD, a constant-offset residual gives MAE above it and SD at zero, so the comparison is a bias and tail-shape detector — the one thing neither figure says alone.

R2 RETURNS AS AN OPERAND, and the reason AC34 is amended rather than deleted. A ratio of two possibly-negative numbers flips sign and does not order by magnitude, and negative R2 is the NORM here rather than an edge case — MODEL-FLOW-005 recorded a real r2 of -1,110,858, MODEL-FLOW-016-T12 read cv_r2_mean of -12.09 off a real ModelVersion row, MODEL-FLOW-004's own fixture run scored -2.4067. A bare COMPARISON has no such problem: holdout_R2 < test_R2 is well defined whatever the signs. So dropping the number recovers a metric the ratio form had to refuse, and METRIC_RATIO_META's non-negativity flag stops gating offerability (its unit-class flag still does).

A NEW REFUSAL THE RATIO FORM NEVER NEEDED: WITHIN ONE CRITERION, EITHER BOTH OPERANDS PIN A SOURCE OR NEITHER DOES. T10 established that residual SD's population varies by run shape (test split for a non-CV run, holdout for a SCORED CV run), which is why T11 left SD-bearing pairs run-resolved on both sides. Mixing the two — a pinned holdout MAE against a run-resolved SD — compares a figure whose population is known against one whose population depends on the run, so the SAME criterion means different things on two rows of one table. That is exactly the conflation this feature exists to prevent, reachable through the operand pair rather than through a column header. Derive the rule; do not hand-write an allow-list (MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a's second-source-of-truth argument applies to an admissible-pair list precisely as it does to a render mode, and T11 already built offerableRatioPairs derived for this reason).

CANONICAL FORM ON COMMIT, OR THE SAME CRITERION EXISTS TWICE. With both operands and the operator free, 'A < B' and 'B > A' are one criterion written two ways and nothing stops a user adding both — two rows that mark identically in Step 4 and cannot be told apart. Normalise on commit (fix the operand order by a stable key, express the operator in that frame) and make pairsEqual compare NORMALISED criteria rather than raw fields, so the picker's own already-added filter actually excludes the mirror. Note this is a NEW hazard: T11's pairs were pre-oriented by KNOWN_INEQUALITIES, so no mirror could be constructed.

ONE NUMBER SURVIVES AND IT IS NOT A GUESS: R2 >= 0, as a CHECKBOX WITH NO INPUT FIELD. Zero is structural rather than chosen — the line at which a model stops beating the target's own mean — and openDecision 6 recorded that this is where the SD-of-the-data reading ('my error is smaller than the natural variation in the data') now lives, since RMSE/SD(y_true) <= 1 is algebraically R2 > 0. Removing it to satisfy 'no numbers' would delete a MEANING rather than a guess. Its comparator stays derived from RANK_DIRECTION, never chosen.

SHOW BOTH OPERAND VALUES, NOT A DERIVED FIGURE. AC31's calibration intent is better served without the number: render each operand's own value from the draft's most recent SUCCEEDED run and say plainly whether the comparison currently holds. 'Validate RMSE 0.21 vs Test RMSE 0.19 — fires today' tells a reader more than any ratio did and needs no threshold to interpret. Step 3 passes residualSd: null (its own shipped choice — one advisory preview is not worth a second request there), so an SD-bearing criterion states that plainly on that surface rather than showing a number, exactly as T11's own SD caveat already does.

ONE DERIVATION, NOT TWO — V14's rule generalises. The evaluator returns the verdict AND both operand values, and every surface renders what it returned, reusing metricValueOf (T02) and residualSdOf (T10) rather than reading a metric a second way. Two derivations of one comparison is how a row marked fail comes to display values that look like they pass.

AC35 SURVIVES UNCHANGED AND IS THE SHARPEST TRAP: metricValueOf answers a cv-fold-estimate from its own `mean` (T03's own result says so), so a comparison engine reading a CV run silently receives the FOLD MEAN and compares an estimate of a CONFIGURATION against a measurement of the SHIPPED REFIT — MODEL-FLOW-016's finding 3 category error, which that feature records as having already shipped once here and been corrected only by renaming a heading. Gate it AT THE OPERAND; it cannot fall through the operand-absence path, because the value is PRESENT rather than missing.

AC37 IS WITHDRAWN — no division remains, so a zero denominator is unreachable. ratioFloorOf and ThresholdInput's floor-refused-on-commit behaviour go with it.

WHAT SURVIVES FROM T07 AND T11 AND MUST BE RE-PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED TO HAVE COME ALONG: advisory and never blocking, so a failing candidate is marked and still selectable and still saveable (AC13, and DS-LAKE-019's own reasoning for moving this codebase's statistical checks from blocking to advisory transfers verbatim); an absent operand reads not-evaluated and never fail, both directions, each carrying T02's own holdoutAbsence reason (no-dataset-holdout, holdout-not-recorded, not-scored-yet); view state in mpAcceptanceCriteriaAtom committed on Apply through useRunConfigDraft with no ModelDraft column (AC16, keeping finding 6 true as written); RowCriteriaMarks stays a per-ROW column rather than a per-cell mark, since a comparison belongs to the run and not to one figure — with no number to print, the mark can be an icon plus a compact label, which is a simplification rather than a loss; icon shape and never colour, since red and amber are reserved for workspace and plant status here.

MIGRATION IS NOW TWO SHAPES DEEP, AND BOTH ARE DETECTED BY SHAPE RATHER THAN BY A VERSION FIELD: T07's {metric, source, value} and T11's {left, right, ratio}. isLegacyCriterion currently detects the first by the ABSENCE of `ratio`; it must now detect the second by its PRESENCE, and the check inverts. Neither is silently discarded — state the count and offer a Clear, the answer T07 already gave when the holdout-only narrowing landed and T11 gave again. A stored criterion no longer applied in Step 4 must say so on screen.

FILES THIS TOUCHES, since it reverses shipped code rather than adding to a blank file: lib/acceptance-criteria.ts (RatioPair -> the comparison pair; offerableRatioPairs' rule inverted; ratioFloorOf, ratioValueOf and ratioPairLabel removed or repointed; evaluateRatioCriterion returns both values; pairsEqual canonicalised; isLegacyCriterion widened), its colocated test, core-config.tsx's AcceptanceCriteriaControl (ThresholdInput deleted, the grid loses its value column, lossAlignedMetric repointed to order the left-operand choices), and phase-4-model-selection.tsx's RowCriteriaMarks.

JSON HYGIENE, since this task edits the ledger's own block: T01 recorded that this feature's block once failed to parse on 16 unescaped double quotes inside T04's detail, and that until it was fixed no session could set a status programmatically and every tool reading the ledger failed. Use single quotes inside these strings.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08. Shipped exactly as specified: AcceptanceCriterion is now {kind:'comparison', left, operator, right} | {kind:'r2-floor'} in lib/acceptance-criteria.ts. offerablePairs() derives the offered set from one rule (exactly one of {metric, source} differs) plus three refusals (AC29 pin-parity, AC25 unit class, AC24 KNOWN_INEQUALITIES in either direction) -- proven as a SET in the colocated test, yielding exactly the four pairs: holdout/test RMSE, holdout/test MAE, holdout/test R2, and MAE vs SD (run-resolved). canonicalise()+criterionEqual() refuse the mirror (AC31/AC38). evaluateCriterion() returns both operand READINGS (value+absence), never a second derivation (V14); the CV fold mean is refused at the operand via an explicit 'cross-validation' absence (AC28/V18, latent guard -- residualSdOf never emits cv-fold-estimate today, so the test constructs the state deliberately). Validate R2 >= 0 ships as a checkbox with no input field (AC33), pinned to holdout per openDecision 10's un-reopened threshold narrowing -- picker shape resolved via openDecision 11 as PAIR LIST + OPERATOR TOGGLE, not free operands (see userDecisions). core-config.tsx's ThresholdInput is deleted outright; phase-4-model-selection.tsx's RowCriteriaMarks filters legacy criteria (both T07's and T11's shape) before evaluating, per-row, icon-shape-only. A file NOT in this task's original list also needed the fix: hooks/model/use-run-config-draft.ts's criteriaEqual compared a now-nonexistent 'ratio' field, which would have silently broken Apply's dirty flag for an operator-only edit -- rewritten to delegate to lib/acceptance-criteria.ts's own criterionEqual. Verified: lib/acceptance-criteria.ts check-types/lint clean; 28/28 unit tests pass; phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx's advisory-acceptance-criteria block (6 tests) rewritten to the new shape and passing; zero new failures introduced across the full pipeline/training-config/hooks test sweep (pre-existing failures from a concurrent, unrelated seed-control refactor and missing-rate wiring task are unchanged in count and identity, verified before and after this task's edits).

tasks.title: A y_true against y_pred scatter beneath the Actual vs Predicted chart
tasks.detail:
CLIENT-ONLY, and confirm that before scoping anything else — MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code. run_predictions (MODEL-FLOW-004) already returns the point array with y_true and y_pred plus FULL-FRAME y-ranges, and useDraftRunEvaluation already fetches it for the two charts Step 5 renders today. No endpoint, no Prisma column, no trainer change, no image bump.

WHY IT IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH THE CHART ABOVE IT: ActualVsPredictedChart plots both series against TIME — confirmed by EVAL_SYNC_ID being wired into syncId on it and on ResidualChart alike (MODEL-FLOW-017-T01 finding 4 locates the constant at actual-vs-predicted-chart.tsx:17), which only synchronises charts sharing an x-axis. A time overlay hides curvature, saturation at the ends of the target's range, heteroscedasticity, and range compression; a parity plot shows all four at a glance. They are two views of one series, not one view twice.

EQUAL SHARED DOMAIN ON BOTH AXES, AND A SQUARE ASPECT — the trap that makes this chart lie while looking correct. Recharts auto-scales each axis independently, so with x spanning the target's own range and y spanning the prediction's, the identity line renders as a diagonal that is NOT at 45 degrees and does not pass through the visual corners: a systematically biased model reads as well-calibrated, and a calibrated one reads as biased. Force one domain, [min(both series), max(both series)], onto BOTH axes, and take it from the endpoint's own FULL-FRAME y-ranges rather than from the rendered points, so the axis does not shift if the point set ever changes.

THE REFERENCE LINE IS THE IDENTITY LINE, NOT A FIT. A regression line on a parity plot is a different claim — its slope is range compression and its intercept is bias, both real and both worth having — but the two must be visually distinguishable or a reader cannot tell what they are measuring against. MODEL-FLOW-004 deleted seededNoise, comparePoints and compareFit from this very step rather than let a chart carry a series whose provenance was unclear; the same rule applies to a line.

DO NOT JOIN EVAL_SYNC_ID. That group's members share a time x-axis; this chart's x-axis is y_true. Joining it crosshair-links two incompatible axes, which is a different hazard from the one MODEL-FLOW-017-T01 flagged for the same constant and is caused by the same module-level scope.

NAME THE POPULATION, exactly as MODEL-FLOW-019-T10 must for SD and for the same reason: for a non-CV run predictions.parquet is the TEST SPLIT, and for a SCORED CV run score.py wrote the HOLDOUT under the same predictionsKey (MODEL-FLOW-017-T01 finding 5). Read the phase from cvScoringPhaseOf and label the chart from it, never from the algorithm name (MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a). An unscored CV run reaches the awaiting-scoring branch and renders no chart at all, which MODEL-FLOW-016-T11 already built.

CHECK TagScatterChart BEFORE WRITING A COMPONENT, and expect it not to fit. It renders a point cloud with a regression fit and the 'N of M shown; fit uses all M' disclosure DraftScatterResult carries, which is the right disclosure vocabulary — but its input is an artifact's two tags, it has no identity line, and it has no shared-domain constraint. MODEL-FLOW-010-T05 judged DataAnalysisCard reusable, found it draft-scoped and store-coupled, and the resolution was to make the component store-agnostic rather than to copy it. Reach the same kind of answer explicitly rather than assuming either way.

NO DECIMATION IS NEEDED AND THE REASON MUST BE RECORDED FOR WHOEVER CHANGES IT. Step 5 reads the SINGLE-run endpoint, which has no decimation branch at all: MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS=20000 and a run above it is refused by name, with the largest real predictions.parquet in the system measured at 4,633 rows (MODEL-FLOW-017-T01). So the scatter gets the full frame. If this chart is ever routed through run_predictions_batch, the decimation basis becomes WRONG for it — MODEL-FLOW-017-T02 decimates by LTTB keyed on (timestamp, y_true), which is correct for a time series, while MODEL-FLOW-017's own finding 5 records that a scatter needs 2D grid binning 'because a scatter's axes are tag values rather than time', which is exactly why DS-LAKE's scatter_service does not use the LTTB path.

OVERPLOTTING IS A RENDER CONCERN AND ALREADY BOUNDED: a small radius with low opacity is sufficient at 4,633 points, and the 20,000 refusal caps the worst case. Do not build 2D binning for a bound that is already enforced upstream.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08. Confirmed client-only as the task required: run_predictions already returns every point undecimated and the full-frame y_true/y_pred ranges; no endpoint, Prisma column, or trainer change made. useDraftRunEvaluation widened with a new ParityRange field (yTrueMin/Max, yPredMin/Max) surfaced from RunPredictions rather than folded into ModelFit, which is shared with the models/[id] monitoring surfaces. New component pipeline/evaluation/parity-scatter-chart.tsx modelled explicitly on QQPlotChart (same domain array on both axes, an identity ReferenceLine) rather than TagScatterChart (tag-shaped, has its own regression fit, no shared-domain constraint) -- the choice is recorded in the component's own doc comment as T13 requires. No syncId, no EVAL_SYNC_ID import (V20, proven as a static-source contract test since syncId never reaches the DOM). No regression line -- only the y=x identity line. Population label ('Test' vs 'Validate') derived from the SAME cvPhase variable the existing CV branches already read, never from the algorithm name; the existing, separately-tested 'Test-split residual diagnostics' heading text was left byte-identical since it is asserted verbatim by an existing passing test outside T13's scope. Wired into phase-5-evaluation.tsx immediately beneath the Actual vs Predicted section, inside the hasFit gate, using the FULL (non-zoomed) row set -- a time-window zoom has no clear meaning for a chart whose x-axis is a value, not time. Pre-work done in the same file since T13 touches it anyway: removed the dead GitCompareArrows import and the stale 'Compare with...' test assertion, both leftover from an unrelated, already-landed removal of that control. Verified: check-types/lint clean; V20 (contract) and V21 (non-CV vs scored-CV population labels differ) both pass; full phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx suite (18 tests) passes; zero new failures elsewhere.

tasks.title: Permutation importance beside the impurity figures, scored on the holdout
tasks.blocked_reason: BLOCKED ON openDecision 8 (placement) AND openDecision 9 (which seed drives the permutation, since either answer contradicts something already shipped). Both are user calls that change what is built rather than how it is worded — the discipline MODEL-FLOW-019-T09's own method question and MODEL-FLOW-016-T12's unscored-save question each followed.
tasks.detail:
DISCHARGES MODEL-FLOW-019's openDecision 5, whose recommendation was impurity first with permutation 'recorded as a follow-up, not scheduled'. MODEL-FLOW-019-T09 shipped impurity and coefficient; this is the follow-up, now scheduled.

PERMUTATION ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION AND ITS DISAGREEMENT WITH IMPURITY IS THE FINDING — openDecision 5's own option (c), verbatim: 'a feature ranked first by impurity and tenth by permutation is telling the reader something neither number says alone.' The bias it corrects is MEASURED here rather than cited: MODEL-FLOW-020-T03's parquet census found process tags holding roughly 1,000 distinct values each while the target holds 32 to 97, and sklearn's own documentation warns impurity-based importances inflate with cardinality — so the current ranking favours the finest-grained sensor over a coarser predictive one, and the number looks entirely plausible. SHOW BOTH, SIDE BY SIDE, IN ONE TABLE. Replacing impurity would throw away the comparison that is the whole point.

IT RUNS IN THE TRAINER, LIKE IMPURITY, AND FOR THE SAME REASON: it needs the fitted estimator, and model.joblib can only be loaded where the estimator's own libraries live — MODEL-FLOW-016-T07 established that apps/python carries no sklearn or joblib at all, which is also why MODEL-FLOW-019-T09 forbids any compute-on-read reconstruction.

PERMUTE THE HOLDOUT WHERE IT EXISTS, AND TAG WHAT WAS PERMUTED. Permuting the training frame measures what the model USED; permuting held-out rows measures what GENERALISES. On this system's data those are nearly the same population — the test split comes from the same cleaned artifact past the same recipe, at lag-1 autocorrelation 0.9992 across 19 to 97 distinct labelled values — so the test split is close to permuting the training distribution. The holdout is the only population no fit ever saw (DS-LAKE-018), and it is ALREADY IN HAND ON BOTH PATHS with no new read: a non-CV run receives holdoutDataUrl at claim time and scores it inline, and a CV run has model and holdout together inside run_score(). Where no holdout exists, permute the test split and SAY SO — the source-tagging rule of MODEL-FLOW-019's AC1, applied to a figure rather than a metric.

CORRELATED FEATURES MAKE PERMUTATION UNDERSTATE, AND THIS MUST BE STATED WHERE THE FIGURES ARE. Permuting one tag while a correlated sibling still carries the signal reports the first as unimportant, and on plant data tags in one loop correlate by construction — MODEL-FLOW-010-T05 built a top-correlated-pairs list for Step 2 precisely because that correlation is a visible property of these datasets. The failure this prevents is a physical conclusion drawn from a statistical artefact: 'this sensor does not matter'. Point at Step 2's own pairs list rather than recomputing correlation here.

REPORT THE SPREAD, NOT ONLY THE MEAN. permutation_importance returns importances_mean and importances_std over n_repeats, and a feature at 0.04 +/- 0.002 is not the same finding as one at 0.04 +/- 0.05 — the same reasoning MODEL-FLOW-016-T05 gives for cv_rmse_std ('storing only a fold mean throws away the one thing k fits were paid for'). Also record the baseline score, the metric it was scored with, and n_repeats: an importance is a DROP from a baseline and is uninterpretable without it. The metric is RMSE, minimised, and this task does not reopen that — MODEL-FLOW-005 chose it over R2 after a real run scored r2 = -1,110,858 while its rmse stayed readable.

A SECOND ARTIFACT, NOT A WIDENED ONE. MODEL-FLOW-019-T09 shipped feature_importance.json as {algorithm, method, features:[{name, importance}]} with method a REQUIRED top-level string, and 179 existing runs plus every run since carry that shape; holding two methods would mean methods:[{...}], a breaking change to an artifact just shipped. Permutation also carries fields impurity has no use for — std, n_repeats, scored_on, baseline_score, metric — so different fields make it a different artifact rather than a variant. Register permutation_importance.json in the SAME THREE PLACES every run filename is registered (the trainer's outputs dict, apps/python's _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS, and TS RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES) plus a MIRRORS.md entry for the shared filename constant: MODEL-FLOW-013-T05 records that missing one is how a filename ends up refused at upload, and MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 separately had to add a missing Dockerfile COPY for the same class of omission — though T09 confirmed this Dockerfile COPYs the whole app/ package, so a new module needs no COPY line.

Nullable permutationImportanceKey, and a run predating this reads as not recorded for this run — the honest-legacy-null pattern MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 established for validationMissingPct and MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 reused for frameworkVersions. Read path mirrors get_run_cv_folds and T09's own get_run_feature_importance exactly: guard, read, shape-check, a backend wrapper, and attach it in getDraftRunService soft-failing to null so a storage hiccup never fails the run fetch.

THE SAME ALGORITHMS THAT HAVE NO IMPORTANCE STILL HAVE NONE — but for a different reason, which is worth stating rather than reusing T09's list by reflex. Permutation needs only predict(), so it is computable for svm on any kernel and for grp, which have no impurity or coefficient at all. It is NOT computable for lstm and gru at acceptable cost: MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 measured a torch forward pass under the production 2-CPU cgroup and found a 500-window fit taking over ten minutes before the thread pool was capped, and n_features x n_repeats forward passes would multiply exactly that. Decide per algorithm on cost rather than on attribute availability, and write nothing rather than a partial table where it is refused.

COST, TO BE MEASURED AND RECORDED RATHER THAN ASSERTED — the standard GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS, LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS and MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD were each set by, and the template is the measured table at apps/python/services/split_stats_service.py:60-127. openDecision 5 estimated 21 features against a 2,554-row test split as 21 predict() calls and noted it 'is still a per-run cost this ledger has not measured'; with n_repeats that is n_features x n_repeats. Measure it against the real image under the real memory and CPU limits before choosing n_repeats, and record the measurement beside the constant.

BUNDLE THE IMAGE BUMP WITH MODEL-FLOW-019-T12. Both change score_holdout and run_score, and MODEL-FLOW-016-T07 set the rule from its own experience: 'ONE bump per the plan's own sequencing rule — two bumps would leave a window where a scoring container runs a CV-only image.' Remember resolveDigest() pins TRAINING_IMAGE at BACKEND BOOT, so a bump does nothing until the backend restarts, and nothing in CI builds images/trainer's Dockerfile — for a figure like this a stale image is a SILENT no-op, indistinguishable on screen from the honest-legacy-null path.

tasks.title: One population derivation for every Step 5 surface, derived from MetricSource rather than declared
tasks.detail:
READ, DO NOT INFER — MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code, and every audit task in this ledger opens this way.

THE DEFECT IS THREE INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS OF ONE FACT, AND THE PARTIAL RENAME IS ALREADY ON SCREEN. phase-5-evaluation.tsx reads cvPhase three times and says three different things: parityPopulation resolves to 'Validate', the residual-diagnostics HEADING resolves to 'Holdout residual diagnostics', and that same section's BODY says 'validation holdout'. Meanwhile the Actual vs Predicted and Residuals sections still say 'test' for a scored CV run whose fit IS the holdout — MODEL-FLOW-017-T01 finding 5 established that score.py writes the holdout under the same predictionsKey, and MODEL-FLOW-019-T10/T13 already had to state the population for SD and for the parity axes for exactly this reason. This is MODEL-FLOW-004's renamed heading ('Validation residual diagnostics' -> 'Test-split residual diagnostics') arriving a second time in the same file, and it is HALF applied rather than absent, which is the harder state to spot.

DERIVE THE TYPE, DO NOT DECLARE A FOURTH VOCABULARY. lib/metric-source.ts already owns MetricSource ('test-split' | 'holdout' | 'cv-fold-estimate'), cvScoringPhaseOf (moved there by T02 on the stated grounds that deciding which SOURCE a figure has is that module's whole subject), and METRIC_SOURCE_LABELS. A predictions file is never a fold estimate, so the population type is Extract<MetricSource, 'test-split' | 'holdout'> — derived from the union that already exists, not a new enum beside it. A hand-written second union is the second-source-of-truth this feature's own T11 and T12 each refused for pair lists, and MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a refused for render modes.

TWO LABEL FORMS, BOTH IN ONE PLACE, because the axes and the prose need different words: an axis form in the dataset's own split vocabulary (what ParityScatterChart's population prop already takes) and a prose form for a sentence. Put both beside METRIC_SOURCE_LABELS so the file that owns the source owns every name for it.

THE NON-'scored' BRANCH IS CORRECT BY CONTROL FLOW, NOT BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS THE REAL EXPOSURE. cvPhase !== 'scored' currently maps to the test split for ALL of awaiting-scoring and scoring, which are CV runs with no test split to name at all; it does not misreport today only because two early returns fire before the scatter. Move the correctness into the type: exhaust the four phases explicitly and let a fifth phase fail at compile rather than defaulting to a label. T01 already recorded that cvScoringPhaseOf has FOUR states, not three, after this feature's own finding said three.

DO NOT RESOLVE Holdout-vs-Validate HERE. MODEL-FLOW-019-T04's detail argues for 'Holdout' on the grounds that `validate` names the dataset QUALITY GATE in this codebase; MODEL-FLOW-021's own finding records a concurrent, partial rename toward 'Validate' and leaves it as an open user decision. This task is what makes that decision a one-line change whichever way it goes — it must not pick a side, and its tests must assert the SHAPE (every panel agrees, the two run kinds differ) rather than the contested word.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08. `EvaluationPopulation` moved to lib/metric-source.ts and DERIVED (`Extract<MetricSource, 'test-split' | 'holdout'>`), replacing the hand-written `'test' | 'holdout'` union that had drifted into lib/model-evaluation.ts -- the exact second-source-of-truth this task existed to remove. `populationOf(phase)` is exhaustive over all four CvScoringPhase members via a `never`-typed default branch (V26, proven as a compile-time `@ts-expect-error` test in lib/metric-source.test.ts -- an unused directive is itself a build failure, not a silently green test). All FOUR chart panels plus the success banner now read the ONE `population` derivation -- the banner previously read raw `cvPhase` a fifth time and was switched to match (V25, proven end to end in phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx: both run kinds asserted across every panel, the wrong word asserted ABSENT in each case). Holdout-vs-Validate deliberately left unresolved per the task's own instruction -- MODEL-FLOW-021's open decision is untouched; the word is now a one-line change in one file. Three label forms (populationAxisLabel/populationLabel/populationTitle) live beside METRIC_SOURCE_LABELS in the file that owns MetricSource.

tasks.title: Three sentences per chart: what it plots, which population, what it detects
tasks.detail:
DEPENDS ON T15 — every sentence below names a population, and writing them against three separate ternaries would triple the rename this feature has already paid for once.

EVERY PANEL ANSWERS THREE THINGS IN THIS ORDER: what is plotted, written as a definition ('residual = y - y_hat') rather than a description; which population, from T15's single derivation; and the failure mode this panel detects that no other panel does. A panel whose third sentence duplicates a neighbour's has no reason to be its own panel.

FOUR DEFECTS TO FIX RATHER THAN REWORD.
(1) The Actual vs Predicted detail TERMINATES MID-CLAUSE, on a semicolon, after 'inside the +/-1 SD band;'. It has been on screen in that state.
(2) The parity section has NO detail at all and its heading collides with the chart above it — 'Actual vs Predicted' over a time axis, 'Actual vs Predicted Scatter Plot' over a value axis, two different claims one word apart. T13's own doc comment already states why the second exists (curvature, saturation, heteroscedasticity, range compression — four things a time overlay hides); none of that reasoning reached the screen.
(3) The histogram and Q-Q are computed over `residuals`, the FULL frame, while the two charts above them render `visibleRows`, the ZOOM WINDOW. Nothing says so, so a reader who zooms watches two charts move and two not, and reads it as a bug. State the scope; do not make the diagnostics follow the zoom, since a distribution over a hand-picked window is a different and weaker claim.
(4) The per-fold table says a fold far from its neighbours is a real finding, but not that an expanding window makes fold 1 systematically worse for a reason that has nothing to do with the period it tested — MODEL-FLOW-016-T03 records exactly that ('a reader shown five RMSEs without five row counts will read a data-volume artefact as a regime change'), and the row counts are already in the table.

THE +/-1 SD BAND MUST STOP READING AS A PREDICTIVE INTERVAL, and this is the one item that needs an audit before a word is written. The band is ONE constant width from fit.sd across the whole series, not per-point uncertainty, and a reader who takes it for the latter draws conclusions about individual predictions that the chart cannot support. READ, DO NOT INFER, before choosing the wording: whether fit.sd is the residual SD of the population being plotted or of the training residuals. If it is the former, RMSE sitting above SD is bias exactly (RMSE^2 = SD^2 + mean(residual)^2) and the metric cards and the band are two views of one fact worth saying so; if it is the latter, the band is a training-residual width laid over held-out rows and the copy must say THAT instead. MODEL-FLOW-019-T10's own userDecision resolved 'which SD' to residual SD for the Step 4 column and cites run_predictions as its source — confirm the same figure reaches this band rather than assuming the two agree.

WRITE THE METRIC CARDS' OWN SENTENCE IN THE VOCABULARY STEP 3 ALREADY USES. Step 3's acceptance criteria are ratios (RMSE vs SD, RMSE vs MAE, holdout vs test — MODEL-FLOW-019-T11/T12), so a reader who set criteria there should not have to translate. The cards today carry n and nothing else.

MOVE THE FEATURE-IMPORTANCE CAVEAT INTO A METHOD TABLE, not because this task needs it but because T14 does. T09 shipped three methods (impurity, coefficient, pls-coefficient) with the method NAMED beside the figures, and the per-method warning currently lives as prose in JSX. T14 adds a fourth whose caveats are different in kind (no cardinality bias, but correlated features split credit and the population permuted must be stated) — a METHOD_META entry per method, holding label and caveat, means T14 extends a table instead of writing a second copy of a sentence. T09's own findings 10 and 11 are the content.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08. All four named defects fixed. (1) The Actual vs Predicted detail no longer terminates mid-clause on a semicolon; it now also states the SD band is ONE constant width (this run's own residual SD), never a per-point bound -- audited from source first (artifact_service.py: `sd = residual.std(ddof=0)` over the SAME frame `rmse` is computed from), confirming `fit.sd` is the plotted population's own residual SD, so RMSE-above-SD is bias exactly. Wording avoids 'confidence'/'predictive interval' literally, per V29's own ban on those substrings appearing at all (proven in phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx). (2) Parity's detail and disambiguated headings were already shipped when this task started; left unchanged. (3) The residual-diagnostics copy now states it is computed over the FULL population, not the zoom window above -- proven structurally (V30, evaluation-contract.test.ts): `residuals`/`histogramBins`/`qq` depend only on `[fit]`/`[residuals]`, never `zoom`, while `visibleRows`/`tickFormatter` (feeding the two charts above) do depend on it -- a source-level proof of the split rather than a fragile UI-interaction test re-confirming the same array. (4) The per-fold table now states the expanding-window caveat (MODEL-FLOW-016-T03: fold 1 systematically trains on the least data), pointing at the Train rows column already present. METHOD_META (label + caveat per method) replaces the label-only METHOD_LABEL, sourced verbatim from this feature's own recorded findings 10 and 11 -- the table T14 needs to extend rather than write a second copy of a sentence. One additional fix beyond the four named defects: the metric cards now carry a derived RMSE-vs-SD sentence in Step 3's own ratio vocabulary (lib/acceptance-criteria.ts), computing bias as the exact mean of `residuals` already in scope rather than approximating it as `RMSE - SD` (a math error caught and corrected before merge -- the true identity is `bias = sqrt(RMSE^2 - SD^2)`, and reading the mean directly avoids even that).

tasks.title: Every chart owns the colours its legend claims
tasks.detail:
phase-5-evaluation.tsx hardcodes var(--foreground), var(--chart-1), var(--chart-2) and var(--destructive) into legend swatches for charts it does not own — a second source of truth for a colour, drifting silently on the first theme or density change, and invisible in every test that asserts on text. T13 already closed this for the parity chart by exporting PARITY_LEGEND from the component that draws the marks; this generalises that rather than inventing a pattern.

ONE LEGEND COMPONENT, THREE SWATCH SHAPES. The existing local LegendItem draws a square only, which cannot represent either of the two marks the parity chart actually has — a low-opacity dot and a dashed identity line. Extract it with a shape union (square, dot, dashed) and carry OPACITY, since a swatch more solid than the marks it explains misrepresents them at the densities this chart runs at (the largest real predictions.parquet measured in this system is 4,633 rows, MODEL-FLOW-017-T01).

THE DASHED SWATCH IS AN SVG LINE, NOT A CSS BORDER. border-dashed's dash length is browser-derived and cannot be matched to the chart's own strokeDasharray, so the swatch would advertise a different line than the one drawn.

EACH CHART EXPORTS ITS OWN ENTRIES, and the consumer renders what it is given. Actual vs Predicted and Residuals follow the parity chart's precedent; the strip component itself learns no colours.

NAME THE REFERENCE LINE 'Ideal (y = x)', NEVER 'Baseline'. In ML a baseline is a REFERENCE MODEL (mean predictor, persistence, last-value) and one could legitimately be plotted here — so that word announces a second series this chart deliberately does not draw. T13's own doc comment is explicit that the line is the identity line and not a fit, and MODEL-FLOW-004 deleted seededNoise, comparePoints and compareFit from this very step rather than let a chart carry a series whose provenance was unclear; a label is the same claim as a series.

MEANING IS NEVER CARRIED BY COLOUR ALONE — the two parity entries differ by SHAPE (points against a line), which is what makes the legend readable in greyscale and to a colour-blind reader. The +/-1/2/3 SD guidelines on the residual chart are the case where colour is doing the work today; state the multiplier in the label rather than relying on the swatch.

THE LEGEND MUST NOT EAT THE SQUARE. The parity chart's aspect-square wrapper is what makes the shared domain mean anything — a 45-degree line at 45 degrees on screen — so a legend strip added inside that wrapper silently un-squares it and every reading taken off the diagonal becomes wrong while looking correct. Legend and chart are siblings inside one width-bounded container; the aspect ratio belongs to the chart's own box.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08. All three charts now export their own LegendEntry[] (AVP_LEGEND, RESIDUAL_LEGEND, PARITY_LEGEND already existed) built from colour consts exported from the SAME file that draws the marks -- phase-5-evaluation.tsx's dead local `LegendItem` (5 hardcoded var(--chart-N) literals) is deleted; every legend strip now renders via the shared `ChartLegend`. V27 proven by importing the SAME exported constant a legend entry and its chart's JSX both bind to and asserting equality -- not a literal that could drift silently (evaluation-contract.test.ts). The parity chart's identity line already read 'Perfect Predictions (y = x)', never 'Baseline'; V31 proves it contains 'y = x', never 'baseline', and that its two entries differ by swatch SHAPE (dot vs dashed), not colour alone. The task's own premise that 'T13 already closed this by exporting PARITY_LEGEND' was checked and found FALSE -- T13 shipped no such export; it was added later, by a different task.

tasks.title: The parity plot's absence, and whether its axes and its points come from one read
tasks.detail:
TWO THINGS, BOTH ABOUT parityRange, both follow-ons to T13 rather than repairs of it.

(1) IT DISAPPEARS SILENTLY. The section renders behind a bare `parityDomain &&`, so a run whose ranges were not recorded shows nothing at all — no heading, no reason, no next action. Every other panel in this file states its own absence: feature importance names both real causes, the run states name the failure reason, MODEL-FLOW-016-T11 built three distinguishable scoring-phase states. This is the same three-facts discipline AC11 requires of an absent holdout figure and AC25 requires of an absent importance artifact, and the reason is identical — a blank cannot be told from a defect. Name which figure is missing, not merely that the chart is unavailable.

(2) THE AXES AND THE POINTS MAY NOT COME FROM ONE READ, AND THIS ONE MUST BE CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The chart takes `rows` from buildFitRows(fit.points, fit.sd) and `domain` from parityRange's own y-ranges. T13's own doc comment states the domain is deliberately the caller's full-frame range 'never derived from the rendered point set, so the axis does not shift if that set is ever decimated' — which is correct and is exactly why the pair needs verifying: if the two ever come from different responses, a point can fall outside the domain and be clipped by ifOverflow='hidden' with nothing on screen saying a point was dropped. CONFIRM FROM SOURCE that both fields arrive in one run_predictions response, and that MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS is the hard refusal T13 and MODEL-FLOW-004 both record rather than a downsample anywhere in the path. If it is a refusal, record that the pair is consistent BY CONSTRUCTION and add no guard — a redundant check would read as though someone had found a real inconsistency. If a decimation branch exists anywhere on this path, the clipping is reachable and the count must be stated the way DraftScatterResult's own 'N of M shown' disclosure already does for scatter.

MODEL-FLOW-017-T02's decimation is NOT the path in question and must not be reached for here: it keys LTTB on (timestamp, y_true), correct for a time series and wrong for a scatter, which MODEL-FLOW-017's own finding 5 records needs 2D grid binning. Step 5 reads the SINGLE-run endpoint, which has no decimation branch at all.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-08 (no code change needed -- already correct). (1) The absence branch states which figure is missing ('this run's prediction range wasn't recorded'), never rendering nothing; V28 proves it end to end. (2) Confirmed from source: `fit.points` and `parityRange` both come from ONE `run_predictions` response inside `fetchEvaluation` (a single `predRes` variable feeds both), and `MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS` is a hard `raise ValueError` in artifact_service.py with NO decimation branch on the single-run path -- so the pair is consistent BY CONSTRUCTION, and per the task's own instruction no guard was added (a redundant check would read as though a real inconsistency had been found). MODEL-FLOW-017-T02's LTTB decimation is a different endpoint (`run_predictions_batch`) not reached on this path, as the task itself warns.

tasks.title: Audit: the candidate overlay and the Step 5 time charts display a date range the plotted data does not have
tasks.detail:
REPRODUCE BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. A user-reported symptom is not a repro, and this task must not propose a fix until one exists: a named draft, a named run, and the two figures side by side -- the min/max timestamp read directly from that run's predictions.parquet, and the first/last tick the chart renders. Without that pair every hypothesis below is a guess about which of two numbers is wrong.

THE SYMPTOM, AS REPORTED 2026-09-08: the chart displays 21 Feb - 27 Feb while the data spans 25 Jan - 26 Jan. THE ARITHMETIC IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THIS TASK AND IT ALREADY ELIMINATES A WHOLE CLASS: the start moves +27 days, the end moves +32 days, and the span STRETCHES from about two days to seven. Because the two ends move by DIFFERENT amounts, this is not a constant offset -- timezone handling, DST, and UTC-versus-local Date parsing are all ruled out without running anything, since each shifts both ends by the same interval, and a seconds-versus-milliseconds unit error is ruled out because scaling an epoch moves a date by decades rather than weeks. A shift COMBINED WITH a stretch leaves two families: the axis and the points come from different reads, or the series on screen is not the series the reader believes it is.

FIVE RANKED HYPOTHESES, DISPROOF FIRST. H0 (cheapest, run it before the others): the REFERENCE is wrong rather than the chart -- 25 Jan - 26 Jan may have been read from the dataset artifact rather than from the run's own predictions.parquet, which need not share a span. Disproof: read min/max timestamp from that predictions file directly; if it reads February, the chart is right and the defect is upstream in the artifact.

H1, AND THE ONE WITH DOCUMENTED PRECEDENT IN THIS LEDGER: the overlay is plotting a run belonging to ANOTHER DRAFT. mpCompareRunIdsAtom is never pruned or reset per draft -- MODEL-FLOW-019-T08 part 3 records exactly this, and RunParamsPanel handles it by intersecting the atom against the current draft's run list before every read, so its own count and Step 4's table can never disagree. If candidate-overlay-chart.tsx reads the RAW atom instead, a stale id from a previous draft or session fetches predictions for a different dataset, which explains the shift AND the stretch together rather than one or the other. Disproof: grep the file for mpCompareRunIdsAtom and check whether the read is intersected; if it is, H1 dies.

H2: the axis domain and the plotted points come from different reads -- the same class MODEL-FLOW-019-T18 verified as SAFE for the parity chart (one predRes carries both fit.points and parityRange, and MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS is a hard refusal with no decimation branch on that path) but which was never checked for the TIME charts or the overlay. If a domain arrives from selectedDataset's own time range, or from whichever series resolved first, ticks can sit entirely outside the data and the points are then clipped by ifOverflow with nothing on screen saying so. Disproof: log the domain passed to XAxis beside min/max of the rows actually rendered.

H3: multiple series merged by ARRAY INDEX rather than by timestamp. MODEL-FLOW-017-T02's LTTB decimation is keyed on (timestamp, y_true) and runs PER SERIES, so two candidates decimate to different timestamps; zipping them by index misaligns x from y, and rows with no matching key drop out, leaving the surviving series' axis to describe both. Disproof: reduce the comparison to ONE run -- if the dates correct themselves, the fault is in the merge or in which runs were fetched; if they do not, the merge is exonerated.

H4: tickFormatter consumes Recharts' second argument. Recharts passes (value, index), so a formatter that uses index -- or looks up rows[index] against an array that was decimated after the fact -- prints labels unrelated to the x it sits under. Disproof: remove the formatter and render the raw value; an epoch in January under a February label proves H4 outright.

CHECK BOTH SURFACES, AND DO NOT ASSUME THEY SHARE A CAUSE. The report names candidate-overlay-chart.tsx, but phase-5-evaluation.tsx's Actual vs Predicted and Residuals charts read a DIFFERENT source (one run_predictions response via fetchEvaluation) than the overlay does, and they are joined by EVAL_SYNC_ID while the overlay is not. Two surfaces showing one wrong range may be one bug upstream or two bugs that happen to rhyme; establish which before writing a fix in either. If only the overlay is wrong, H1 and H3 rise and H2 falls, since the Step 5 charts' single-read path was already verified under T18.

EVERY RUN IS A BREADCRUMB: record each disproof and what it ruled out, and re-check any surviving hypothesis against ALL of them -- notably against the +27/+32/x3.5 arithmetic above, which any real root cause must explain in full rather than approximately.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-09 (no code change needed -- the charts were already correct; the reference was wrong). REPRO, against live infra (client 3000, backend 4000, FastAPI 8000, MinIO 9000, Postgres 5432): draft 8d9370cc-53e5-495a-9d0a-adf166f98bbc, run d1520372-e7b6-4233-a585-9f97bb57f364 (created 2026-09-08, the symptom's own report date), dataset f7d2d259 'DatasetM2'. Dataset GOLD spans 2026-01-25 08:05 to 2026-02-27 08:00 (8350 rows @ 5 min, read directly from data_gold.parquet in MinIO). The run's splitSpec: {ratio: 0.8, method: chronological, cut_timestamp: '2026-02-21 12:55:00', test_rows: 1670, source_rows: 8350}. The run's own predictions.parquet, read directly from MinIO: 2026-02-21 12:55:00 to 2026-02-27 08:00:00, 1670 rows. The parquet's min equals cut_timestamp TO THE MINUTE; its max equals the dataset's last row TO THE MINUTE; 1670 is exactly 20% of 8350. The chart renders precisely the run's own test split. Second run, independent confirmation: draft af80fbfe.../run f2d979a1..., ratio 0.7, cut_timestamp 2026-02-18 15:20:00, parquet min identical, 2505 rows = 30% of 8350. H0 CONFIRMED: the reference, not the chart, was wrong. Traced to MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = 200 (apps/python/schemas/preprocess.py:33) -- 200 rows x 5 min from 2026-01-25 08:05 ends 2026-01-26 00:45, which is the dataset preview's 200-row HEAD CUT, not the data's end. The chart plots the split's TAIL. The full arithmetic the task demanded: start '+27d' is the chronological TRAIN fraction (80% of a 33-day span is 26.4 days from 25 Jan, landing on 21 Feb) -- a split point, not a shift. End '+32d' is not a move at all: 27 Feb IS the dataset's last row: it read as +32 only because the reference's '26 Jan' was the preview's 200th row, never the data's true end. The '3.5x stretch' is a 6-day test window compared against a ~17-hour preview head. H1-H4 each disproved from source: H1 (stale mpCompareRunIdsAtom leaking another draft's run) DEAD -- candidate-overlay-chart.tsx's CandidateOverlayChart reads no atom at all, props only; both call sites in phase-4-model-selection.tsx (job path and standalone path) intersect the atom against their own run list before it ever reaches the chart, same as run-params-panel.tsx's RunParamsPanel; resetWizardAtom also clears the atom on every draft resume. H2 (axis domain and points from different reads) DEAD -- every chart uses domain=['dataMin','dataMax'] computed from the SAME rows it plots, and the server returns no time-domain field at all (only y_true/y_pred min/max), so no second source for the x axis exists. H3 (series merged by array index) DEAD -- buildOverlayRows merges via a Map keyed on the ISO timestamp string. H4 (tickFormatter consumes Recharts' index argument) DEAD -- pickTimeFormat returns a single-parameter (t: number) => string, and both time charts' Props narrow tickFormatter to that exact signature. Both surfaces (the Step 4 overlay and the Step 5 Actual-vs-Predicted/Residual charts) show the same window for the same reason -- both plot the run's test split -- not two bugs that rhyme. V32/V33/V34 closed with a new regression suite: apps/client/app/(default)/models/create/components/pipeline/__tests__/chart-time-axis.test.tsx (8 passing cases). Two related-but-separate findings surfaced during this audit and were filed as their own tasks rather than folded in here, since neither explains this report's arithmetic: T21 (Date.parse on a zone-less, space-separated timestamp) and T22 (an orphaned test file, run-comparison-panel.test.tsx, importing a component that does not exist in the tree). A genuine product gap surfaced too -- the dataset's validation holdout (27-31 Jan) has no per-row predictions and is never shown anywhere, which is the actual source of the user's January expectation -- filed as T20.

tasks.title: Show the dataset's validation holdout as its own actual-vs-predicted chart, alongside the test split
tasks.detail:
USER REQUEST, following T19's audit: in Model Selection's overlay (candidate-overlay-chart.tsx), show a SECOND chart, same layout, plotting the dataset's validation holdout (actual vs predicted) beside the existing test-split overlay. T19 found the two windows are genuinely different and both real -- the holdout is 27-31 Jan, the run's own test split is 21-27 Feb -- and confusing them for one another is what produced T19's report in the first place.

DO NOT BUILD A NEW PERSISTENCE MECHANISM. Per-row holdout predictions ALREADY exist for CV runs, via infrastructure this ledger already shipped: MODEL-FLOW-016-T07's score-mode container (images/trainer/app/pipelines/score.py, triggered by ModelRunScoreAuthorizedService.triggerScoringService) scores model.joblib against the dataset's validation holdout and uploads the resulting {timestamp,y_true,y_pred} frame AS predictions.parquet, so a scored CV run's own predictionsKey IS its holdout series (verified live: runs f8ec969e-f13a-4176-8990-ad59b17fd457 and 1a72bda1-9d9a-4be1-a4a5-e5efc640ea39 both carry exactly this -- 1153 rows, 2026-01-27 to 2026-01-31, matching validate_ready.parquet's own span). MODEL-FLOW-019-T15 already wired the READ side of this for Step 5: lib/metric-source.ts's cvScoringPhaseOf/populationOf/populationLabel/populationAxisLabel/populationTitle, consumed by phase-5-evaluation.tsx, already switch the SAME Actual-vs-Predicted/Residual charts between 'test split' and 'validation holdout' labelling depending on the run's own scoring phase, with a working triggerScoring() action. A second holdoutPredictionsKey Prisma column would duplicate a mechanism that already works -- do not add one.

THE ACTUAL GAP, AND THE BLOCKING PRODUCT QUESTION THIS TASK MUST NOT GUESS AT: triggerScoringService explicitly REFUSES a non-CV run (model-run-score.authorized.service.ts, 'is not a Cross-Validation run -- its holdout score is already computed during training'). That refusal is TRUE for the AGGREGATE (a non-CV run's holdoutMetrics is already populated inline, via _score_holdout_if_present in images/trainer/app/pipelines/__init__.py) and FALSE for the PER-ROW FRAME (that same function computes it, then discards it: 'holdout_metrics, _ = score_holdout(...)'). The overwhelming majority of runs, including the draft T19 audited (8d9370cc.../d1520372..., algorithm=ols, not CV), are non-CV, so a chart for THEM needs this refusal deliberately relaxed -- a real product decision, not a bug fix. Ask before building: does score-mode extend to non-CV runs, or does this chart exist only for CV runs (where it already works via the existing trigger + population toggle)? Per CLAUDE.md's conflict rule: state the conflict, then follow the explicit user request once given -- do not silently relax the guard and do not silently refuse the request either.

A SEPARATE, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME AUDIT: candidate-overlay-chart.tsx (the Step 4 overlay) has ZERO population awareness -- for an already-scored CV candidate it plots holdout data captioned as an ordinary test-split comparison today, live, for the 2 real runs above. This is the SAME conflation T19 audited, on a surface T19's audit did not reach, and needs fixing regardless of how the non-CV question resolves: the overlay must read cvScoringPhaseOf/populationOf per candidate and caption accordingly, the same way phase-5-evaluation.tsx already does.

IF non-CV extension is approved: relax triggerScoringService's cvFoldsKey gate (or add a parallel path) so a non-CV SUCCEEDED run can also be scored into its own holdout predictions.parquet-equivalent -- reusing score.py/scoreUploadUrlsService/scoreCompleteService's existing plumbing, deciding the object-key question (same predictions.parquet slot vs a second key) only after confirming a non-CV run's predictionsKey is not already something else load-bearing. Then widen the overlay and Step 4/5 to offer scoring and show the holdout chart for any SUCCEEDED run, not only CV ones.

IF CV-only: build the second overlay chart only for candidates where cvScoringPhaseOf(candidate) === 'scored', with the existing absence-state pattern (T18 part 1 / AC11 / AC25's three facts: which figure is missing, why, next action) for every other candidate -- 'not-cv' (no dataset holdout path exists for this run), 'awaiting-scoring'/'scoring' (trigger exists, not yet run), never a blank. Either way: each chart must NAME its own window (test split vs validation holdout) via populationLabel/populationTitle from lib/metric-source.ts, never inline prose -- that file's own doc comment states the Holdout-vs-Validate wording is a deliberate one-line change point, not a string to respell per caller.
tasks.result:
IN PROGRESS 2026-09-09. THE BLOCKING PRODUCT QUESTION WAS ASKED (AskUserQuestion, not guessed) and answered: EXTEND TO NON-CV. A migration adding ModelTrainingRun.holdoutPredictionsKey (packages/prisma/prisma/migrations/20260909100000_model_flow_019_t20_holdout_predictions_key) was already applied to the dev DB at session start, uncommitted, with zero downstream code reading or writing it -- inert until this pass, not evidence of a prior decision on its own, but its own doc comment's reasoning (a non-CV run's predictionsKey is load-bearing, a CV run's is not) matched the answer once asked.

BACKEND (DONE, tested, image rebuilt): triggerScoringService's cvFoldsKey-only refusal removed -- any SUCCEEDED run may now trigger scoring. scoreClaimService returns isCvRun (Boolean(run.cvFoldsKey)) so score.py knows which filename to upload: predictions.parquet for a CV run (unchanged, it has no test split to lose), holdout_predictions.parquet (NEW) for a non-CV run (its predictions.parquet already holds the TEST split -- scoring must never overwrite it, confirmed live-checked before writing any code). scoreUploadUrlsService is now run-aware (was a fixed literal) and scoreCompleteService writes predictionsKey OR holdoutPredictionsKey, never both, keyed off which filename was actually uploaded.
