ScoreCompleteSchema widened to the two-literal union with a matching refine. holdout_predictions.parquet registered through the full mirror set (images/trainer/app/artifacts.py, apps/python's object_store.py + _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS, artifact-keys.ts's RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES, MIRRORS.md entry 8 added) -- the exact 3-copy discipline entries 4 and 7 already established. Trainer image rebuilt and bumped 1.0.7->1.0.8 (score.py's own upload filename changed -- same class of bump as 1.0.5, not the purely-additive 1.0.3/1.0.7 shape), verified in-image via docker run --entrypoint python: HOLDOUT_PREDICTIONS_FILENAME imports cleanly and run_scoring's isCvRun branch is present in the built image, not just the source tree. packages/prisma rebuilt (pnpm db:generate + tsc --build) so the new column's TS types actually reach apps/backend. model-run-score.authorized.service.spec.ts updated: the old 'refuses a NON-CV run' test replaced with one proving it now spawns; new coverage for isCvRun on both run kinds, the per-run-kind upload allowlist (including the CV run still refusing the NEW filename and vice versa), and a non-CV score writing holdoutPredictionsKey while leaving predictionsKey untouched. 22/22 passing. tsc --noEmit and eslint clean on every backend file touched.

CLIENT (PARTIAL -- the smaller finding closed, the actual feature not yet visible to a user): ModelTrainingRun.holdoutPredictionsKey added client-side (services/model-draft.ts) and every affected test fixture updated for it (5 files). Separately, and explicitly called out in this task's own detail as needed 'regardless of how the non-CV question resolves': candidate-overlay-chart.tsx had ZERO population awareness -- it capped every candidate's series as an ordinary comparison with no source named, which for an already-scored CV candidate (2 real runs in the dev DB, confirmed live in T19's audit) means holdout data was captioned identically to a test-split comparison, the exact conflation this whole feature exists to prevent. Fixed: OverlaySeries now extends CvScoringSignals (cvFoldsKey/predictionsKey/scoringContainerId -- both real callers' underlying types already carry these, so neither call site needed a change), and every series' legend label now carries its own population via cvScoringPhaseOf/populationOf/populationAxisLabel from lib/metric-source.ts (never inline prose, per this task's own requirement) -- '<algorithm> (Test)' or '<algorithm> (Validate)' per series, so a mixed CV/non-CV group is visibly mixed rather than silently implied to be one comparison. New regression test proves this with one CV-scored and one non-CV candidate in the same chart. 9/9 chart-time-axis tests passing (8 pre-existing + 1 new).

NOT YET BUILT, why this stays in_progress: the actual second chart (a holdout actual-vs-predicted view for a non-CV run) has no UI anywhere -- no 'Score holdout' trigger surfaced for a non-CV run in Step 4/5, no read path for holdoutPredictionsKey (getDraftRunPredictionsService/getDraftRunPredictionsBatchService still only ever read predictionsKey, so even a successfully-scored non-CV run's holdout series is unreachable from the client today), and no second chart component. This is real, substantial remaining work (a new/widened read endpoint, a scoring-trigger affordance, a second chart), scoped and sequenced but deliberately not started this pass -- advisor guidance was not to run this and the MODEL-FLOW-021/T22 component-recovery work in the same pass, and T20(a) was prioritized as what the user actually asked to continue.

Pre-existing, unrelated to this task, found while running the full client suite: run-params-panel.test.tsx (7 failures) and phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx (3 failures) are broken by the OTHER uncommitted work already in this working tree at session start (run-params-panel.tsx's own 549-line uncommitted diff) -- confirmed by diffing this session's one-line fixture addition against each failing file, not by anything this task changed. Not fixed here; flagged so a future reader does not mistake it for regression from this pass.

TWO FOLLOW-UP FIXES LANDED IN A SECOND PASS THE SAME DAY, both caught by advisor review before being reported done. FIRST (real, fixed): holdoutAbsenceOf (client)/holdoutAbsenceFor (backend) still gated 'not-scored-yet' on cvFoldsKey -- a non-CV run with a confirmed holdout-bearing dataset and no figure fell through to 'not-recorded', defined elsewhere as a defect claim, even though the trigger this task just widened makes it actionable. Fixed both copies to key off datasetHasHoldout alone; tests updated (44/44 backend, 23/23 client), schema.prisma's holdoutPredictionsKey comment corrected to stop implying CV runs use it too. SECOND (noted, not fixed -- not yet reachable): candidate-overlay-chart.tsx's new populationOfEntry calls populationOf(cvScoringPhaseOf(candidate)), which returns 'test-split' unconditionally for any non-CV run today -- correct ONLY because nothing serves holdoutPredictionsKey to the client yet. The moment the read endpoint in 'NOT YET BUILT' above lands, a non-CV run's holdout series will caption as '(Test)', reintroducing the exact conflation this pass just fixed from the CV side. Whoever builds that read path must widen populationOf's own source (today it is a pure function of CvScoringPhase, which cannot see holdoutPredictionsKey) before wiring it in -- flagged here so it is not rediscovered by reading the bug report a second time.

COMPLETED 2026-09-09, SECOND PASS (the read + chart half). A READ-SIDE ALLOWLIST THE FIRST PASS MISSED WAS THE REAL TRAP, and it was found by checking rather than by assuming: registering holdout_predictions.parquet in _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS made it WRITABLE, but artifact_service.py's run_predictions AND _decimated_run_predictions each hard-gated on the basename being exactly predictions.parquet, so score-mode's upload would have landed in object storage and then been refused by name on every read. Widened both to a new _READABLE_PREDICTION_FILENAMES frozenset, deliberately its own set beside the write allowlist: one gates what a CONTAINER may write, the other what a reader will parse as a series. Both filenames carry the identical {timestamp,y_true,y_pred} shape -- WHICH population the rows describe is the caller's fact to state, never inferred from a filename. 3 new python tests (11/11 in that file); the 3 pre-existing get_run_manifest failures in test_artifact_service.py were confirmed to pre-date this work by stashing the change and re-running.

BACKEND: getDraftRunPredictionsService and getDraftRunPredictionsBatchService take an optional `population` ('test' | 'holdout'), defaulting to 'test' so every existing caller is byte-identical in behaviour; exposed as an optional query param on both routes (PredictionPopulationEnum). WHICH COLUMN backs each population is a PER-RUN question and now lives in exactly one place, apps/backend/src/lib/run-prediction-source.ts's predictionKeyFor: a CV run's predictionsKey IS its holdout (unchanged since -016-T07) while a non-CV run's is its test split, so `predictionsKey` alone answers neither question and cvFoldsKey is what disambiguates it. The dangerous case is pinned by its own test: predictionKeyFor(cvRun, 'test') returns null rather than handing back a holdout series that would plot as a plausible-looking test split. 6 new lib tests; the batch spec's `select` assertion updated for the widened column read. The /score route's ApiOperation, which still described the deleted CV-only refusal, was corrected.

CLIENT: Step 4 now issues TWO batch fetches per path (job and standalone) and renders the holdout overlay BESIDE the test-split one, never merged -- T19's own finding was that the two windows are genuinely different data and confusing them is what produced that report. CandidateOverlayChart takes an EXPLICIT `population` prop; the per-series derivation added in this feature's first pass was REVERSED because it is wrong for exactly the case this task adds -- populationOf(cvScoringPhaseOf(nonCvRun)) is 'test-split' unconditionally, so a non-CV run's holdout series would have captioned as Test, which is this feature's own failure mode arriving through a derivation that looks careful. That closes the gap the first pass explicitly flagged as open. The holdout chart renders NOTHING when no candidate in the group has been scored, rather than an empty axis implying a measurement nobody took. AC2 is honoured at group level by lib/metric-source.ts's new holdoutGroupMissingRateText, which reports differs-by-candidate rather than printing the first candidate's rate over a mixed group. chart-time-axis.test.tsx's useCandidatePredictions mock was made population-AWARE -- a blind mock fed the same test series to both charts, staging the very conflation these tests exist to catch.

LIVE VERIFICATION (real running FastAPI on :8000, not a fake): POSTing a holdout_predictions.parquet key now passes the name guard and fails only at object lookup (NoSuchKey), predictions.parquet behaves identically as before, and model.joblib is still refused BY NAME with the widened message naming both allowed files. That is end-to-end proof of the read side against the running service.

NOT LIVE-VERIFIED, STATED PLAINLY: no non-CV run has actually been scored end to end through a real container since this landed, so the full chain (trigger -> score.py writes holdout_predictions.parquet -> scoreCompleteService records holdoutPredictionsKey -> Step 4 draws the second chart) has not been observed on real data. Two deployment facts gate that and are recorded so they are not rediscovered: the backend must be RESTARTED for the 1.0.8 image bump to take effect (resolveDigest pins the image at BOOT, MODEL-FLOW-016-T07), and only runs scored AFTER that restart can carry the new artifact.

ALSO NOT BUILT, deliberately out of this task's scope: no UI affordance yet OFFERS scoring for a non-CV run. Step 5's existing trigger is still reached only through the CV awaiting-scoring branch, so today a non-CV run's holdout series can be produced by calling the endpoint but not by clicking anything. The gate for such a control is already derivable and should NOT be invented fresh: holdoutAbsence === 'not-scored-yet' is exactly the actionable state, and this feature's own second pass already made holdoutAbsenceOf/holdoutAbsenceFor report it for non-CV runs.

REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED AFTER THIS TASK WAS FIRST CLOSED (commit 7ff11fb). Giving the single-run predictions endpoint a population parameter defaulting to 'test' was NOT backward-compatible: predictionKeyFor(cvRun, 'test') is null by design, so Step 5's fetchEvaluation -- which still called predictions(draftId, runId) with no population, and early-returns only for an UNSCORED CV run -- turned every SCORED CV run's evaluation into a 404 reading 'recorded no test predictions artifact'. Two such runs exist in the dev database. Fixed by deriving cvFoldsKey ? 'holdout' : 'test' at that one call site, which resolves to the key the endpoint read unconditionally before T20. Deriving is right there and wrong in CandidateOverlayChart, for the reason that component's own comment gives. Three new spec cases pin the asymmetry from both sides. THE LESSON: no test covered the single-run read path for a CV run, so widening a shared endpoint's contract shipped a silent break in a surface this task never edited -- a defaulted parameter is a behaviour change for every caller that omits it.

tasks.title: Date.parse on a zone-less, space-separated timestamp reads as LOCAL time in two chart-row builders
tasks.detail: Found while auditing T19, explicitly NOT the cause of T19's report (it shifts both ends of a window by the same interval -- the exact class T19's own +27/+32 arithmetic ruled out before anything was run -- so it is filed separately rather than folded into that close). lib/monitoring.ts:65 (buildMonitoringRows) and candidate-overlay-chart.tsx:76ish (buildOverlayRows) both call Date.parse(p.timestamp) on the server's own wire form, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss' (artifact_service.py's ts.isoformat(sep=' ')) -- a space-separated, zone-less string that is NOT an ECMA-262 standard date format. V8 (and most engines) parse this as LOCAL time rather than UTC, so the SAME timestamp renders at a different wall-clock position depending on the browser's timezone, and there is no NaN guard on either call site if a future format change ever makes the string unparseable. Fix: parse explicitly and consistently (e.g. treat the server's wire form as UTC, matching how it was serialized, or normalize to an ISO 8601 string with a T separator and Z/offset before Date.parse), and add a guard for the NaN case rather than silently plotting an Invalid Date as epoch 0/NaN.
tasks.result: COMPLETED 2026-09-09. Added lib/monitoring.ts's parseServerTimestamp (exported, HAS_TZ regex passthrough for already-zoned strings, else space->T + Z appended before Date.parse) and used it at both call sites: buildMonitoringRows (monitoring.ts:65-ish, now flatMap so an unparseable point is dropped rather than plotted at epoch 0/NaN) and candidate-overlay-chart.tsx's buildOverlayRows (imports parseServerTimestamp from lib/monitoring, `continue`s past a NaN point). No behavior change for already-zoned strings (tests use full ISO+Z fixtures and stay green -- monitoring.test.ts + chart-time-axis.test.tsx, 18 total). tsc --noEmit clean on both touched files.

tasks.title: Orphaned test file imports a component that no longer exists in the tree
tasks.detail: Found while auditing T19. app/(default)/models/create/components/pipeline/training-config/__tests__/run-comparison-panel.test.tsx imports `{ RunComparisonPanel } from '../run-comparison-panel'` -- that file does not exist anywhere in the tree. candidate-overlay-chart.tsx's own OverlaySeries doc comment (MODEL-FLOW-021-T02) also cites 'Step 3's RunComparisonPanel' as a second consumer that does not exist. Either the component was renamed/merged (into run-params-panel.tsx, which now owns the compare-checkbox behaviour the doc comment describes) and the test + doc comment are stale, or the component was deleted before being committed and the test should be deleted with it. Resolve which, then delete the stale test/comment or restore the missing component -- currently this test file cannot even be collected by vitest without an import-resolution failure.

acceptance_criteria: No figure appears anywhere in Step 4 without its source — test split, validation holdout, or CV fold estimate — being visible.
A holdout figure is never shown without its own missing rate.
Ranking prefers the holdout metric where every ranked row has one, falls back to the test split otherwise, and states which was used for the ordering.
A mixed set is never sorted as though one column held one kind of number.
A candidate with no metric — failed, running, or holdout-skipped — keeps its row and its reason, and where it sorts is a stated rule rather than a default.
The metric picker shares its vocabulary with Step 5's rather than declaring a second one.
MODEL-FLOW-013-T11's phase grouping survives the table.
Selection still writes selectedRunId, bestRunId is still untouched, and the override is still reachable from the table.
Model Selection still creates no Model row and adds no ModelDraft column.
Test and holdout figures are both shown by default, in separate columns, never merged and never behind a toggle.
An absent holdout figure distinguishes 'this dataset has no holdout' from 'scoring failed' from 'not scored yet' — three facts with three different next actions, never one blank cell.
Every threshold names the metric source it applies to, and is evaluated only against a figure of that source.
A candidate missing a threshold is marked, never hidden, never barred from selection, and never blocks Save Model.
A threshold whose source is absent for a candidate reads as 'not evaluated' rather than as a failure.
A threshold's comparator is fixed by its metric's own direction — a criterion that admits worse models cannot be expressed.
Thresholds add no ModelDraft column; the step still holds selectedRunId as its only server state.

AC22. Feature importance is read from the fitted estimator inside the trainer and written as its own artifact naming the METHOD it measured; an algorithm with no importance to read writes nothing at all -- no placeholder, no empty array.
AC23. The Evaluation table lists the top 10 by importance and states the total feature count and what the remaining features carry in aggregate, so a top-10 list is never mistaken for the whole set.
AC24. A target-derived feature is flagged where it ranks, read from the run's own manifest and never re-derived client-side.
AC25. A run predating this feature reads as 'not recorded for this run'; nothing is reconstructed by loading a model artifact outside the trainer image.

AC26. No recommended feature count is displayed unless a measurement on this system's own data supports it. The cumulative importance share and the observations-per-feature figure ARE displayed, as arithmetic over figures the run already recorded.
AC27. A linear fit's coefficients are not ranked as importances unless the scaling that makes them comparable is recorded and stated.
AC28. AMENDED 2026-09-08 by T12. A criterion compares two figures of the same run with a USER-CHOSEN operator and no numeric value. The operator is free; the PAIR is not.

AC29. AMENDED 2026-09-08 by T12 — the rule moves from the comparator to the pair. A pair whose order is fixed by algebra (RMSE against MAE, RMSE against residual SD) is not offerable in EITHER direction, because one direction fires always and the other never.
AC30. AMENDED 2026-09-08 by T12. A pair spanning two unit classes cannot be expressed. Non-negativity no longer gates offerability — that gate existed for division and is withdrawn with it.
AC31. AMENDED 2026-09-08 by T12. No numeric value is typed anywhere. BOTH operands' own values from the draft's most recent SUCCEEDED run are displayed, with whether the comparison currently holds.

AC34. R2 is admissible as a COMPARISON operand and remains inadmissible as a ratio operand — a comparison is well defined across negative values, a ratio is not, and negative R2 is the norm in this system rather than an edge case.
AC35. A cv-fold-estimate is never an operand. A CV run's fold mean is refused AT THE OPERAND rather than reached through the operand-absence path, because the value is present rather than missing.
AC36. Within one criterion, either both operands pin a source or neither does. A pinned figure is never compared against a run-resolved one, whose population varies by run shape.
AC37. WITHDRAWN 2026-09-08 by T12 — no division remains, so a zero denominator is unreachable.
AC38. A criterion is stored in canonical form. A mirrored duplicate (A < B beside B > A) cannot be added, and the already-added filter compares canonical forms rather than raw fields.
AC39. Exactly two operators are offered. Strict and non-strict are not distinguished, and equality is not claimed to be reachable.
AC40. R2 >= 0 is offered as a checkbox with no input field. It is the one structural constant and is not a typed threshold.
AC41. Every Step 5 surface names its population from ONE derivation. A scored CV run reads holdout in all four chart panels and the banner, not only in the residual-diagnostics section.
AC42. The population type is derived from MetricSource rather than declared beside it, and a new scoring phase fails at compile rather than defaulting to the test-split label.
AC43. Each chart states what it plots as a definition, which population it plots, and the failure mode it detects that no sibling panel detects.
AC44. The +/-1 SD band is stated as one constant residual-SD width. The words predictive interval and confidence appear nowhere near it.
AC45. A panel computed over the full frame while its neighbours are zoomed says so.
AC46. A panel that cannot render names which figure is missing. The parity plot never disappears without a stated reason.
AC47. A legend swatch's colour and dash come from the chart that draws them; no consumer hardcodes a CSS variable for a chart it does not own.
AC48. No legend entry distinguishes itself by colour alone.
AC49. The parity chart's reference line is named as the identity line and never as a baseline or a fit.
AC50. Every time-axis chart in this pipeline renders ticks drawn from the same read as the points it plots. A chart never labels a span its data does not occupy.

AC51. A run id that does not belong to the current draft is never fetched or plotted. Every read of the compare set is intersected against the draft's own run list, in every consumer, not only in RunParamsPanel.
AC52. When a point falls outside the rendered domain it is disclosed rather than clipped silently.

verification.description: PROVE THE SOURCES CANNOT BE CONFLATED: render a set where one candidate has a holdout score and another does not, and assert each figure names its own source and the two never share a column. A set where every candidate has the same source would pass against a table that labels nothing.

Assert a holdout figure is never rendered without its missing rate — including the case where the rate itself is null on a legacy artifact, which must read as 'not recorded' rather than being omitted, the honest-legacy-null pattern MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 established.

PROVE THE NULL ORDERING IS THE STATED ONE: rank a set containing a FAILED candidate, a running one, and a holdout-skipped one, and assert each lands where the rule says AND keeps its reason visible. Ranking a set of complete candidates cannot distinguish a defined rule from an accident of the sort implementation.

Change the selected metric columns and confirm the sort follows, and that deselecting down to one metric is still refused — the guard Step 5's own picker already carries, verified here rather than assumed to have come along with the vocabulary.

Once MODEL-FLOW-016-T08 lands, rank a set where every candidate has a real holdout score and confirm the ordering uses it — the claim T03 makes, unverifiable until a holdout figure exists at all (finding 2). Until then this item stays pending rather than being marked satisfied by the fallback path.

Render one candidate per absent-holdout reason and assert each reads differently. All three collapsing to a dash would pass any weaker check while telling a user nothing about which of three unrelated situations they are in.

COMPLETED 2026-09-07 by MODEL-FLOW-019-T07. Proven at two levels: lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts's own 'not-evaluated is never fail' block (a run with no holdout entry, an entry with a null field, an empty candidate set, and a cv-fold-estimate source all read 'not-evaluated') and phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx's 'reads Not evaluated rather than failed when the threshold source is absent' case, exercised through the rendered table against a run with holdoutAbsence: 'no-dataset-holdout' -- the shape every real run in this system is in today.

COMPLETED 2026-09-07 by MODEL-FLOW-019-T07. Proven at two levels: lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts's 'source-bound, never cross-read' case and phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx's 'evaluates a test-sourced and a holdout-sourced threshold on the SAME metric independently' case, both using T03's own recorded shape (test 0.42, holdout 0.81) and confirming a strict test-sourced ceiling fails while a lenient holdout-sourced one on the same metric passes, in the same render.

COMPLETED 2026-09-07 by MODEL-FLOW-019-T07. AcceptanceCriterion has no comparator field -- {metric, source, value} only, asserted directly in lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts -- so a criterion admitting worse models cannot be constructed. comparatorSymbol's own two cases prove the render-time half: rmse/mae render <=, r2 renders >=, both derived from lib/metric-ranking.ts's existing RANK_DIRECTION rather than a caller-supplied choice.

AMENDED 2026-09-08 by T12 — this item's own T11-era completion is superseded, not deleted: it proved a pair was ORIENTED, and the rule is now that the pair is ABSENT. PROVE THE ALGEBRAICALLY-ORDERED PAIR IS UNREACHABLE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: assert RMSE against MAE and RMSE against residual SD are absent from the picker entirely, in either operand order. Asserting only that 'RMSE < MAE' is rejected would pass against an implementation that still offers 'RMSE > MAE', which fires on every run that will ever exist. Proven: offerablePairs() output is asserted as a full SET, and rmse/mae + rmse/sd are each asserted absent in BOTH operand orders (lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts).

PROVE SD'S SOURCE BITES: render a non-CV run beside a SCORED CV run and assert their SD cells name DIFFERENT populations — test split for the first, holdout for the second, since score.py wrote the holdout under the same predictionsKey. Two non-CV runs would pass against a column that tags nothing. COMPLETED 2026-09-08 by MODEL-FLOW-019-T10. Proven at the unit level (lib/residual-sd.test.ts's 'population differs by run shape' block: a non-CV run reads test-split, a SCORED CV run reads holdout, source differs between them) and end to end (__tests__/phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx's 'renders a non-CV run's SD under Test and a SCORED CV run's SD under Validate', two distinct figures each printed exactly once).

Render one run per null-SD cause — an unscored CV run, a run predating the predictions endpoint, and a run whose object prefix was reclaimed by MODEL-FLOW-011's sweeper — and assert the three read differently. All three collapsing to an em dash would pass any weaker check while telling a reader nothing about which of three unrelated situations they are in, or what to do next. COMPLETED 2026-09-08 by MODEL-FLOW-019-T10. Proven at the unit level (lib/residual-sd.test.ts's three-cause block, including a pairwise-distinctness assertion) and end to end (__tests__/phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx's 'reads three different reasons for three different null causes': an awaiting-scoring CV run, a predictionsKey-null legacy run, and a batch item carrying its own error each read a different string).

Assert a ratio with one absent operand reads 'not evaluated' and never 'fail', for BOTH absences (left missing, right missing) — two operands give two ways to be absent where MODEL-FLOW-019-T07's single-operand threshold had one, so checking a single direction leaves half the rule unverified. COMPLETED 2026-09-08 by MODEL-FLOW-019-T11. lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts's 'not-evaluated is never fail' block asserts both absence directions (left operand's source absent; right operand's field null though its source exists) plus the SD-specific absence (residualSd null on a surface like Step 3's own preview) and a zero-denominator guard -- and the row-level rendering is proven end to end in __tests__/phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx.

AMENDED 2026-09-08 by T12 — the same single-derivation rule, over two operand values instead of one ratio. Assert the values shown beside a criterion come from the same evaluation the table's own verdict does, not a second read. Two derivations of one comparison is how a row marked fail comes to display values that look like they pass. Proven: evaluateCriterion() is the one derivation both the verdict and any displayed operand value read -- no caller computes a second reading (core-config.tsx's preview and phase-4-model-selection.tsx's RowCriteriaMarks both call the same function).

PROVE R2 IS ADMISSIBLE AS A COMPARISON: assert holdout_R2 against test_R2 is offerable and evaluates correctly with BOTH operands NEGATIVE — a fixture with positive R2 would pass against an implementation still carrying the ratio form's own sign refusal, and negative R2 is the norm here (a real -1,110,858 is on record). Proven: holdout R2 vs test R2 is offerable, and evaluated correctly with BOTH operands negative (test -1,110,858, holdout -4.2) in lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts.

PROVE THE SOURCE-PINNING RULE BITES: assert a pinned operand cannot be paired with a run-resolved one (holdout MAE against SD), while both-pinned and both-run-resolved pairs are offerable. Testing only the offerable cases leaves the mixed case — where one criterion means different things on two rows of one table — completely unverified. Proven: a pinned operand (holdout mae) is never offered against a run-resolved one (sd); both-pinned and both-run-resolved pairs remain offerable -- asserted directly on offerablePairs()'s output.

PROVE CANONICALISATION BITES: add a criterion, then attempt its mirror (operands swapped, operator inverted) and assert it is absent from the picker and cannot be committed. Adding two DIFFERENT criteria would pass against no canonicalisation at all — and this hazard is new, since T11's pairs were pre-oriented and no mirror could be built. Proven: a criterion and its operand-swapped, operator-inverted mirror canonicalise to the same value and are criterionEqual -- lib/acceptance-criteria.test.ts's canonicalise/criterionEqual block.

PROVE THE CV FOLD MEAN IS REFUSED AT THE OPERAND, NOT AT ABSENCE: give a CV run whose cv_rmse_mean is PRESENT and assert the criterion reads not-evaluated with cross-validation named, rather than comparing against the fold mean. A CV run with no metrics at all would pass through the operand-absence path and leave the real trap — metricValueOf answering a cv-fold-estimate from its own mean — untested. Proven as a type-level guard (latent, not live -- residualSdOf never emits cv-fold-estimate today): a deliberately-constructed CV run whose fold mean IS present reads not-evaluated with a 'cross-validation' absence, and the displayed value is never the fold mean.

Assert BOTH legacy shapes are detected by shape, counted on screen as no longer applied, and clearable, and that neither crashes a render — T07's {metric, source, value} and T11's {left, right, ratio}. Testing one leaves the other's migration path unverified, and the second is the shape this ledger's own previous task shipped. Proven: both prior shapes (T07's {metric,source,value} and T11's {left,right,ratio}) are detected by isLegacyCriterion via the absence of 'kind', counted and clearable in core-config.tsx's migration strip, and RowCriteriaMarks filters them out before evaluating so neither crashes a render.

Assert the parity scatter is absent from the time-axis sync group — hovering the Actual vs Predicted chart must not move a crosshair on it. A visual check cannot distinguish an unsynced chart from a synced one whose axes happen to overlap. Proven as a static-source contract test (evaluation-contract.test.ts): parity-scatter-chart.tsx's code (comments stripped) contains no syncId prop and no EVAL_SYNC_ID import -- syncId never reaches the DOM, so only a source check can prove this.

Render a non-CV run beside a SCORED CV run and assert their scatters name DIFFERENT populations — test split for the first, holdout for the second. Two non-CV runs would pass against a chart that labels nothing. Proven end to end (phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx): a non-CV run's parity scatter names the TEST split and a SCORED CV run's names the VALIDATION holdout, on the same fixture shape apart from that one field.

PROVE THE TWO METHODS ARE BOTH PRESENT AND DISTINGUISHABLE: fit a tree-based model on a frame carrying one high-cardinality feature and one lower-cardinality predictive one, and assert impurity and permutation rank them DIFFERENTLY and that each figure names its own method. A fixture where both methods agree cannot distinguish a working comparison from one table rendered twice — and the cardinality bias MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 measured is exactly what makes disagreement the expected case here.
Assert a permutation figure never renders without its spread and its baseline score, and that a legacy run reads 'not recorded for this run' rather than a blank or a zero.

Measure n_features x n_repeats permutation cost against the real built image under --memory=8g --cpus=2 on the largest available predictions frame, and record the table. An unmeasured n_repeats is the guess-wearing-a-constant MODEL-FLOW-020's finding 3 forbids.

PROVE THE RENAME IS WHOLE: render a non-CV run and a SCORED CV run and assert ALL FOUR chart panels plus the banner name the same population within each run, and that the two runs name DIFFERENT ones. Asserting one panel would pass against exactly the half-applied state this file is in today. Proven end to end (phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx): a non-CV run and a SCORED CV run each assert their OWN population word across the banner and all four chart panels, and assert the OTHER run's word is absent throughout.

Add a fifth cvScoringPhaseOf phase in a type-level fixture and assert the population derivation fails to compile. A runtime default cannot be distinguished from a correct mapping by any render test, which is how the current awaiting-scoring branch survives. Proven as a compile-time test (lib/metric-source.test.ts): `@ts-expect-error` on `populationOf('rescoring')` -- an unused directive is itself a `tsc --noEmit` failure, so this fails loudly if the exhaustiveness guard is ever weakened.

Assert each legend swatch's colour and dash equal the values the chart draws with, read from the same exported constant. A test asserting a hardcoded literal would pass against the drift this criterion exists to prevent. Proven by importing the exact exported constant each legend entry and its chart's own JSX colour prop both bind to, and asserting equality (evaluation-contract.test.ts) -- not a hardcoded literal that could drift from the chart silently.

Render a run with no recorded prediction range and assert the parity section states which figure is missing, rather than rendering nothing. Proven end to end (phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx): a run with parityRange: null renders the stated absence text naming the missing figure, not a blank section.

Assert the SD-band copy names a constant width and contains neither 'predictive interval' nor 'confidence', and that it matches whichever SD the T16 audit found fit.sd to hold. Proven (phase-3-evaluation.test.tsx): the SD-band copy states 'ONE constant width' and the rendered container text contains neither 'predictive interval' nor 'confidence', case-insensitively.

Zoom the shared window and assert the residual-diagnostics copy still states its full-frame scope while the two charts above it re-render. Proven structurally (evaluation-contract.test.ts), not by driving the zoom control: `residuals`/`histogramBins`/`qq`'s own useMemo dependency arrays never list `zoom`, while `visibleRows`/`tickFormatter`'s do -- the split the diagnostics copy states in prose is real in the dependency graph, not merely claimed.

Assert the parity legend's line entry contains 'y = x' and does not contain 'baseline', and that its two entries differ by swatch SHAPE rather than only by colour. Proven (evaluation-contract.test.ts): the parity legend's dashed entry matches /y = x/ and no entry matches /baseline/i; its two entries' swatch shapes are asserted distinct (a Set of the two shapes has size 2).

REPRO GATE -- no fix merges before this passes: a fixture whose predictions span a known window asserts the chart's first and last rendered tick fall inside that window. Assert against the TICKS, not against the data passed in; a test that reads the input array cannot see a formatter or a domain disagreeing with it, which is the whole defect class. Proven end to end (chart-time-axis.test.tsx): CandidateOverlayChart, ActualVsPredictedChart and ResidualChart each render a fixture spanning the real observed window (2026-02-21 12:55 to 2026-02-27 08:00) and every rendered X-axis tick parses back inside that window (+/-1 day tolerance for tick placement). Asserts tick count > 0 FIRST in every case, so a 0x0 jsdom ResponsiveContainer measurement (or, as found while writing this, a flat getBoundingClientRect mock that also breaks recharts' own text-measurement span and prunes every tick as 'overlapping') cannot pass vacuously. A sensitivity case shifts the same fixture by the reported +27 days and confirms the assertion actually fails on it.

Seed mpCompareRunIdsAtom with an id belonging to no run in the current draft and assert every consumer -- the overlay chart included, not only RunParamsPanel -- fetches nothing for it and plots nothing from it. This is the stale-id path T08 part 3 recorded and only one consumer currently guards. Proven end to end (chart-time-axis.test.tsx): mpCompareRunIdsAtom seeded with an id belonging to no run in the draft/job. All three consumers -- the job-path CandidateComparison (overlay + table), the standalone-path StandaloneComparison (overlay + table), and RunParamsPanel -- still render/count every real candidate ('all 2 runs', never '0 of 2'), and the foreign id is never among the runIds actually requested from useCandidatePredictions.

Overlay two runs whose decimated timestamps do NOT coincide and assert each series' points keep their own x values, and that no row is dropped without being counted. Two series that already share timestamps would pass an index-based merge and prove nothing. Proven end to end (chart-time-axis.test.tsx): buildOverlayRows fed two runs with deliberately disjoint timestamps. Each run's own timestamps carry only that run's prediction (the other's column is undefined, not zero or dropped), the merged row count equals the UNION of both series (5, not 3 or 2), and rows stay sorted by time -- an index-based merge would have aligned the two series' row 0 onto one shared x and passed for the wrong reason.

features.title: Size the search grids and the per-algorithm defaults from the dataset, not from a constant
features.description: Two related fixes. (1) TUNING_GRID and the Find-Best-Model candidate list are fixed data, identical for a 200-row dataset and a 200,000-row one — derive their bounds from the dataset's own size instead. (2) The per-algorithm hyperparameter defaults a user sees on selecting an algorithm are single values with no indication of what range is reasonable — add a suggested range beside each, drawn from the estimator's own documented behaviour.
userDecisions: GRIDS ARE DERIVED, NOT DECLARED (resolved). The shape of the derivation is the formula the user supplied — n_estimators, max_depth and SVR's C scaled by dataset size, with floors and caps — but the INPUT is corrected from row count to distinct labelled observations (finding 1). The formula's structure is kept; its variable is not.

DEFAULTS STAY SINGLE VALUES, WITH A SUGGESTED RANGE BESIDE THEM (resolved). A range as the default would mean the form no longer describes one run. The suggestion is advisory text next to the field, the same shape MODEL-FLOW-012-T05 chose for the Loss function control — annotate rather than remove or restrict.
findings: ROW COUNT IS THE WRONG VARIABLE, MEASURED NOT ARGUED. A real predictions.parquet from run 61f9aa28 carries 1,341 rows holding only NINETEEN distinct y_true values — median run of 67 consecutive identical rows, lag-1 autocorrelation 0.9992, and copying the previous row scores R² 0.9984 against the model's own -2.4067. The supplied formula's `n_samples // 10` yields est_small = 50 on that dataset (hitting its own cap) for data with nineteen independent observations. Fifty estimators fitted to nineteen points is an overfit that produces entirely plausible numbers. This is the identical correction MODEL-FLOW-016-T02 had to make for MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD, and for the same reason: a lab target forward-filled onto a fine grid makes rows and observations different quantities, and every capacity decision must key on the second.

THE GRID IS ALREADY DATA, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS SMALL. MODEL-FLOW-013-T11 built TUNING_GRID (apps/backend/src/lib/tuning-grid.ts) as a declared table covering all ten runnable algorithms, with tuningCandidatesFor(algorithm, alreadyTried) excluding the winner's own setting and capping at TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB=4. It is pinned by a static source guard (tuning-grid.spec.ts) that reads build_model's actual .get() calls out of images/trainer/train.py, so the grid cannot silently drift from what the trainer reads. Making the table a FUNCTION of dataset size means the guard must still hold for every value the function can produce — a fixed table can be checked exhaustively; a derived one has to be checked over its range.

GPR AND SVR ALREADY HAVE MEASURED CEILINGS, AND THE PRECEDENT IS THE METHOD. build_model refuses GPR above GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS (O(n^2) kernel matrix) and lstm/gru above LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS, the latter set by MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 to the largest value ACTUALLY MEASURED against the real image under production memory and CPU limits, with one further point shown safely beyond it — explicitly not an extrapolation. Any floor or cap this feature introduces is set the same way or it is a guess wearing a constant's clothes. The user's own `svr_C = [0.1, 1] if n_samples < 200 else [0.1, 1, 10]` is exactly this kind of threshold and needs the same treatment.

A DERIVED GRID CHANGES WHAT A RUN'S PROVENANCE MEANS. Today a candidate job's hyperparameterSets are the literal values a user or the fixed grid chose, and ModelTrainingRun.hyperparameters records them (MODEL-FLOW-012-T01 confirmed the column is required with no default, written inside launchDraftRun's own transaction). With derivation, two jobs on the same algorithm but different-sized datasets get different grids — which is the point, and which means the RECORD must show what the grid was derived FROM, or a later reader cannot tell a deliberate difference from a code change between the two runs.

THE DEFAULTS AND THE GRID ARE TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH FOR ONE THING. HYPERPARAMS (apps/client/lib/training-config.ts) holds the per-algorithm defaults a form shows; TUNING_GRID holds the variants a tuning phase tries. MODEL-FLOW-012-T01 verified the two agree key-for-key across all ten runnable algorithms today. Adding suggested ranges to the first while deriving the second risks them drifting apart — a form suggesting 100-500 estimators beside a grid that only ever tries 50-100 tells the user two different things about the same parameter.

T01 AUDIT (a)+(b), 2026-09-06 — READ FROM SOURCE. (a) TUNING_GRID (tuning-grid.ts:26-77) is a pure literal table: ten algorithms, 1-4 variants each, NOTHING varies with anything, TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB=4. lstm/gru have no entry by design (TrainingAlgorithmEnum omits them). (b) Finding 5's key-for-key agreement STILL HOLDS — compared HYPERPARAMS (training-config.ts:41-327) against the grid and both against images/trainer/app/models.py's own hyperparameters.get() calls: all ten runnable algorithms agree exactly, so MODEL-FLOW-012-T01's claim is not stale. CORRECTS FINDING 2's path in passing: the source guard reads images/trainer/app/models.py, NOT train.py — the trainer image was split into a package and build_model moved to its own module (the guard's own doc comment records this; finding 2 above predates it). SPELLING TRAP FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS: the Gaussian-process algorithm is `grp` in the grid, in HYPERPARAMS and in models.py's branch alike, never `gpr` — TUNING_GRID['gpr'] returns undefined, which tuningCandidatesFor turns into [] and the caller reads as an honest 'nothing left to tune'.

T01 AUDIT (c), 2026-09-06 — THE DATASET FIGURE IS NOT REACHABLE AT DERIVATION TIME, WHICH REORDERS THIS FEATURE'S OWN TASKS. advanceJobForRun (model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts:571-599) holds a job row carrying goldArtifactId and no size figure of any kind. distinct_labelled_values requires a FULL ARTIFACT READ, and model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:174-182 already carries an explicit, reasoned refusal to add one on the launch path ('doing it a third time would make Start Training wait on a second read of the whole artifact'). CONSEQUENCE: T04's columns are a PREREQUISITE for T03, not a follow-on — the input must be captured at job creation and stored on the job, never recomputed where the grid is built. The client already holds both figures at Step 3 (useArtifactSplitStats -> labelled_rows + distinct_labelled_values, always present in both ratio and CV mode since MODEL-FLOW-016-T09), on the same step as the algorithm form. Path: client -> CreateCandidateJobSchema -> nullable columns on ModelCandidateJob -> read off the job row. Zero new artifact reads. This also RESOLVES openDecision 1 (server-side or client-side): the figure is COMPUTED server-side by /split-stats exactly once, CARRIED by the client because that is the only caller that has already paid for it, and STORED on the job so the backend reads it from a row rather than an artifact.

T01 AUDIT (d), 2026-09-06 — T06 IS NOT A NO-OP, AND FINDING 5'S TWO-SOURCES-OF-TRUTH IS ALREADY LIVE INSIDE ONE JOB. T06's own scope note asks whether Find Best Model passes only user-ticked algorithms with no hyperparameters of its own. It does not: use-model-training.ts:427-438 sends defaultHyperparams(a) — the CLIENT's HYPERPARAMS defaults — as each sweep candidate's hyperparameters. So in a single SWEEP_THEN_TUNE job, phase 1's values come from apps/client/lib/training-config.ts and phase 2's from apps/backend/src/lib/tuning-grid.ts. They agree today only because (b) holds; nothing enforces it across the wire. SECOND HALF OF T06 IS REAL AND REACHABLE, measured: `grp` has 0 runs of 175 in the live database, so build_model's GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS=10,000 refusal (models.py:55,185-190) has never once fired — while the largest GOLD artifact in the system is 46,070 rows. A sweep ticking Gaussian Process on it spends a container to reach a refusal that was knowable at selection time.

T01 AUDIT (e), 2026-09-06 — THE SOURCE GUARD ASSERTS KEYS, NOT VALUES, SO A DERIVED GRID NEEDS NO NEW GUARD PROPERTY. tuning-grid.spec.ts:91-100 extracts every hyperparameters.get("KEY") out of models.py's build_model and asserts each grid variant's KEY SET is a subset of what that algorithm's branch reads. Values are never checked. V02 is therefore satisfied by generating grids at several effective sample sizes and running the SAME key-set assertion over each — the guard iterates sizes.flatMap(derive) instead of a literal table, and no new property has to be invented. Cheap, real, and not a blocker for T03.

T01 AUDIT (f), 2026-09-06 — MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE DATABASE. FINDING 1 IS CONFIRMED AND UNDERSTATED, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE FEATURE. GOLD artifact rowCount across 55 artifacts spans 54 to 46,070 (850x). splitSpec.source_rows on real runs spans 4,470 to 15,441. But distinct_labelled_values — the variable finding 1 establishes every capacity decision must key on — is recorded on only 4 of 175 runs (CV runs only; it is filled by the container, not at create time) and EVERY value ever measured in this system is one of 19, 32, 59, 97. That is a 5x range against row count's 850x. The 8,350-row artifact holds 32 distinct labelled values; the 8,512-row one holds 59 — ratios of 140x to 260x. TWO CONSEQUENCES. First, a grid keyed on the correct variable would be very nearly the SAME GRID on every dataset this system has ever seen: the derivation's premise has almost no range to scale over once the variable is corrected. Second, the whole observable range sits far below where today's fixed bounds bind — xgboost currently tries n_estimators 500 / max_depth 8 against 32 independent observations, which is not a hypothetical overfit but current behaviour on real data. What the measured range DOES support is a refusal threshold (AC5) and honesty about both figures (AC2); neither needs a scaling law.

T01 AUDIT (g), 2026-09-06 — T03 IS BLOCKED, AND THE BLOCKER IS ITSELF MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. T03 requires every floor, cap and threshold to be the largest value ACTUALLY MEASURED — the standard GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS, LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS and MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD were each set by. The template to match is the measured table at apps/python/services/split_stats_service.py:60-127, which records the per-k RMSE coefficient-of-variation on two real artifacts, names the k where it degrades, states its own confound, and gives the scikit-learn version it was measured against. That measurement CANNOT BE TAKEN from this system's data: 'at what effective sample size does a deeper tree stop helping' has no answer inside a range of 19 to 97 distinct observations, where every bound in the current grid is already saturated. A constant written now would be extrapolation — exactly the 'guess wearing a formula' this feature's own finding 3 forbids. See T03's own status entry for what would unblock it.
openDecisions: IS THE DERIVATION SERVER-SIDE OR CLIENT-SIDE? The grid is consumed by advanceJobForRun (backend) and the suggested ranges are rendered by the form (client), but both need the same dataset figure. The distinct-labelled count is computable in one place only — MODEL-FLOW-014's /split-stats, which already reads the artifact once and already derives the labelled count for its own cut. Deriving it twice is how the form and the grid start disagreeing (finding 5); routing the client's suggestions through that endpoint costs a fetch the panel is already making.

DOES A DERIVED GRID NEED ITS OWN CAP SEPARATE FROM TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB? A larger dataset admits a wider grid, but the budget is fits, not values — and MODEL-FLOW-016 multiplies each fit by k folds. Whether a big dataset earns more variants or the cap stays at 4 regardless is a cost decision, not a correctness one. UNDECIDED AND UNTOUCHED by the 2026-09-06 pass — TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB stays 4.

AC1 CONTRADICTS T06 AS WRITTEN, AND THE AMENDMENT IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN APPLIED SILENTLY (raised 2026-09-06 by T01). AC1 says 'Every derived bound keys on distinct labelled observations, never on row count.' But GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS is an O(n^2) kernel matrix over ROWS — a memory ceiling that is correctly keyed on rows, and T06's own second half asks for exactly that refusal to be surfaced at algorithm selection. PROPOSED READING, applied by the 2026-09-06 pass and open to reversal: AC1 governs CAPACITY bounds — how much model the data can support, which is a statement about independent observations. RESOURCE ceilings — how much a container can hold, which is a statement about bytes in memory — key on rows and stay exactly as they are. The two are different quantities answering different questions, and collapsing them would make the GPR refusal wrong in the direction of spawning containers that cannot finish.

THE SUPPLIED svr_C FORMULA DOES NOT FIT THE GRID'S SHAPE, UNRESOLVED (raised 2026-09-06 by T01, deliberately not settled mid-audit). The user's `svr_C = [0.1, 1] if n_samples < 200 else [0.1, 1, 10]` is a LIST OF VALUES for one key. TUNING_GRID's svm entry is four WHOLE RECORDS, each carrying C plus kernel plus epsilon together (tuning-grid.ts:35-40), because a variant is a complete hyperparameter set the trainer receives verbatim — not a per-key axis the backend crosses. Turning a per-key list into variants means deciding what the other two keys hold in each, which is a design question the formula does not answer. Belongs to T03.

tasks.result: COMPLETED AS A DELIBERATE NO-OP 2026-09-06, decided by the user on the measurement below rather than by argument. NO DERIVATION WAS BUILT AND THE GRID STAYS THE FIXED TABLE. This task's own standard — every floor, cap and threshold measured rather than picked — was met by measuring whether the derivation is worth having at all, and the answer is no. See this task's `blocked` field, kept verbatim, for the full ladder: at 32 distinct labelled values holdout RMSE by max_depth reads 4=0.1505 / 5=0.1585 / 10=0.1564 / 20=0.1566 / unlimited=0.1570, and at 59 distinct the SAME ladder reads 4=0.1725 / 5=0.1639 / 10=0.1697 / 20=0.1666 / unlimited=0.1669 — a 5% spread both times, non-monotone both times, with the ordering INVERTED between the two datasets (depth 4 best-to-worst, depth 5 worst-to-best). Within-cell SDs of 0.0002-0.0030 sit far below the 0.008 between-depth spread, so the differences are real within a dataset and simply do not replicate across one. That is noise, and a grid scaled by effective sample size would be fitting it. For scale, capacity spans 5% of holdout RMSE while ALGORITHM choice spans 106% (random_forest 0.157 to pls 0.323) — already swept by Find Best Model. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: one target on one process, two artifacts, max_depth and n_estimators only. Capacity is not shown to be irrelevant in general — it is shown not to separate on the data this system has. Revisit if a dataset with materially more distinct labelled values is ever ingested. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AFFECTED, stated rather than silently dropped: AC1/AC3/AC4/AC7 and verifications V01-V04 describe a derived grid that now will not exist, and are resolved as not-applicable rather than passed. At 97 distinct the ladder reads max_depth 4=0.1905 (n=2, sd 0.0019), 5=0.2017 (n=2, sd 0.0009), 10=0.1890 (n=2, sd 0.0002), 20=0.1877 (n=2, sd 0.0009), unlimited=0.1883 (n=1). Across the three datasets the same five settings rank differently every time: depth 4 is BEST at 32, WORST at 59 and mid at 97; depth 5 is WORST at 32, BEST at 59 and WORST again at 97; unlimited sits mid at 32 and 59 and near-best at 97. Three datasets, three orderings, no setting consistently better anywhere. This is the strongest form of the original finding rather than a new one: if capacity had a learnable relationship with effective sample size, the ranking would be stable or would shift systematically as n grows from 32 to 59 to 97. It does neither. The closure stands, now on three points instead of two, and on the full 32-97 range this system actually holds.

Per finding 4: two jobs on one algorithm and differently-sized datasets now get different grids by design, and nothing in the record distinguishes that from a code change between the two runs.

tasks.result: PARTIALLY RESOLVED BY T03's CLOSURE 2026-09-06, and left pending for what survives it. This task has two halves. The finding-5 risk this task was written to guard against is also reduced but NOT gone: with the grid staying fixed, a suggested range need only agree with a table anyone can read (TUNING_GRID) rather than with a moving derivation — but the two tables it must agree with are still TWO (client HYPERPARAMS and backend TUNING_GRID), and T01(d) found the sweep already feeds the first into a job whose phase 2 uses the second. SEED AND LOSS FUNCTION still get no range, unchanged by any of this. ||| COMPLETED 2026-09-06 for exactly the surviving half. `SuggestedRange {min,max,note}` added to the number and nullable-number field kinds in training-config.ts, populated for all 28 numeric fields across all 12 algorithms, and rendered by a new `RangeHint` under each input in dynamic-hyperparameters.tsx. NO SIZE-DEPENDENT FIGURE IS SHOWN anywhere, per T03. Seed and lossFunction gained no range and are asserted to remain absent from HYPERPARAMS entirely. 24 tests, all passing; tsc and eslint clean on every touched file. ONE BLOCK-LEVEL CAVEAT SHIPS WITH THE BANDS, added last and deliberately: 28 per-field ranges rendered with nothing said about their scope would have re-created this feature's own finding 1 from the other direction — a confident-looking number in front of the user on exactly the data where T03 measured that it carries no information. DRAWN FROM THE ESTIMATOR'S OWN DOCUMENTED BEHAVIOUR, and cited. tasks.result:

HALF ONE — SIZE THE SWEEP'S OWN HYPERPARAMETERS: NOT a no-op (T01(d) settled the scope question this task opens with), but BLOCKED BEHIND T03. use-model-training.ts:427-438 sends defaultHyperparams(a) per sweep candidate, so phase 1's values come from the CLIENT's HYPERPARAMS and phase 2's from the BACKEND's TUNING_GRID — finding 5's two-sources-of-truth is already live inside a single SWEEP_THEN_TUNE job, agreeing today only because T01(b) found the two tables still key-for-key identical, with nothing enforcing it across the wire. Sizing them from a common derivation is exactly what T03 cannot yet do, so this half waits rather than inventing its own constants.

HALF TWO — REFUSE AN ALGORITHM THE DATASET CANNOT SUPPORT: DONE. AlgorithmSelector now disables Gaussian Process, with the reason and both numbers stated, when the dataset is over the ceiling build_model measures it against — the disable-with-reason discipline lstm/gru, Find Best Parameters and Evaluation's Compare already follow. Measured motivation, not hypothetical: grp had 0 runs of 175 in the live DB, so that refusal had never once fired, while the largest GOLD artifact is 46,070 rows; reaching it costs a container spawn, an artifact download and a queue slot.

KEYED ON train_labelled_rows, NOT ROW COUNT, and not on distinct labelled values either — read from source rather than assumed: models.py:185 guards `n_train_rows`, the post-split post-mask count, which is precisely /split-stats' train_labelled_rows. Using the artifact's raw rowCount would refuse datasets that genuinely fit. NULL is left unrefused on purpose (before Apply, and in CV mode where train_labelled_rows is null by construction): refusing on a number the component does not have would be a guess wearing a limit, and train.py's fit-time backstop still fires.

This is also the one place in MODEL-FLOW-020 that keys on rows rather than distinct observations, which contradicts AC1 as literally written — see this feature's own openDecisions entry for the capacity-vs-resource amendment, recorded rather than applied silently. GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS is mirrored from models.py:55 with a comment pointing back at it, the same mirror discipline MIRRORS.md records for MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD.

Covered by a new algorithm-selector.test.tsx (no test file for that component existed): disabled above the ceiling with both figures in the copy, selectable below it, no refusal when the figure is unknown, and the refusal scoped to grp alone rather than shrinking the whole catalogue on a large dataset. ||| NOW COMPLETE 2026-09-06, both halves resolved — one built, one closed on evidence. HALF ONE is CLOSED AS A NO-OP rather than built, and this is the explicit statement this task's own detail demands instead of being quietly marked done. Sizing the sweep's hyperparameters was to come 'from the same derivation as T03's grid'; T03 closed as a measured no-op (three datasets, three different orderings of the same five max_depth settings), so there is no derivation for a sweep to share. The sweep keeps sending defaultHyperparams and the tuning phase keeps reading the fixed TUNING_GRID. BUT THE UNDERLYING DEFECT T01(d) FOUND IS NOW GUARDED, which is the part worth having and needed no derivation at all. Phase 1's values come from the client's HYPERPARAMS and phase 2's from the backend's TUNING_GRID inside ONE SWEEP_THEN_TUNE job — finding 5's two-sources-of-truth, live, agreeing only because MODEL-FLOW-012-T01 and MODEL-FLOW-020-T01(b) each checked by hand. training-config-grid-agreement.test.ts now asserts every key TUNING_GRID varies is a field the form actually shows, per algorithm, by reading the backend source rather than copying it; it also mirrors tuning-grid.spec.ts's lstm/gru assertion from the client side. A tuning phase that changed a knob the user was never shown now fails a test instead of shipping. HALF TWO (the GPR size refusal) was already delivered earlier in this same session and is unchanged: AlgorithmSelector disables Gaussian Process above GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS, keyed on train_labelled_rows because models.py:185 guards n_train_rows, with the constant mirrored from models.py and now registered as MIRRORS.md entry 5.
tasks.detail:
SCOPE DEPENDS ON T01(d). If the sweep already passes only the algorithms a user ticked, with no hyperparameters of its own, then there is nothing to derive and this task says so explicitly rather than being quietly marked done — the no-op discipline MODEL-FLOW-012-T02 and -T09 both followed.

If it does supply per-algorithm hyperparameters for its candidates, they come from the same derivation as T03's grid. A sweep and a tuning phase disagreeing about what a reasonable n_estimators is for one dataset would be two answers to one question inside one job — and MODEL-FLOW-013-T11 made them phases of ONE job precisely so they could not diverge.

SEPARATELY, AND WORTH CHECKING WHILE HERE: an algorithm the dataset cannot support should not be offered as a sweep candidate at all. build_model already refuses GPR above its measured row ceiling by name; a sweep that includes GPR on a dataset above it spends a container to reach that refusal. Refuse at selection with the reason stated, the disable-with-reason discipline lstm/gru, Find Best Parameters and Evaluation's Compare control all already follow in this wizard.

acceptance_criteria: Every derived bound keys on distinct labelled observations, never on row count.
Both figures — rows and distinct observations — are shown wherever a derived bound is displayed or recorded.
Every floor, cap and threshold has a recorded measurement behind it, not a chosen constant.
The tuning grid's source guard holds across the whole range the derivation can produce, including its degenerate small end.
A dataset too small to support tuning is refused with the reason named, never given a floored grid that implies it can be tuned.
A job records what its grid was derived from; a job predating this feature reads as not derived rather than being reconstructed.
A suggested range contains every value the derived grid can produce for that algorithm at that size — proven by a test, not by inspection.
Suggested ranges cite the estimator behaviour they rest on.
Seed and loss function gain no suggested range, and keep their existing per-algorithm honesty labels.
The sweep and the tuning phase never present different bounds for the same parameter on the same dataset.

WHERE EACH CRITERION LANDED, 2026-09-06 — recorded because four of the ten describe a derived grid this feature deliberately did not build. AC1 (bounds key on distinct observations): NOT APPLICABLE, no bound is derived; the one size-keyed refusal that shipped (GPR) is a RESOURCE ceiling on rows, per the amendment in openDecisions. AC2 (both figures shown wherever recorded): MET — ModelCandidateJob.sizedRowCount/sizedDistinctLabelled are written together or not at all, and RunParamsPanel renders both or neither. AC3 (every constant measured): MET IN THE ONLY WAY LEFT — the measurement was taken and it said not to introduce the constants at all. GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS, the one constant echoed client-side, is measured in models.py. AC4 (source guard holds across the derivation's range): NOT APPLICABLE, there is no range; the guard still holds exhaustively over the fixed table, and a second guard now checks it from the client side too. AC5 (a too-small dataset is refused by name): NOT MET, and deliberately so — the ladder found no size in 32-97 that performed measurably worse, so there is no threshold to refuse at. Refusing on an unmeasured one is the failure AC3 exists to prevent. This is the single criterion left open by this feature's completion, and it is now open ONLY as a missing refusal — the present-tense honesty gap it also implied is closed. T05's suggested ranges would otherwise have advertised bands on datasets where T03 proved no value inside them separates, so DynamicHyperparameters carries a block-level caveat saying the ranges describe the estimator and not this dataset. What remains unbuilt is a threshold; what is no longer unsaid is that the bands are not sized to the data. AC6 (a job records what it was derived from; legacy reads as not-derived): MET, live-verified, with the columns named sized* rather than derivedFrom* precisely because nothing is derived from them yet. AC7 (suggested range contains every value the grid can produce, proven by test): MET against the fixed grid, which is the only form of it left — training-config-grid-agreement.test.ts reads the backend source and was proven to fail when a band is narrowed. AC8 (ranges cite estimator behaviour): MET — each note states what the parameter does in checkable terms. AC9 (seed and loss function gain no range): MET and asserted structurally; neither is a HYPERPARAMS member. AC10 (sweep and tuning phase never present different bounds): MET more narrowly than written — with no derivation there are no per-dataset bounds to disagree about, and the key-level agreement that WAS at risk is now guarded by a test rather than by hand.

Run a real tuning phase on a small dataset and a large one and confirm the grids actually differ, and that each job records what it derived from. features.title: Step 3 — compare runs in place: a metrics table and an overlay chart the run cards drive
features.description: Training Config's RunParamsPanel showed one metric per run (RMSE) and no table or chart of any kind, so a draft with three runs had nowhere in Step 3 to read RMSE/MAE/R2 side by side or see which run tracks reality best. This brings Step 4's ranked-table and overlay-chart layout into Step 3, and replaces the per-card single Select with a multi-select Compare checkbox: the checked runs are the comparison, and checking nothing means compare them all.
userDecisions: COMPARE REPLACES SELECT ON THE CARD, AND THE EMERALD RING STAYS (resolved by the user 2026-09-07). The user's words: 'Replaces it but keep emarald ring don't use word carrying forward'. So the per-card control is one checkbox, not a checkbox plus the old button; the emerald ring now means 'in the comparison'; and the phrase 'Carrying forward' is retired from this panel — the footer reads 'Selected: <algorithm> · <timestamp>'.

THE CHECKBOX WRITES NO SERVER STATE — the one deliberate departure from a literal reading of 'replaces it', taken because the literal reading is unsound. ModelDraft.selectedRunId is exactly one run and is what Step 4 and Step 5 resolve against; a compare set is any number of runs and is often empty. Deriving the write from 'whichever box was ticked first' would persist a choice the user never made, and un-ticking to get back to compare-all would silently leave it behind. The carry-forward therefore keeps its own explicit control, moved to the footer as a 'Use this run' radio picker. Stated rule: nothing checked -> selectedRunId unchanged; three checked, no picker use -> unchanged; picker used, then all unchecked -> the pick stands.
findings: STEP 3 HAD NO TABLE AND NO CHART AT ALL, at any run count — confirmed by a directory-wide grep of training-config/ for <table|recharts|Chart|METRIC. The only <table> there is split-distribution-panel's CV fold plan (Fold/Cut/Train rows/Test rows/Distinct) and the only chart is its TagBoxplotChart; neither carries a model metric. The single metric a run card rendered was run.metrics.rmse. So this feature is not 'fix a broken table' — it is 'the table was only ever built one step later'.

AND STEP 4'S TABLE IS REACHABLE ONLY VIA A CANDIDATE JOB. phase-4-model-selection.tsx renders CandidateTable + CandidateOverlayChart under CandidateComparison, which requires mpCandidateJobIdAtom. The standalone branch (StandaloneComparison) renders a card grid with ONE headline RMSE per row and no chart. Since use-model-training.ts refuses more than one algorithm without Find Best Model ('Select exactly one algorithm — a run fits one algorithm per model.'), the only way to get three algorithms on a draft one at a time is three standalone runs — which is exactly the case with no table.

THE OVERLAY CHART NEEDED WIDENING, NOT COPYING. CandidateOverlayChart reads exactly two fields off each candidate (runId, algorithm) and looks the rest up in byRunId. Its Props were CandidateResult[]; they are now the structural minimum { runId: string | null; algorithm: string }[] (exported as OverlaySeries), which CandidateResult still satisfies. Copying it into training-config/ would have moved it outside model-selection-contract.test.ts's grep, which targets hardcoded relative paths — the copy would have been silently uncovered by the no-algorithm-branching guard.

holdoutAbsence IS DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPLIED BY STEP 3. It is optional on RankableRow, and holdoutAbsenceOf(run, null) returns 'not-recorded' — an assertion that a defect occurred. Step 3 does not know whether the dataset has a holdout, so supplying it would fabricate an explanation. The ranking states the source it ran on and says nothing it cannot support.

jobStillLive IS A SELECTION RULE, NOT A COMPARISON RULE. The old Select carried three disable reasons; only two of them survive onto the compare checkbox (non-terminal, and FAILED/CANCELED — both genuinely have nothing to plot). A SUCCEEDED run owned by a still-running sweep has real metrics and real predictions and compares fine; what it cannot do is be committed as the draft's choice while that job may overwrite it. It therefore gates the footer picker and not the checkbox.

OUT OF SCOPE, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT IS REAL: mpCandidateJobIdAtom is client-only and is NOT hydrated on draft resume (no reference in lib/model-draft-hydration.ts, use-model-draft-resume.ts or use-model-draft-sync.ts). Resuming a draft whose runs came from a sweep therefore drops Step 4 into the standalone branch and loses its ranked table and overlay chart. Not fixed by this feature.

THE LEDGER ITSELF WAS UNPARSEABLE WHEN THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN. Eight unescaped double quotes in prose on lines 2395 and 2419 (MODEL-FLOW-019's T-detail text: "how scattered are the residuals", "RMSE <= [ ]", and others) broke json.load. Escaped in this same pass. Same class as the earlier occurrence — parse the file before and after every edit.

A CONCURRENT PROCESS IS RENAMING Holdout -> Validate WHILE THIS LANDED, and it contradicts MODEL-FLOW-019's own recorded decision ("COLUMN NAMES ARE 'Test RMSE' AND 'Holdout RMSE', NOT 'Validate RMSE'", because `validate` names the dataset QUALITY GATE in this codebase). Observed directly: this feature's new table header was rewritten from Holdout to Validate twice, the second time 4 seconds after being written, and phase-4-model-selection.tsx:969 changed from 'Holdout RMSE' to 'Validate RMSE' at 08:43 without this session touching it. Not a project hook — .claude/hooks/post-write.sh does no such rewrite. The rename is PARTIAL: phase-4's own table sub-header (:494) still reads Holdout, and phase-4-model-selection.test.tsx still asserts 'Holdout RMSE' (:1372, :1395, :1417), which is why that suite gained a third failure mid-session. NOT RESOLVED HERE — needs a decision from the user. This feature's own test was made to assert the two-source-columns SHAPE rather than the contested word, so it does not take a side.
