features.title: Step 3 — a per-algorithm parameter block, so a multi-algorithm sweep stops silently training on defaults
features.description: Selecting several algorithms today produces an ALGORITHM_SWEEP whose candidates all carry the CLIENT'S DEFAULT hyperparameters — there is no way to set any of them, because the hyperparameter form belongs to the primary algorithm alone. Give each selected algorithm its own tab and its own parameter form, and send what the user actually set.
userDecisions: TABS PER SELECTED ALGORITHM (resolved by the user 2026-09-07). One block, one tab per ticked algorithm, each holding that algorithm's own DynamicHyperparameters form.
THE VALUES ARE THE USER'S, NOT defaultHyperparams (the point of the feature). Each candidate is launched with the values from its own tab, seeded FROM the defaults rather than replaced by them.

TABS RENDER FOR EVERY JOB KIND THAT CAN CARRY USER VALUES, RESOLVED BY THE USER (2026-09-08). phase-3-training-config.tsx:81's showHyperparams hides the form whenever findBestParams is on, which would make V03 (SWEEP_THEN_TUNE with user-authored phase-1 values) unreachable. Resolved: the form (single control or tabbed block) stays visible and editable regardless of findBestParams. Find Best Parameters additionally shows, read-only, the variants TUNING_GRID will search for that algorithm afterward, fetched from a new backend endpoint — never a client copy of apps/backend/src/lib/tuning-grid.ts.

AC9 (a run's recorded hyperparameters distinguish user-authored from supplied-default) IS DEFERRED THIS PASS, RESOLVED BY THE USER (2026-09-08). It is the one AC that needs a ModelCandidateJob column and migration; packages/prisma/prisma/migrations/20260907120000_model_flow_019_t09_feature_importance/ is still unapplied in the working tree, and stacking a second unapplied migration on top was rejected as the wrong sequencing. MODEL-FLOW-022 stays in_progress with AC9 explicitly unmet and recorded here, not marked completed this pass.
findings: THE DEFECT IS ALREADY RECORDED AND WAS NEVER FIXED. MODEL-FLOW-020-T01(d) read it from source: use-model-training.ts:427-438 sends defaultHyperparams(a) as each sweep candidate's hyperparameters. So in one SWEEP_THEN_TUNE job, phase 1's values come from apps/client/lib/training-config.ts and phase 2's from apps/backend/src/lib/tuning-grid.ts — finding 5's two-sources-of-truth, live, inside a single job. MODEL-FLOW-020-T06's first half was to size those values from a derivation; it closed as a no-op when MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 closed, and the underlying inability to SET them was left untouched. A user-authored version needs no derivation at all.

THE BACKEND NEEDS NO CHANGE, WHICH IS MOST OF THIS FEATURE'S SCOPE GONE. CreateCandidateJobSchema has taken candidates: [{algorithm, hyperparameters}] since MODEL-FLOW-013-T03 generalized ModelFineTuningJob, runDtoFor reads algorithm off the candidate rather than the job root, and launchDraftRun records what it launched on ModelTrainingRun.hyperparameters (required, no default, written inside the launch transaction — MODEL-FLOW-012-T01 confirmed). The provenance record is therefore already correct for per-candidate values; only the client cannot author them.

mpHyperparametersAtom IS ONE DICT FOR THE PRIMARY ALGORITHM, AND useRunConfigDraft ACTIVELY CLEARS IT. setAlgorithms 'resets hyperparameters to the new primary's clean defaults' (MODEL-FLOW-014-T08's own result). So the state shape is the work, and the blast radius is every writer and reader of that atom: useRunConfigDraft's draftsEqual comparison (which already needed criteriaEqual for nested objects, the precedent to follow), resetWizardAtom, resetPipeline, use-model-draft-sync's debounced PATCH, use-apply-run-params, and lib/model-draft-hydration.ts.

PARALLEL TRAINING IS NOT WHAT A CANDIDATE JOB DOES, AND THE TABS MUST NOT IMPLY IT. advanceJobForRun launches ONE candidate at a time, chained by a compare-and-swap on (id, currentRunId, status IN QUEUED/RUNNING); getJobService's own candidate shaping matches candidates to runs BY LAUNCH ORDER for that reason. A partial unique index allows one live job per draft. Spawning containers concurrently would be a different feature with a resource argument to make first — each container is capped at 8 GiB with --cpus=2 (trainning-container.authorized.service.ts), and MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 already measured what happens when a fit oversubscribes a 2-CPU cgroup: a 500-window benchmark took over ten minutes before torch's thread pool was capped, and 0.39s after.

PER-ALGORITHM ELIGIBILITY IS ALREADY ENFORCED ONE LAYER UP AND MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED. MODEL-FLOW-020-T06 disables Gaussian Process in AlgorithmSelector above GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS, keyed on train_labelled_rows because models.py:185 guards n_train_rows; lstm/gru carry their own LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS ceiling. A tab for an algorithm the dataset cannot support must not exist, and the tab set must read the same predicate the selector does rather than a copy of it — MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a's rule about a membership list in the client being a second source of truth applies to a tab list exactly as it does to a render mode.

THE SEED IS NOT PER-ALGORITHM AND MUST NOT APPEAR IN A TAB. MODEL-FLOW-014-T07 added one seed for a single run; MODEL-FLOW-016-T09's own note records that candidate-job creation correctly gets NO seed field. A per-tab seed input would be a control whose value is never sent — the exact defect MODEL-FLOW-012-T05 had to annotate its way out of for lossFunction. Same for CV: MODEL-FLOW-016-T10 made cross-validation and Find Best Model mutually exclusive in both directions, so the multi-algorithm block and the CV control can never be active together and each already disables the other.

2026-09-08 DATED APPEND (T01 audit, read from source — 8 corrections to the findings above; openDecisions 1 and 2 both resolved). (1) The atom is mpHyperparamsAtom, not mpHyperparametersAtom (finding 3) — zero repo-wide hits for the latter. (2) TWO defaultHyperparams call sites send defaults into a candidate job, not one: use-model-training.ts:484 (the sweep, finding 1's own citation) AND :451 (HYPERPARAMETER_SEARCH — single algorithm + Find Best Parameters). Finding 2's 'the backend needs no change' still holds for sending values (both sites need only a client-side fix), but no longer holds for the whole feature — see (8). (3) ALGORITHM_LABELS lives in store/model-pipeline.ts:88, not lib/training-config.ts. (4) LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS (images/trainer/app/models.py:115) has NO client-side mirror — algorithm-selector.tsx's DEFERRED_REASON is empty and GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS/oversizedReason is the sole client eligibility rule. V04's fixture must therefore use grp crossing 10,000 train rows; lstm/gru have no client-side ineligibility to trigger. (5) Seven flat mpHyperparamsAtom writers, not five — finding 3's list misses use-model-wizard-mode.ts:148 and use-model-preset.ts:86. Every writer replaces the whole dict; there is no merge writer outside the local draft (use-run-config-draft.ts:197-205). (6) openDecision 2 ANSWERED, verified not reasoned: sameHyperparams (tuning-grid.ts:80-85) is strict === over sorted keys, no float tolerance. The feared string/number mismatch does not apply — dynamic-hyperparameters.tsx coerces number inputs with Number(e.target.value). Client HYPERPARAMS key sets match TUNING_GRID's one-for-one per algorithm, but no client default equals any grid row, so the exclusion has NEVER fired against a UI-originated job; it can fire for the first time once values are user-authored. Both call sites checked for the resulting empty-list case: phase 2 (model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts, tuneVariants.length > 0 guard) completes the job with phase 1 only if the grid empties — safe; expandSearchCandidates (same file, HYPERPARAMETER_SEARCH path) throws a 400 'No distinct hyperparameter variants to try' if it empties — reachable only for ols, whose grid is a single row {fit_intercept: false} (tuning-grid.ts:27). Handled as a client-side pre-flight refusal in T03, recorded as new scope since no AC asks for it. (7) openDecision 1 RESOLVED client-only, and it is free rather than merely cheap: PatchModelDraftSchema.hyperparameters is HyperparametersSchema = z.record(z.string(), z.union([string, number, boolean, null])) (model-run.authorized.dto.ts:39-42), so a nested object value IS rejected by it — task (e)'s silent-400-into-useModelDraftSync's-catch is real. The design keeps the per-algorithm state in a sibling client atom that never enters the PATCH body, so V02 passes by construction rather than needing a workaround. No ModelDraft column added; AC8 holds. (8) Finding 2's 'THE BACKEND NEEDS NO CHANGE' no longer covers the whole feature: the user decided (2026-09-08) that Find Best Parameters should show the variants it will search, sourced from a new read-only backend endpoint over tuning-grid.ts rather than a client copy of the grid (use-model-training.ts:425-428's own no-duplication rule) — this is new scope, given its own task/ledger line (T03b) rather than folded into T04 silently.

2026-09-08 DATED APPEND (T15-T18 scoping, read from phase-5-evaluation.tsx and parity-scatter-chart.tsx). EIGHT ITEMS, five of them already on screen. (1) ONE FACT, THREE DERIVATIONS, PARTIALLY RENAMED: cvPhase is read three times in one file and yields 'Validate' (parityPopulation), 'Holdout residual diagnostics' (a heading) and 'validation holdout' (that section's body), while Actual vs Predicted and Residuals still say 'test' for a scored CV run whose fit IS the holdout. MODEL-FLOW-004's renamed heading, arriving a second time in the same file and half-applied. (2) parityPopulation's non-'scored' branch maps awaiting-scoring AND scoring to the test split, which those runs do not have; it is correct only because two early returns precede the scatter, so moving or removing one turns the label into a silent lie with no type error. (3) The Actual vs Predicted detail terminates mid-clause on a semicolon. (4) The parity section has no detail at all, and its heading is one word from the time-axis chart above it. (5) The histogram and Q-Q are computed over the full residual vector while the two charts above render the zoom window; nothing says so, so zooming makes two panels look broken. (6) phase-5-evaluation.tsx hardcodes four CSS variables into legend swatches for charts it does not own — the drift class T13 closed for the parity chart alone by exporting PARITY_LEGEND. (7) The +/-1 SD band is ONE constant width from fit.sd, not per-point uncertainty, and nothing on screen says so; a reader taking it for a predictive interval draws per-prediction conclusions the chart cannot support. (8) UNVERIFIED AND LOAD-BEARING FOR (7)'s wording: whether fit.sd is the residual SD of the population plotted or of the TRAINING residuals. T10's own userDecision resolved 'which SD' to residual SD for the Step 4 column citing run_predictions; nothing has confirmed the same figure reaches this band. If it is the training residuals, 'RMSE above SD is bias' is false here and the copy must say what it actually is.
openDecisions: DO PER-ALGORITHM VALUES SURVIVE A DRAFT RESUME? ModelDraft.hyperparameters is ONE Json dict (MODEL-FLOW-002-T06, the single-run spec). Per-algorithm values therefore either stay client-only and are lost on resume, or need a ModelDraft column — and MODEL-FLOW-008 AC10, -012 AC5, -013 AC7, -017 AC9 and -019 AC16 each assert that no such column is added. MODEL-FLOW-018-T02 added selectedRunId and had to amend four of those in the same pass, which is the cost. RECOMMENDATION IS CLIENT-ONLY, on MODEL-FLOW-006-T02's own reasoning: training reads target, algorithm and split from the REQUEST BODY and not from the draft, precisely because the draft can be stale at the debounced-PATCH boundary — so the authoritative record is the candidate job plus the run row, both of which already carry per-candidate values. Cost, stated: a resumed draft's tabs come back at defaults, and MODEL-FLOW-014-T07's nSplits and MODEL-FLOW-019-T07's thresholds are both already client-only for the same reason, so this is the established class rather than a new one.

WHAT DOES SWEEP_THEN_TUNE's PHASE 2 DO WITH A USER-AUTHORED PHASE 1? tuningCandidatesFor(algorithm, alreadyTried) excludes 'the winner's own setting' and caps at TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB=4. With user values in phase 1, alreadyTried now names a set the user chose rather than a default, so the exclusion becomes MORE correct — but the case where a user's value coincides exactly with a grid variant has never occurred and needs a check rather than an assumption. MODEL-FLOW-020-T05's training-config-grid-agreement.test.ts (which reads tuning-grid.ts as source and asserts every key the grid varies is a field the form shows) still holds either way and is the guard to extend, not to duplicate.

tasks.title: Audit: what the sweep actually sends, and every writer of mpHyperparametersAtom
tasks.detail:
READ, DO NOT INFER — MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code, and -004/-005/-006/-012/-016/-020 each opened with an audit that changed their own scope.

Establish: (a) that use-model-training.ts's sweep branch still sends defaultHyperparams per candidate and that nothing between it and CreateCandidateJobSchema rewrites them; (b) every reader and writer of mpHyperparametersAtom, and which of them would need to learn a nested shape versus which reads only the primary algorithm's entry; (c) whether components/ui/tabs exists and is already used anywhere, since a first use sets the pattern; (d) what DynamicHyperparameters reads besides the atom — MODEL-FLOW-020-T05 added RangeHint and a block-level caveat to it, and both must appear per tab rather than once for the primary; (e) whether use-model-draft-sync's PATCH would send a nested dict to ModelDraft.hyperparameters and be refused, since MODEL-FLOW-006 tightened PatchModelDraftSchema.hyperparameters to the same scalar-record constraint the run path enforces — a nested object is NOT a scalar record and this PATCH would 400 into useModelDraftSync's silent catch, which is the failure MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's third recorded gap describes.

(e) IS THE ONE THAT CAN SHIP BROKEN AND SILENT. Check it first.

tasks.title: Per-algorithm hyperparameter state, inside the Apply boundary
tasks.detail:
Record<algorithm, Record<key, scalar>>, seeded from HYPERPARAMS defaults when an algorithm is ticked and DISCARDED when it is unticked — a value kept for an algorithm no longer selected would be sent by a later sweep the user does not associate with it.

INSIDE MODEL-FLOW-014-T08's APPLY BOUNDARY, not on change, and through useRunConfigDraft rather than beside it. That feature's own acceptance criterion is that relock has exactly ONE trigger and useCommitRunConfig is its single writer; a second commit path for these values would be a second notion of when Step 3 is done. draftsEqual needs a nested comparison — follow criteriaEqual, added for the same reason.

THE SINGLE-RUN PATH MUST NOT REGRESS. One algorithm ticked still sends a flat dict to POST .../runs, because CreateTrainingRunSchema takes hyperparameters as a scalar record and is .strict(). The primary algorithm's entry IS that dict; nothing about the single-run request shape changes.

MODEL-FLOW-012's Apply WRITES ONE ALGORITHM'S VALUES AND THAT STAYS TRUE. useApplyRunParams applies a past run's parameters, and a run has exactly one algorithm — so it writes that algorithm's entry and switches the selection to it, which is what MODEL-FLOW-012-T08 already does. It must keep using RAW atom setters: MODEL-FLOW-010-T08 and -012-T06 both recorded that routing through useModelPipelineNav's setAlgorithm overwrites hyperparameters with defaults, and -012-V01's fixture deliberately stores a non-default value (ridge alpha 0.037) so a refactor that reintroduces that path fails loudly. Extend that fixture to the nested shape rather than replacing it.

tasks.title: The tabbed block
tasks.detail:
One tab per selected algorithm, each rendering that algorithm's DynamicHyperparameters with its RangeHint and the block-level caveat MODEL-FLOW-020-T05 ships. Tab label is the algorithm's own catalogue label via ALGORITHM_LABELS — a display lookup, never a branch (MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a, and MODEL-FLOW-019-V05's static guard greps for exactly this).

STATE THAT CANDIDATES RUN IN SEQUENCE, in the block's own copy. A tabbed form invites the reading that the tabs run together; they do not (finding 4), and a user expecting five parallel fits will read a sequential sweep as a hang. Say what it costs too — N fits, and N x k if Find Best Parameters is on — the same cost-and-benefit discipline MODEL-FLOW-016-T10's CV control carries.

NO TAB FOR AN ALGORITHM THE DATASET CANNOT SUPPORT, reading the same predicate AlgorithmSelector uses rather than a copy (finding 5). If it is already unselectable there, the tab cannot arise; the guard exists for a value that becomes ineligible AFTER selection, when the dataset or split changes under it — the self-correcting case MODEL-FLOW-016-T10's CvControl already handles for itself.

NO PER-TAB SEED AND NO PER-TAB LOSS FUNCTION (finding 6). Both are controls whose per-algorithm value would never be sent.

tasks.title: Tuning-grid read endpoint — new scope, not in the original task list
tasks.detail: User decision 2026-09-08: Find Best Parameters shows the variants TUNING_GRID will search, never a client copy (use-model-training.ts:425-428's own rule). New read-only GET under apps/backend/src/api/v1/model-run/authorized/ (tuning-grid.authorized.controller.ts + .service.ts), matching the existing <Thing>AuthorizedController/Service convention in that module. Returns TUNING_GRID[algorithm] and TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB from apps/backend/src/lib/tuning-grid.ts verbatim — no Prisma, no new schema, no migration. AppException from @softsensor/common for an unknown algorithm, never a Nest built-in. Registered in model-run.module.ts. Client: services/tuning-grid.ts + hooks/model/use-tuning-grid.ts, fetched only while findBestParams is on. This contradicts finding 2's 'the backend needs no change' for the feature as a whole, which is why it is its own task rather than folded into T04.

tasks.title: Pre-flight refusal when a user's value leaves zero grid variants — new scope, no AC asks for it
tasks.detail: Finding/correction 6: sameHyperparams exclusion in tuning-grid.ts has never fired against a UI-originated job because no client default equals a grid row; with user-authored values it can, and for ols (whose grid is the single row {fit_intercept: false}) the result is expandSearchCandidates throwing a 400 'No distinct hyperparameter variants to try' at launch time. Detect this client-side before Start Training, once T03b's endpoint is wired, and refuse in the same place algorithm-selector.tsx:22-27 already states its own refusals — not as a training-container failure. Reachable only because T03 keeps the form editable with findBestParams on. Not required by any acceptance criterion; drop it and let the backend's 400 stand if this surface isn't wanted. BLOCKED, dropped from this pass 2026-09-08: expandSearchCandidates (the only throwing call site) fires exclusively for HYPERPARAMETER_SEARCH with exactly one candidate, and the grid can only empty for ols with fit_intercept:false (its grid is the single row {fit_intercept:false}) — a one-row edge case the backend's existing 400 already covers. Building a client-side pre-flight would mean reimplementing sameHyperparams' strict equality client-side, a second copy of exactly the rule finding 6 and the grid-agreement test exist to prevent. Left blocked rather than deleted, per CLAUDE.md's blocked-feature handling: what would unblock it is a shared equality helper the client and backend both import, which does not exist today and is a bigger change than this feature's own scope.

tasks.title: Send the user's values, per candidate
tasks.detail:
use-model-training.ts's sweep branch maps each selected algorithm to {algorithm, hyperparameters: draft[algorithm]} instead of defaultHyperparams(a). No backend change (finding 2), no schema change, no migration.

SCALAR-FILTER BEFORE SENDING, and state what was dropped. CreateCandidateJobSchema's candidates carry the same HyperparametersSchema scalar constraint the run path enforces, and MODEL-FLOW-012-T09 already built toApplyPatch's defensive filter with a `dropped` return for exactly this class. Reuse it rather than adding a second filter with its own rules.

RECORD THAT THE VALUES WERE AUTHORED, not merely that they were used. MODEL-FLOW-020-T04 named its columns sized* rather than derivedFrom* precisely because a name must not assert something the code does not do; the inverse applies here — a reader of RunParamsPanel comparing two candidates cannot otherwise tell a value the user chose from a default the client supplied, and MODEL-FLOW-012's whole purpose is that panel telling the truth about what produced a run. Check whether ModelCandidateJob already distinguishes this before adding anything: if it does not, the honest minimum is one flag on the job, and it is a decision rather than a reflex.

tasks.title: Tests
tasks.detail:
PROVE THE VALUES REACH THE CANDIDATES, WITH A FIXTURE THAT IS NOT THE DEFAULTS. Set a non-default value on the SECOND tab of three and assert the created job's candidates carry it — a fixture using default values would pass unchanged against the current defaultHyperparams call, which is the bug. This is MODEL-FLOW-010-V05 and -012-V01's own fixture discipline, and both recorded it for the same reason.

Assert unticking an algorithm discards its values, that a single-algorithm launch still sends a flat scalar dict, and that Apply from RunParamsPanel writes one algorithm's entry and leaves the others alone. Extend MODEL-FLOW-020-T05's grid-agreement test rather than duplicating it.

acceptance_criteria: Every candidate in a multi-algorithm sweep carries the hyperparameters the user set for that algorithm, not the client's defaults.
Unticking an algorithm discards its values; a later sweep cannot send them.
A single-algorithm run's request shape is unchanged.
Values commit on Apply, and relock still has exactly one trigger.
No tab exists for an algorithm the current dataset cannot support, and the reason is stated where the selection is made.
No per-tab seed and no per-tab loss function exists.
The block states that candidates run in sequence and what the run costs.
No Model row is created and — pending openDecision 1 — no ModelDraft column is added.
A run's recorded hyperparameters distinguish a user-authored value from a supplied default.

verification.description: PROVE THE PER-CANDIDATE VALUES BITE: create a real 3-algorithm sweep with a DELIBERATELY non-default value on one of them and assert that candidate's own ModelTrainingRun.hyperparameters records it while the other two record theirs. A sweep of defaults would pass against today's code. PARTIALLY VERIFIED 2026-09-08: a unit test on useModelTraining (hooks/model/__tests__/use-model-training.test.tsx) proves the CLIENT sends each candidate's own value in the ALGORITHM_SWEEP request body — a non-default ridge alpha on the second of three algorithms. The backend write path (runDtoFor -> launchDraftRun -> ModelTrainingRun.create) was read, not re-run: it is unchanged code, already covered by MODEL-FLOW-012-T01's own audit (finding 2). A live end-to-end run against a real database was not executed this pass.

Assert use-model-draft-sync's PATCH still succeeds with the nested state present — the T01(e) failure, which would otherwise 400 into a silent catch and leave the user configuring against a draft that stopped accepting updates. VERIFIED 2026-09-08 by construction: mpPerAlgorithmHyperparamsAtom never enters use-model-draft-sync's PATCH body (that hook reads only the unchanged flat mpHyperparamsAtom) — confirmed by inspection, no code path added there.

Run a real SWEEP_THEN_TUNE with user-authored phase-1 values and assert phase 2's appended candidates exclude the value phase 1 already tried — openDecision 2, verified rather than reasoned. NOT YET RUN 2026-09-08: requires a live SWEEP_THEN_TUNE integration test (real training containers) to observe tuningCandidatesFor's exclusion firing for the first time against a user-authored value — reasoned about from source (tuning-grid.ts's sameHyperparams, strict === over sorted keys) but not empirically exercised this pass.

Tick an algorithm, then change the dataset so it becomes ineligible, and assert the tab disappears with the reason visible rather than remaining and failing at fit time. VERIFIED 2026-09-08: algorithm-selector.test.tsx asserts BOTH halves — the tab disappearing is necessary but not sufficient, so the test asserts onChange is called dropping the newly-ineligible algorithm from the selection itself, not merely that its tab stops rendering.

global_definition_of_done: Serving, promotion and retraining are OUT of this ledger's scope and live in MODEL-SERVE; what this ledger owes them is a saved Model that records its artifact, checksum, feature spec and framework version — nothing downstream re-derives those.
The six-step Model Creation Flow is preserved (MODEL-FLOW-010 went four to five; MODEL-FLOW-013 inserted Model Selection, five to six).
A dataset selected at Step 1 is reviewable at Step 2 before any training is configured.
Step 3 Training Configuration behavior remains unchanged.
Step 6 Save Model behavior remains unchanged.
Training runs without committing the Model to the database.
Evaluation works without a persistent Model database record.
Fine-Tuning runs as a background process.
Fine-Tuning does not commit the Model to the database.
Model configuration is preserved before final Save Model.
Model artifacts are stored and referenced correctly.
Save Model is the only persistence boundary for the final Model.
Failed Save Model operations do not leave partial Model records.
No unrelated functionality is changed or broken.
No persistent MODEL record is created before Save Model. Draft, job and log rows ARE written before it — they are what makes a container able to run and report at all.
Every metric shown in Step 3 comes from a run whose target-leakage guard actually executed.
